source: Written 2026-10-23/24 by Claude Sonnet from our own summaries of the NC 2017 standards, and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin.

notes.NC17.M1.N-RN.2: All integer-exponent rules (product, quotient, power of a power, power of a product or quotient, zero, negative) with variable and numeric bases. Choice algebra answers were checked numerically in the build script. Distractors are common slips (adding for multiplying, ignoring a coefficient, sign of the exponent). Scientific-notation context kept to one question.
notes.NC17.M1.A-SSE.1: Interpreting parts of expressions (A-SSE.1): 30 questions, 10 per difficulty, linear, exponential and quadratic expressions with contexts. Everything is asked in words; meaning-in-context questions are choice, value-of-a-part and counting questions are numeric.
notes.NC17.M1.A-SSE.3: Answers asking for two zeros are posed as the smaller/larger/positive zero, their sum or product, or as choice questions. Quadratic equations with a not 1 are included (6x^2+x-12, 2x^2+3x-20, 3x^2+5x-2).
notes.NC17.M1.A-APR.1: Multiplication is of linear expressions only (and a monomial times a linear one), as the summary says; quadratics are only added and subtracted. Division of polynomials appears once, only as the thing that is not closed.
notes.NC17.M1.A-APR.3: Skills (rough counts): solve a factored equation 3, zeros of a factored function 3, zeros as x-intercepts 5, factor a trinomial to find zeros 3, write factors or an equation from solutions 5, solve by factoring 5, connect a factor, a zero and a solution 5, quadratic equations in context 3 (plus the rocket and the vertex questions). Leading coefficient is 1 except one that factors out a 2 first. Graphs are described by their features in words.
notes.NC17.M1.A-CED.1: Exponential equations that need logarithms are not solved; numeric solve questions use powers that come out exactly (doubling, tripling, halving), and growth or decay rates with awkward answers are choice questions that only ask for the equation or inequality. Quadratic situations are solved by factoring or by square roots only.
notes.NC17.M1.A-CED.2: Graphing is tested through what words can carry: intercepts, direction and shape of a graph read from its equation, and tables of values; no picture is referred to. The quadratic questions use the vertex-free features only (intercepts), since vertex form is not named in the summary.
notes.NC17.M1.A-CED.3: Skills (rough counts): equations from a story 3, inequalities from a story 4, equation plus inequality 2, phrase into an inequality 3, checking values against constraints 3, interpreting a model or solution 3, finding a limit from the constraints 3, solving counts-and-prices 4, two related quantities 3, rates or break-even 2. Solving is kept small and exact; writing the system is the standard's focus. Graphing is not asked because no picture is available.
notes.NC17.M1.A-CED.4: Formulas are linear in the chosen variable (rearranging uses the steps of solving an equation); numeric questions ask for a value after rearranging. No answer is irrational.
notes.NC17.M1.A-REI.1: Text-only: steps are written out rather than shown. 17 choice, 13 numeric because naming a justification is naturally a choice. Skills: name the step done (6), justify with a property (5), square roots and Zero Product Property (5), completing the square (4), why a method works (3), find the error (3), carry out justified steps (3), check by substitution (1).
notes.NC17.M1.A-REI.3: All solutions are single numbers or simple inequality statements; no graphing of solution sets on number lines (not testable in text). Skills: two-step equations (5), variables on both sides (5), distributive property and like terms (5), fractions and decimals (5), number of solutions (2), linear inequalities incl. reversing the sign (6), one compound inequality, one literal equation (letters as coefficients).
notes.NC17.M1.A-REI.4: Only taking square roots and factoring are used, as the summary says: no completing the square and no quadratic formula. A few equations have irrational solutions (written with a radical), asked only as choice questions.
notes.NC17.M1.A-REI.5: Text-only. 17 choice, 13 numeric: explaining WHY is naturally a choice, so the numeric ones check the mechanics (sums, multiples, multipliers, recovering an equation). Skills: add two equations (3), a solution still fits the new equation (4), adding equals to equals (2), multiply an equation by a number (4), why the solutions stay the same (4), recover the old equation (2), add a multiple of one equation to the other (6), which replacements are allowed (5).
notes.NC17.M1.A-REI.6: Text-only: tables are written out in the stem, and graphs are given by their equations, two points on each line, or a crossing point. 15 choice, 15 numeric. Skills: elimination (6), substitution (5), word problems (5), tables (4), graph (3), no or infinitely many solutions (3), interpret in context (3), check a point (1).
notes.NC17.M1.A-REI.10: Graphs are never shown: points are tested by substituting, and lines are described by points or equations. The standard is conceptual, so many questions are about what it means to lie on the graph.
notes.NC17.M1.A-REI.11: Graphs are never shown: crossing points are given as coordinates, graphs are described by their equations or by features, and approximation "with technology or tables" is asked through written tables of values (exact crossings and "between two x-values" brackets). Skills: why the x-coordinate solves f(x) = g(x) (3), the common output (3), writing the equation (2), number of solutions (3), linear (6), tables (5), exponential (4), quadratic (4).
notes.NC17.M1.A-REI.12: Graphs are described in words (solid or dashed, which side is shaded, intercepts, corners) and regions are tested with points; no figure is referred to. Numeric answers are intercepts, counts of points, a corner coordinate or a greatest or least whole number.
notes.NC17.M1.F-IF.1: Skills: recognize a function from ordered pairs (3), evaluate f(x) and the meaning of the notation (7), link f(x) to the graph of y = f(x) (4), domain and range (6), find an input for a given output (2), function from an equation, graph or situation (5), swapped relation (1), missing value (1). Graph features are described in words or points, since no picture can be shown.
notes.NC17.M1.F-IF.4: Graphs are described by their features in words or by short tables; no pictures. Quadratic features need the vertex, which is standard in NC Math 1.
notes.NC17.M1.F-IF.5: Domain and range in context, written as text only: graphs are given as described segments, arcs or tables of values.
notes.NC17.M1.F-IF.6: Tables and graphs are given as pairs of values or points, since no picture can be shown. Formulas are linear, quadratic and exponential only (NC Math 1). Skills: from a table or two values, from points on a graph, from a formula, interpreting in context, comparing, finding a missing value, and the linear case.
notes.NC17.M1.F-IF.8: Quadratics are given in standard, factored or vertex form as text; exponential forms like (1.02)^{12t} are interpreted from the written function.
notes.NC17.M1.F-IF.9: Graphs are never shown: functions are given as equations, tables written as lists, two points, or verbal descriptions. Quadratic tables are symmetric so the vertex is readable.
notes.NC17.M1.F-BF.2: Arithmetic and geometric sequences only; explicit and recursive forms use a_1 and a_{n-1} notation. Percent decay and doubling stories kept to ratio form.
notes.NC17.M1.F-LE.3: Graphs are described by where they meet and which is above (text only); tables are written as lists of values. Growth is compared with linear and quadratic functions only, with whole-number inputs. Quadratic tables appear as comparisons, not as a topic of their own.
notes.NC17.M1.F-LE.5: Thirty questions on the meaning of the parameters of a linear function (slope as rate, y-intercept as starting value) and of an exponential function (initial value a, base b as growth or decay factor and percent change), plus choosing a model type, writing a model from its parameters and the effect of changing a parameter. Graphs are not used; tables and two-point descriptions stand in.
notes.NC17.M1.G-GPE.4: Thirty questions: distance, perimeter, area of rectangles and triangles (including non-axis-aligned shapes and triangles needing the enclosing-rectangle method), and classifying triangles and quadrilaterals by slopes and lengths. Coordinates are given in text; no figures. Irrational lengths only appear inside choice questions or as intermediate steps.
notes.NC17.M1.G-GPE.5: Equations of lines are choice questions; the numeric versions ask for a y-intercept, a crossing point or an unknown constant. Coordinates and slopes are stated in text; no graphs are used.
notes.NC17.M1.S-ID.1: The standard says to use technology to draw histograms and box plots; these questions are answered by hand from written-out data, bars and five-number summaries. Quartile questions state the method or use data where it is stated.
notes.NC17.M1.S-ID.2: Text-only: data are given as short lists or as five-number summaries, and spread is compared by range, IQR (Q1 and Q3 as medians of the lower and upper halves, stated in each question that needs it) and a given standard deviation. Standard deviation is never computed by hand; it is interpreted from given values or compared on small sets.
notes.NC17.M1.S-ID.3: All 30 questions are on outliers and their effect on center, spread and shape; quartiles are defined by the median of each half where IQR is used. Graphs are described in words only.
notes.NC17.M1.S-ID.6: Fitting a least squares line or exponential model needs technology, so every fitted equation is given and the questions ask for predictions, interpretation, residuals and judgments of fit. Plotting is tested only through which variable goes on which axis and the direction of association, since a plot cannot be drawn in text.
notes.NC17.M1.S-ID.7: All models are given as equations or as two points on the line (no scatter plot is shown), so residuals and fitting are left to S-ID.6 and S-ID.8; the question asks only about reading and using a stated model. Interpolation and extrapolation are judged against a stated range of the data.
notes.NC17.M1.S-ID.8: Technology (computing r or residual plots) is replaced by hand-sized data with exact r, sums given, or residual patterns described in words.
notes.NC17.M1.S-ID.9: Many questions are choice or counting questions, since the standard is conceptual (a numeric answer fits only counting statements). Studies and data are described in words, no pictures.

questions.skill: Product of powers
questions.stem: Simplify $x^3 \cdot x^4$. The result can be written as $x^n$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: When you multiply powers with the same base, you add the exponents: $3 + 4 = 7$.

solve.work: Product of powers: x^3 * x^4 = x^(3+4) = x^7, so n = 7.

questions.skill: Quotient of powers
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\frac{a^9}{a^4}$, for $a \ne 0$?
questions.solution: When you divide powers with the same base, you subtract the exponents: $9 - 4 = 5$, so the result is $a^5$.

solve.work: Quotient of powers: a^9/a^4 = a^(9-4) = a^5.

questions.skill: Power of a power
questions.stem: Write $(m^2)^5$ as a single power of $m$, written $m^n$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: When you raise a power to a power, you multiply the exponents: $2 \cdot 5 = 10$.

solve.work: Power of a power: (m^2)^5 = m^(2*5) = m^10, n = 10.

questions.skill: Zero exponent
questions.stem: What is the value of $9^0$?
questions.solution: Any nonzero number raised to the power 0 equals 1.

solve.work: Any nonzero number to the zero power is 1: 9^0 = 1.

questions.skill: Negative exponents
questions.stem: Which number is equal to $5^{-2}$?
questions.solution: A negative exponent means a reciprocal: $5^{-2} = \frac{1}{5^2} = \frac{1}{25}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
questions.stem: Evaluate $2^3 \cdot 2^2$.
questions.solution: Add the exponents: $2^3 \cdot 2^2 = 2^5 = 32$. (Or: $8 \cdot 4 = 32$.)

questions.skill: Power of a product or quotient
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $(3x)^2$?
questions.solution: The exponent applies to both factors: $(3x)^2 = 3^2 \cdot x^2 = 9x^2$.

questions.skill: Negative exponents
questions.stem: The expression $\frac{1}{x^4}$ can be written as $x^n$ for $x \ne 0$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: A negative exponent means a reciprocal: $x^{-4} = \frac{1}{x^4}$, so $n = -4$.

questions.skill: Zero exponent
questions.stem: Which statement is true for every nonzero number $a$?
questions.solution: Any nonzero number to the power 0 is 1.

solve.work: a^0 = 1 for every nonzero a (a^n/a^n = a^0 = 1).

questions.skill: Product of powers
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $y \cdot y^5$?
questions.solution: The first factor is $y^1$. Add the exponents: $1 + 5 = 6$, so the result is $y^6$.

questions.skill: Zero exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $3^0 + 4^0$.
questions.solution: Any nonzero number to the power 0 is 1, so $3^0 + 4^0 = 1 + 1 = 2$.

questions.skill: Spot and explain a mistake
questions.stem: Nina says $5^0 = 0$. Which statement shows her mistake?
choices: $5^0 = 5$, because the exponent 0 leaves the base unchanged
$5^0 = 1$, because any nonzero number to the power 0 equals 1
$5^0 = -5$, because the exponent 0 changes the sign of the base
$5^0 = \frac{1}{5}$, because the exponent 0 flips the base upside down
questions.answer: $5^0 = 1$, because any nonzero number to the power 0 equals 1
questions.solution: Any nonzero number to the power 0 is 1. For example, $\frac{5^2}{5^2} = 5^{2-2} = 5^0$, and a number divided by itself is 1.

solve.answer: $5^0 = 1$, because any nonzero number to the power 0 equals 1
solve.work: Any nonzero base to the 0 power is 1.

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
questions.stem: Write $\left(3^2\right)^2$ as a single whole number.

questions.skill: Power of a product or quotient
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)^2$?
questions.solution: The exponent applies to both the top and the bottom: $\frac{x^2}{3^2} = \frac{x^2}{9}$.

questions.skill: Find a missing exponent
questions.stem: For $a \ne 0$, $a^{?} \cdot a^2 = a^9$. What number is the ?
questions.solution: Exponents add when multiplying, so ? $+ 2 = 9$ and ? $= 7$.

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $6^3 \cdot 6^{-3}$?
questions.solution: Add the exponents: $6^{3 + (-3)} = 6^0 = 1$.

questions.skill: Negative exponents
questions.stem: Write $10^{-2}$ as a decimal.

questions.skill: Negative exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $x^{-5}$, for $x \ne 0$?
questions.solution: A negative exponent means the reciprocal: $x^{-5} = \frac{1}{x^5}$.

questions.skill: Negative exponents
questions.stem: Which number is equal to $10^{-3}$?
questions.solution: A negative exponent means the reciprocal: $10^{-3} = \frac{1}{10^3} = \frac{1}{1000}$.

questions.skill: Negative exponents
questions.stem: Zane evaluates $3^{-2}$ by writing it as a fraction with 1 on the top. What fraction does he get?

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
questions.stem: Evaluate $\frac{2^8}{2^5}$.
questions.solution: Subtract the exponents: $2^{8-5} = 2^3 = 8$.

questions.skill: Power of a product or quotient
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $(ab)^3$?
questions.solution: The exponent applies to each factor: $(ab)^3 = a^3b^3$.

questions.skill: Product of powers
questions.stem: Simplify $3x^2 \cdot x^3$. The result is $3x^n$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: The coefficient 3 stays. Add the exponents of $x$: $x^2 \cdot x^3 = x^5$. So $n = 5$.

questions.skill: Product of powers
questions.stem: Simplify $k^2 \cdot k^6 \cdot k$. The result is $k^n$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: When powers of the same base are multiplied, the exponents are added. $k^2 \cdot k^6 \cdot k^1 = k^{2+6+1} = k^9$.

questions.skill: Power of a power
questions.stem: Which expression equals $\left(w^{5}\right)^{2}$?
questions.solution: Multiply the exponents: $5 \cdot 2 = 10$, so $\left(w^5\right)^2 = w^{10}$.

questions.skill: Quotient of powers
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $\frac{m^5}{m^5}$, for $m \ne 0$?
questions.solution: A number divided by itself is 1. By the rule, $m^{5-5} = m^0 = 1$.

questions.skill: Power of a power
questions.stem: For $t \ne 0$, $(t^7)^2 = t^{?}$. What number is the ?
questions.solution: A power of a power multiplies the exponents: $(t^7)^2 = t^{7 \cdot 2} = t^{14}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
questions.stem: Evaluate $7^0 \cdot 5^2$.
questions.solution: $7^0 = 1$ and $5^2 = 25$, so the product is 25.

questions.skill: Quotient of powers
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\frac{x^{10}}{x^3}$, for $x \ne 0$?
questions.solution: When powers of the same base are divided, the exponents are subtracted: $x^{10-3} = x^7$.

questions.skill: Zero exponent
questions.stem: Four expressions are shown. Only one of them equals 1 for every nonzero $x$. Which one?
questions.solution: Anything nonzero to the power 0 is 1, and $8x$ is nonzero, so $(8x)^0 = 1$. In $8 \cdot x^0$ only the $x$ has the exponent, so it equals $8 \cdot 1 = 8$. Also $(8x)^1 = 8x$ and $8 + x^0 = 9$.

solve.work: 8 + x^0 = 9; (8x)^1 = 8x; (8x)^0 = 1 for 8x nonzero, i.e. every nonzero x; 8*x^0 = 8. Only (8x)^0.

questions.skill: Power of a product or quotient
questions.stem: Raise the fraction $\frac{2}{3}$ to the power 2. What fraction do you get?
questions.solution: The exponent applies to the top and the bottom: $\frac{2^2}{3^2} = \frac{4}{9}$.

questions.skill: Negative exponents
questions.stem: For $x \ne 0$, $\frac{1}{x^{-2}} = x^n$. What is $n$?

questions.skill: Spot and explain a mistake
questions.stem: Maya simplified $x^2 \cdot x^3$ and wrote $x^6$. What should she have done?
choices: Multiply the exponents, which gives $x^6$, so she was right
Add the exponents and the bases, which gives $2x^5$
questions.solution: When multiplying powers of the same base, add the exponents: $x^{2+3} = x^5$. Multiplying the exponents is the rule for a power of a power.

solve.work: x^2 * x^3 = x^(2+3) = x^5: add exponents.

questions.skill: Quotient of powers
questions.stem: For $x \ne 0$, the expression $\frac{x^3}{x^8}$ equals $x^n$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: Subtract the exponents: $3 - 8 = -5$, so $\frac{x^3}{x^8} = x^{-5}$.

questions.skill: Power of a product or quotient
questions.stem: Simplify $(2x^3)^4$.
questions.solution: Raise each factor to the 4th power: $2^4 = 16$ and $(x^3)^4 = x^{12}$. The result is $16x^{12}$.

questions.skill: Negative exponents
questions.stem: Evaluate $\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{-3}$.
questions.solution: A negative exponent flips the fraction: $\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{-3} = 2^3 = 8$.

questions.skill: Negative exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\frac{3}{x^{-2}}$, for $x \ne 0$?

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
questions.stem: Evaluate $\frac{3^5}{3^7}$.
questions.solution: Subtract the exponents: $3^{5-7} = 3^{-2} = \frac{1}{9}$.

questions.skill: Product of powers
questions.stem: Simplify $x^{-3} \cdot x^5$, for $x \ne 0$.
questions.solution: Add the exponents: $-3 + 5 = 2$, so the result is $x^2$.

questions.skill: Find a missing exponent
questions.stem: For $a \ne 0$, $a^? \cdot a^{-3} = a^5$. What number is the ?
questions.solution: The exponents add up to 5, so $? + (-3) = 5$, which gives $? = 8$.

questions.skill: Combine several properties
questions.stem: For $x \ne 0$, the expression $\frac{(x^3)^4}{x^5}$ equals $x^n$. What is $n$?

questions.skill: Zero exponent
questions.stem: For $x \ne 0$, which expression is NOT equal to 1?
questions.solution: The exponent 0 in $5x^0$ applies only to $x$, so $5x^0 = 5 \cdot 1 = 5$. The other three are a nonzero base to the power 0, which is 1.

questions.skill: Spot and explain a mistake
questions.stem: A student simplified $(x^3)^2$ and got $x^5$. Which explanation is correct?
choices: The exponents should be subtracted, so the result is $x$.
The answer $x^5$ is correct because the exponents are added.
The exponent 3 should be squared, so the result is $x^9$.
The exponents should be multiplied, so the result is $x^6$.
questions.answer: The exponents should be multiplied, so the result is $x^6$.
questions.solution: A power of a power multiplies the exponents: $3 \cdot 2 = 6$, so $(x^3)^2 = x^6$. Adding is the rule for a product of powers, not a power of a power.

solve.answer: The exponents should be multiplied, so the result is $x^6$.
solve.work: (x^3)^2 = x^3 * x^3 = x^6: exponents multiply. The student added. Option 3 is the correct explanation; option 2 gives x^9 (wrong), option 4 gives x (wrong).

questions.skill: Combine product, quotient and power rules
questions.stem: For $x \ne 0$, $\frac{x^{7} \cdot x^{-2}}{x^{4}} = x^n$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: Add the exponents on top: $7 + (-2) = 5$. Then subtract the bottom: $5 - 4 = 1$. So $n = 1$.

questions.skill: Power of a product or quotient
questions.stem: Simplify $\left(\frac{x^2}{y^3}\right)^{4}$, for $y \ne 0$.
questions.solution: Multiply each exponent by 4: $x^{2 \cdot 4} = x^8$ and $y^{3 \cdot 4} = y^{12}$.

questions.skill: Negative exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $(2x)^{-3}$, for $x \ne 0$?
questions.solution: $(2x)^{-3} = \frac{1}{(2x)^3} = \frac{1}{2^3x^3} = \frac{1}{8x^3}$. The exponent applies to the 2 as well as the $x$.

questions.skill: Combine product, quotient and power rules
questions.stem: For $x \ne 0$, $\left(x^{3}\right)^{-2} \cdot x^{8} = x^n$. What is $n$?

questions.skill: Power of a product or quotient
questions.stem: Simplify $(3a^2b)^3$.
questions.solution: Apply the exponent 3 to every factor: $3^3 \cdot \left(a^2\right)^3 \cdot b^3 = 27a^6b^3$.

questions.skill: Spot and explain a mistake
questions.stem: Leah simplified $\frac{x^{-3}}{x^{2}}$ and wrote $x^{-1}$, which is not correct. What is the correct simplification, for $x \ne 0$?
questions.solution: Subtract the exponents: $-3 - 2 = -5$. Leah added them instead, so the correct answer is $x^{-5}$.

questions.skill: Rewrite with only positive exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\frac{2x^{-3}}{y^{-1}}$, for $x \ne 0$ and $y \ne 0$?
questions.solution: $x^{-3} = \frac{1}{x^3}$ moves $x$ to the bottom. $\frac{1}{y^{-1}} = y$ moves $y$ to the top. So the result is $\frac{2y}{x^3}$.

questions.skill: Negative exponents
questions.stem: Evaluate $\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^{-2}$.
questions.solution: A negative exponent flips the fraction: $\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^{-2} = \left(\frac{4}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{16}{9}$.

questions.skill: Combine product, quotient and power rules
questions.stem: For $x \ne 0$, what is the value of $\frac{\left(5x^{2}\right)^{2}}{x^{4}}$?

questions.skill: Find a missing exponent
questions.stem: For $x \ne 0$, $\frac{x^{?}}{x^{5}} = x^{-3}$. What number is the ?
questions.solution: Subtract the exponents: ? $- 5 = -3$, so ? $= 2$.

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
questions.stem: Write $10^{-2} \cdot 10^{-1}$ as a decimal.

questions.skill: Rewrite with only positive exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\frac{1}{3x^{-2}}$, for $x \ne 0$?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{x^{-2}} = x^2$, and the 3 stays on the bottom. So the result is $\frac{x^2}{3}$.

questions.skill: Quotient of powers
questions.stem: Simplify $\frac{x^{-4}}{x^{-7}}$, for $x \ne 0$.
questions.solution: Subtract the exponents: $-4 - (-7) = -4 + 7 = 3$, so the result is $x^3$.

questions.skill: Product of powers
questions.stem: Simplify $4x^{-2} \cdot 3x^{5}$, for $x \ne 0$.
questions.solution: Multiply the coefficients: $4 \cdot 3 = 12$. Add the exponents: $-2 + 5 = 3$. The result is $12x^3$.

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
questions.stem: Evaluate $\left(5^{-1}\right)^{-2}$.
questions.solution: Multiply the exponents: $(-1)(-2) = 2$, so $5^2 = 25$.

questions.skill: Negative exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is NOT equal to $x^{-2}$, for $x \ne 0$?
questions.solution: $\frac{x^{-1}}{x^{-3}} = x^{-1-(-3)} = x^2$, which is not $x^{-2}$. The other three all equal $\frac{1}{x^2}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
Combine product, quotient and power rules
questions.stem: Simplify $\frac{\left(x^{2}\right)^{3}}{x^{-4}}$, for $x \ne 0$.

questions.skill: Rewrite with only positive exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $a^{3} \cdot b^{-2} \cdot a^{-1}$ when written with only positive exponents, for $a \ne 0$ and $b \ne 0$?
questions.solution: Add the exponents of $a$: $3 + (-1) = 2$. Then $b^{-2} = \frac{1}{b^2}$. So the result is $\frac{a^2}{b^2}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
questions.stem: Evaluate $2^{-3} \cdot 2^{5}$.
questions.solution: Add the exponents: $2^{-3+5} = 2^2 = 4$.

questions.skill: Decide which exponent statement is true
questions.stem: Which equation is true for every nonzero $x$?
questions.solution: $\left(x^3\right)^2 = x^{6}$ is true. The others are false: $x^3 \cdot x^2 = x^5$, $\frac{x^6}{x^2} = x^4$ and $(2x)^3 = 8x^3$.

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
questions.solution: Add the exponents on top: $-2 + 4 = 2$. Since $3^0 = 1$, the result is $3^2 = 9$.

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
questions.solution: Subtract the exponents: $-3 - (-6) = 3$, so $2^3 = 8$.

questions.skill: Combine several properties
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\frac{12x^5y^{-2}}{4x^{-1}y^3}$ when written with only positive exponents?
questions.solution: Divide the numbers: $12 \div 4 = 3$. For $x$: $5 - (-1) = 6$. For $y$: $-2 - 3 = -5$. So the result is $3x^6y^{-5} = \frac{3x^6}{y^5}$.

questions.skill: Combine several properties
Find a missing exponent
questions.stem: For what value of $n$ is $(x^n)^3 \cdot x^{-4} = x^5$ true for every $x \ne 0$?

questions.skill: Negative exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\left(\frac{2a}{b^2}\right)^{-3}$, for $a \ne 0$ and $b \ne 0$?
questions.solution: A negative exponent flips the fraction: $\left(\frac{b^2}{2a}\right)^3$. Cube the top and the bottom: $\frac{b^6}{8a^3}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
questions.stem: Find the value of the product $\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{-2} \cdot \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{-1}$ as a fraction.
questions.solution: $\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{-2} = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}$ and $\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{-1} = \frac{2}{3}$. Then $\frac{9}{4} \cdot \frac{2}{3} = \frac{18}{12} = \frac{3}{2}$.

questions.skill: Combine several properties
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $(3x^{-2}y)^2 \cdot x^3y^{-1}$ when written with only positive exponents, for $x \ne 0$ and $y \ne 0$?

questions.skill: Spot and explain a mistake
questions.stem: Which statement is true for every nonzero $x$?

solve.work: (x^-2)^-3 = x^6: true. x^-2*x^-3 = x^-5 not x^6. (2x)^-2 = 1/(4x^2) not 2/x^2. x^-2/x^-3 = x^1 not x^-5. Only the first is true.

questions.skill: Combine several properties
Spot and explain a mistake
questions.stem: Which expression is NOT equal to $\frac{1}{8}$?

questions.skill: Power of a product or quotient
questions.stem: For nonzero $a$ and $b$, $(a^2b^{-3})^{-2} = a^p b^q$. What is $p \cdot q$?
questions.solution: Multiply each exponent by $-2$: $a^{2 \cdot (-2)} b^{-3 \cdot (-2)} = a^{-4} b^{6}$. So $p = -4$, $q = 6$, and $p \cdot q = -24$.

questions.skill: Combine product, quotient and power rules
questions.stem: For nonzero $a$ and $b$, $\left(\frac{a^{-2}b^{3}}{a^{4}b}\right)^{-1} = a^{p}b^{q}$. What is $p + q$?
questions.solution: Inside: $a^{-2-4}b^{3-1} = a^{-6}b^{2}$. Taking the power $-1$ gives $a^{6}b^{-2}$. So $p = 6$, $q = -2$ and $p + q = 4$.

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
Spot and explain a mistake
questions.stem: Dev simplified $\frac{\left(2x^{-3}\right)^{2}}{x^{-1}}$ and wrote $\frac{4}{x^{7}}$, which is not correct. What is the correct simplification, for $x \ne 0$?
questions.solution: The top is $4x^{-6}$. Dividing by $x^{-1}$ subtracts the exponent: $-6 - (-1) = -5$. So the result is $4x^{-5} = \frac{4}{x^5}$. Dev added $-6$ and $-1$ instead.

questions.skill: Find a missing exponent
questions.stem: For $x \ne 0$, $\frac{x^{n} \cdot x^{-3}}{x^{4}} = x^{-1}$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: The exponent on the left is $n + (-3) - 4 = n - 7$. Setting $n - 7 = -1$ gives $n = 6$.

questions.skill: Decide which exponent statement is true
questions.stem: Which equation is true for all nonzero $x$ and $y$?
questions.solution: $x^{-3}$ moves to the bottom and $y^{-2}$ moves to the top, giving $\frac{y^2}{x^3}$. The others are false: $\left(x^{-2}\right)^3 = x^{-6}$, $\frac{x^4}{x^{-2}} = x^6$ and $(3x)^{-1} = \frac{1}{3x}$.

questions.skill: Combine product, quotient and power rules
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to 1 for every nonzero $x$?
questions.solution: $\frac{x^5 \cdot x^{-2}}{x^3} = x^{5-2-3} = x^0 = 1$. The others simplify to $x$, $x^4$ and $x^4$.

questions.skill: Exponents in a context
questions.stem: A square has side length $3x^{-2}$ units, for $x \ne 0$. Which expression gives its area, in square units, with only positive exponents?
questions.solution: Area is side squared: $\left(3x^{-2}\right)^2 = 9x^{-4} = \frac{9}{x^4}$.

questions.skill: Combine product, quotient and power rules
questions.stem: For $a \ne 0$, $\frac{\left(a^{3}\right)^{-2}}{a^{-8}} = a^n$. What is $n$?

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
questions.stem: Evaluate $\left(5^{-2} \cdot 5^{3}\right)^{-1}$.

questions.skill: Negative exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to the sum $x^{-2} + x^{-2}$, for $x \ne 0$? Remember that this is a sum, not a product.
questions.solution: Adding two equal terms doubles one of them: $x^{-2} + x^{-2} = 2x^{-2} = \frac{2}{x^2}$. Exponents are added only when powers are multiplied, not when they are added.

questions.skill: Use a given power to find another
questions.stem: If $m^{5} = 2$, what is the value of $m^{-10}$?

questions.skill: Exponents in a context
questions.stem: A square sticker has sides of length $2 \times 10^{-3}$ meters. Which is its area in square meters?
questions.solution: Area is side squared: $\left(2 \times 10^{-3}\right)^2 = 2^2 \times 10^{-6} = 4 \times 10^{-6}$.

questions.skill: Rewrite with only positive exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\frac{\left(2x^{-2}y^{3}\right)^{3}}{4x^{-1}y^{2}}$ when written with only positive exponents?

questions.skill: Find a missing exponent
questions.stem: What value of $n$ makes $2^{n} \cdot 2^{-5} = \frac{1}{8}$ true?

questions.skill: Use a given power to find another
questions.stem: If $a^{-1} = 5$, what is the value of $a^{-3}$?

questions.skill: Combine product, quotient and power rules
questions.stem: For $x \ne 0$, $\frac{\left(2x^{3}\right)^{-2}}{(4x)^{-1}} = \frac{k}{x^{m}}$. What is $k + m$?
questions.solution: The top is $2^{-2}x^{-6} = \frac{1}{4x^6}$ and the bottom is $\frac{1}{4x}$. Dividing gives $\frac{1}{4x^6} \cdot 4x = \frac{x}{x^6} = \frac{1}{x^5}$. So $k = 1$, $m = 5$ and $k + m = 6$.

questions.skill: Combine product, quotient and power rules
questions.stem: For $x \ne 0$, $\left(\frac{2x^{-3}}{x^{-5}}\right)^{3} = kx^{n}$. What is $k + n$?

questions.skill: Rewrite with only positive exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\frac{\left(a^{2}b^{-1}\right)^{-3}}{a^{-2}b^{4}}$ when written with only positive exponents?

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
questions.stem: What is the sum of $\frac{1}{2^{-3}}$ and $\frac{1}{3^{-2}}$?

questions.skill: Rewrite with only positive exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\left(\frac{x^{-2}y}{z^{3}}\right)^{-2}$ when written with only positive exponents?
questions.solution: Multiply each exponent by $-2$: $x^{4}y^{-2}z^{6}$. Moving $y^{-2}$ to the bottom gives $\frac{x^4z^6}{y^2}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate expressions with integer exponents
questions.stem: Ivy finds the difference between $\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{-2}$ and $3^{-2}$, taking the first minus the second. What is the difference, as a fraction?

questions.skill: Rewrite with only positive exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\frac{9x^{-4}}{3^{-1}x^{2}}$ when written with only positive exponents, for $x \ne 0$?

questions.skill: Decide which exponent statement is true
questions.stem: Which pair of expressions is equivalent for every nonzero $x$?
questions.solution: $\left(x^{-3}\right)^2 = x^{-6} = \frac{1}{x^6}$. In the other pairs the first expression is $x^{-1}$, $x^{-5}$ or $x^{-6}$, so they do not match the second.

questions.skill: Count the terms of an expression
questions.stem: How many terms does the expression $4x^2 - 7x + 9$ have?
questions.solution: The terms are the parts that are added: $4x^2$, $-7x$ and $9$. There are 3 terms.

questions.skill: Identify coefficients, factors and constants
questions.stem: What is the coefficient of $x$ in the expression $-6x + 11$?
questions.solution: The coefficient is the number multiplying $x$, including its sign. In $-6x + 11$ it is $-6$.

questions.skill: Interpret rates and starting values in a linear expression
questions.stem: A gym charges a joining fee plus a fee for each month. The cost, in dollars, after $m$ months is $20 + 15m$. By how many dollars does the cost go up with each extra month?
questions.solution: The term $15m$ adds 15 dollars for every month. The 20 is the joining fee, paid once. So each extra month adds 15 dollars.

questions.skill: Interpret rates and starting values in a linear expression
questions.stem: A plant's height, in centimeters, after $w$ weeks is $12 + 3w$. What was its height, in centimeters, at the start, when $w = 0$?
questions.solution: When $w = 0$ the term $3w$ is 0, so the height is $12 + 0 = 12$ centimeters. The constant term 12 is the starting height.

questions.skill: Identify coefficients, factors and constants
questions.stem: In the product $3(x + 2)$, which of these is a factor?
questions.solution: A factor is a part that is multiplied. The expression $3(x + 2)$ is 3 times $(x + 2)$, so its factors are 3 and $x + 2$. The numbers $x$, $2$ and $3x$ are not multiplied together to make it.

solve.work: 3(x+2) has factors 3 and (x+2); only x + 2 is listed.

questions.skill: Interpret the base, exponent and starting value of an exponential expression
questions.stem: The number of bacteria after $n$ hours is $100 \cdot 3^n$. What does the exponent $n$ tell you?
choices: How many times the amount has been multiplied by 3
How many bacteria there were at the very start, before any growth
What number the amount is multiplied by each time
How many bacteria are added every hour
questions.answer: How many times the amount has been multiplied by 3
questions.solution: The exponent counts the repeated multiplications by 3, one for each hour. The starting amount is 100 and the multiplier is 3.

solve.answer: How many times the amount has been multiplied by 3
solve.work: 3^n means multiplying by 3, n times; n counts how many times the amount has been multiplied by 3.

questions.skill: Interpret the base, exponent and starting value of an exponential expression
questions.stem: A population after $t$ years is modeled by $200 \cdot 2^t$. What is the population at the start, when $t = 0$?
questions.solution: When $t = 0$, $2^0 = 1$, so the population is $200 \times 1 = 200$. The 200 is the starting amount.

questions.skill: Identify coefficients, factors and constants
questions.stem: What is the constant term in the expression $2x^2 + 5x - 8$?
questions.solution: The constant term is the part with no variable. In $2x^2 + 5x - 8$ it is $-8$.

questions.skill: Interpret the parts of a quadratic expression
questions.stem: The height of a ball, in feet, after $t$ seconds is $-16t^2 + 40t + 6$. What does the constant term 6 represent?
choices: The height of the ball after 6 seconds in the air
The speed of the ball at the moment it is thrown
The greatest height that the ball reaches
The height of the ball at the start, when $t = 0$
questions.answer: The height of the ball at the start, when $t = 0$
questions.solution: When $t = 0$, the terms with $t$ are 0, leaving a height of 6 feet. So 6 is the starting height.

solve.answer: The height of the ball at the start, when $t = 0$

questions.skill: Read an expression as a combination of simpler pieces
questions.stem: Which phrase describes the expression $2x + 5$?
choices: Two times the sum of a number and 5
The sum of 2 and a number, times 5
Two raised to the power of a number, plus 5
questions.solution: In $2x + 5$, the number $x$ is multiplied by 2, and then 5 is added.

questions.skill: Identify coefficients, factors and constants
questions.stem: In the expression $3 - 4t$, what is the coefficient of $t$?
questions.solution: The coefficient is the number multiplying $t$, including its sign: $-4$.

questions.skill: Count the terms of an expression
questions.stem: Which of these expressions has exactly two terms?
questions.solution: $3x + 4$ has the terms $3x$ and $4$. $6x$ and $8$ have one term each, and $x^2 - 5x + 2$ has three.

questions.skill: Count the terms of an expression
questions.stem: How many terms does the expression $x^2 + 6$ have?
questions.solution: Terms are separated by plus and minus signs. The terms are $x^2$ and $6$, so there are 2.

questions.skill: Interpret the base, exponent and starting value of an exponential expression
questions.stem: A rumor spreads so that $4 \cdot 5^n$ people have heard it after $n$ hours. How many people knew it at the start, when $n = 0$?
questions.solution: $5^0 = 1$, so the number is $4 \cdot 1 = 4$.

questions.skill: Interpret a part of an expression in context
questions.stem: A parking garage charges $3h + 5$ dollars for $h$ hours: 3 dollars for each hour plus a 5 dollar entry fee. For a 4-hour stay, how many dollars of the bill come from the hourly charges, the part $3h$?
questions.solution: $3h = 3 \cdot 4 = 12$ dollars.

questions.skill: Count the terms of an expression
questions.stem: How many terms does the expression $9a - 2b + 5c - 1$ have?
questions.solution: The terms are $9a$, $2b$, $5c$ and $1$ (each with its sign), so there are 4.

questions.skill: Interpret a part of an expression in context
questions.stem: A rectangle has length $l$ and width $w$, and its perimeter is $2l + 2w$. What does the term $2l$ stand for?
choices: The area inside the rectangle, in square units
The distance all the way around the rectangle
The distance along the two lengths together
The distance along the two widths together
questions.answer: The distance along the two lengths together
questions.solution: A rectangle has two sides of length $l$, so $2l$ is the distance along those two sides.

solve.answer: The distance along the two lengths together
solve.work: 2l is length + length, the two lengths together.

questions.skill: Interpret the parts of a quadratic expression
questions.stem: Which term of the expression $5x^2 - 2x + 7$ is the quadratic term?
questions.solution: The quadratic term is the one with the variable squared, which is $5x^2$.

solve.work: Quadratic term is the x^2 term: 5x^2.

questions.skill: Read an expression as a combination of simpler pieces
questions.stem: Which phrase describes the expression $3(x - 4)$?
choices: The difference of three times a number and 4
Three more than the difference of a number and 4
Three times a number, divided by 4
Three times the difference of a number and 4
questions.answer: Three times the difference of a number and 4
questions.solution: The parentheses hold $x - 4$, the difference of a number and 4. That whole quantity is multiplied by 3.

solve.answer: Three times the difference of a number and 4

questions.skill: Identify coefficients, factors and constants
questions.stem: In the expression $7x^2 + 2x - 5$, which number is the coefficient of $x^2$?
questions.solution: The coefficient of $x^2$ is the number that multiplies $x^2$, which is 7. The 2 multiplies $x$, and $-5$ is the constant term.

questions.skill: Interpret rates and starting values in a linear expression
questions.stem: A hiker is $2 + 4t$ kilometers from the trailhead after $t$ hours of hiking. How fast is the hiker walking?
questions.solution: The distance grows by 4 kilometers for each hour, so the speed is 4 kilometers per hour. (The 2 is the distance at the start.)

solve.work: Distance increases by 4 per hour (coefficient of t); 2 is the starting distance. 4 km/h.

questions.skill: Identify coefficients, factors and constants
questions.stem: The expression $2(x - 7)$ is a product of two factors. What are they?
questions.solution: $2(x - 7)$ means 2 times the quantity $x - 7$. The two factors are 2 and $x - 7$.

questions.skill: Interpret a part of an expression in context
questions.stem: Buying $n$ notebooks at 3 dollars each and 2 pens at 1 dollar each costs $3n + 2$ dollars. What does the part $3n$ represent?
questions.solution: Each notebook costs 3 dollars, so $n$ notebooks cost $3n$ dollars. The 2 is the cost of the pens.

solve.work: 3n = 3 dollars times n notebooks = cost of the notebooks.

questions.skill: Compare what two expressions say about change
questions.stem: Plan A costs $10 + 3m$ dollars for $m$ months and plan B costs $5 + 3m$ dollars. Which statement is true?
choices: Plan A adds more each month, and both start at the same cost
Plan A has the larger starting cost, and both add the same amount each month
Plan B has the larger starting cost, and both add the same amount each month
Plan B adds more each month, and both start at the same cost
questions.answer: Plan A has the larger starting cost, and both add the same amount each month
questions.solution: The starting costs are 10 for A and 5 for B, so A starts higher. Both have 3 as the amount added each month.

solve.answer: Plan A has the larger starting cost, and both add the same amount each month
solve.work: Constants 10 vs 5: A starts higher; both have 3m, same monthly.

questions.skill: Read an expression as a combination of simpler pieces
questions.stem: Which expression means "the sum of 5 and twice a number $n$"?
questions.solution: "Twice a number $n$" is $2n$. The sum of 5 and $2n$ is $5 + 2n$.

questions.skill: Compare what two expressions say about change
questions.stem: After $w$ weeks, plant X is $4 + 2w$ centimeters tall and plant Y is $4 + 3w$ centimeters tall. Which statement is true?
choices: The plants start at the same height, and X grows faster
Y starts taller, and the plants grow at the same rate
X starts taller, and Y grows faster
The plants start at the same height, and Y grows faster
questions.answer: The plants start at the same height, and Y grows faster
questions.solution: Both start at 4 centimeters. Y grows 3 centimeters a week and X grows 2, so Y grows faster.

solve.answer: The plants start at the same height, and Y grows faster
solve.work: Both start at 4 (w=0). X grows 2 cm/week, Y grows 3 cm/week, so Y faster.

questions.skill: Read an expression as a combination of simpler pieces
questions.stem: Look at the expression $6 + 4(n - 1)$. What is the value of the part $n - 1$ when $n = 5$?

questions.skill: Interpret the parts of a quadratic expression
questions.stem: A square floor has a side length of $s$ feet. What does the expression $s^2$ give?
choices: The distance around the floor, in feet
The area of the floor, in square feet
The length of one side, in feet
Twice the side length, in feet
questions.answer: The area of the floor, in square feet
questions.solution: Area is side times side, so $s^2$ is the area of the floor in square feet.

solve.answer: The area of the floor, in square feet
solve.work: s^2 = side x side = area of square floor, in square feet.

questions.skill: Interpret the base, exponent and starting value of an exponential expression
questions.stem: The number of fans of a video after $d$ days is $50 \cdot 2^d$. What does the 50 tell you?
choices: The number of fans at the start, when $d = 0$
The number of new fans that are gained each day
The number of fans after 50 days have passed
The number of days it takes for the fans to double
questions.answer: The number of fans at the start, when $d = 0$
questions.solution: When $d = 0$, $2^0 = 1$, so the number of fans is $50 \cdot 1 = 50$. The 50 is the starting number of fans.

solve.answer: The number of fans at the start, when $d = 0$
solve.work: At d = 0, 50 x 2^0 = 50: the starting number of fans.

questions.skill: Interpret the base, exponent and starting value of an exponential expression
questions.stem: A culture has $300 \cdot 2^h$ bacteria after $h$ hours. By what number is the amount multiplied each hour?
questions.solution: Each extra hour adds 1 to the exponent, which multiplies the amount by the base, 2.

questions.skill: Identify coefficients, factors and constants
questions.stem: What is the constant term of the expression $14 - 3x$?
questions.solution: The constant term is the part with no variable, which is 14.

questions.skill: Interpret rates and starting values in a linear expression
questions.stem: The height of a candle, in centimeters, after $h$ hours of burning is $20 - 2h$. What does the 2 tell you?
choices: The candle is 2 centimeters tall when it is first lit
The candle burns out completely after 2 hours
The candle gets 2 centimeters shorter each hour
The candle is still 2 centimeters tall after 1 hour
questions.answer: The candle gets 2 centimeters shorter each hour
questions.solution: Each hour $h$ goes up by 1, so the height goes down by 2 centimeters. The number 2 is the rate at which the candle burns down.

solve.answer: The candle gets 2 centimeters shorter each hour
solve.work: 20 - 2h: height drops by 2 cm for each hour. 20 is initial height.

questions.skill: Interpret rates and starting values in a linear expression
questions.stem: The amount of money in a jar after $w$ weeks is $30 + 5w$ dollars. How many dollars are added to the jar each week?
questions.solution: The amount grows by 5 dollars for each week, so 5 dollars are added each week.

questions.skill: Interpret a part of an expression in context
questions.stem: The cost, in dollars, of a taxi ride of $m$ miles is $3 + 2.5m$. What is the value of the part $2.5m$ for a ride of 4 miles?
questions.solution: For $m = 4$, $2.5m = 2.5 \times 4 = 10$. This is the part of the cost that depends on the miles driven, 10 dollars.

questions.skill: Interpret the base, exponent and starting value of an exponential expression
questions.stem: The balance of a savings account, in dollars, after $t$ years is $800(1.05)^t$. What does the number 1.05 tell you?
choices: Each year the balance goes up by 1.05 dollars
Each year the balance is 105% of the year before
Each year the balance goes up by 105 percent
The balance on the day that the account was first opened
questions.answer: Each year the balance is 105% of the year before
questions.solution: The base 1.05 is the growth factor. Multiplying by 1.05 each year keeps 100% of the old balance and adds 5% more, so the new balance is 105% of the old one.

solve.answer: Each year the balance is 105% of the year before
solve.work: Growth factor 1.05: each year balance is 105% of previous (up 5%, not 105%).

questions.skill: Interpret the base, exponent and starting value of an exponential expression
questions.stem: The value of an investment, in dollars, after $t$ years is $500(1.06)^t$. For what value of $t$ is the value exactly the starting amount, 500 dollars?
questions.solution: The factor $(1.06)^t$ equals 1 only when $t = 0$, since any number to the power 0 is 1. Then the value is 500. So $t = 0$.

questions.skill: Interpret the parts of a quadratic expression
questions.stem: A company's profit, in dollars, from selling $x$ items is $-2x^2 + 60x - 150$. What does the constant term $-150$ tell you?
choices: Each item that is sold loses the company 150 dollars
The company has to sell 150 items before it makes any profit
The most the company can lose is 150 dollars
With no items sold, the profit is $-150$ dollars, a loss
questions.answer: With no items sold, the profit is $-150$ dollars, a loss
questions.solution: When $x = 0$ (no items sold), the other terms are 0 and the profit is $-150$ dollars. That is a loss of 150 dollars, such as costs that must be paid anyway.

solve.answer: With no items sold, the profit is $-150$ dollars, a loss
solve.work: At x = 0, profit = -150: a loss of 150 with nothing sold.

questions.skill: Read an expression as a combination of simpler pieces
questions.stem: A shirt costs $p$ dollars and is discounted by 25%. Which expression has the same value as the sale price $p - 0.25p$?
questions.solution: The sale price is the whole price $p$ minus one quarter of it. Taking away 25% leaves 75%, so $p - 0.25p = 0.75p$.

questions.skill: Count the terms of an expression
questions.stem: Before anything is multiplied out, how many terms does the expression $5x(x - 2) + 7$ have as it is written?
questions.solution: The terms are the parts that are added. As written, $5x(x - 2)$ is one term, since it is a product, and 7 is the other. There are 2 terms.

questions.skill: Identify coefficients, factors and constants
questions.stem: What is the coefficient of $x^2$ in the expression $\frac{1}{2}x^2 - 3x + 4$?
questions.solution: The coefficient of $x^2$ is the number multiplying it, $\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.skill: Interpret a part of an expression in context
questions.stem: A theater sells child tickets for 7 dollars and adult tickets for 12 dollars. The money from $a$ adult tickets and $c$ child tickets is $12a + 7c$ dollars. How much money, in dollars, do 5 child tickets bring in? (This is the value of the part $7c$ when $c = 5$.)
questions.solution: The part $7c$ is the money from child tickets. With $c = 5$ it is $7 \times 5 = 35$ dollars.

questions.skill: Interpret rates and starting values in a linear expression
questions.stem: A pool holds $5000 - 200m$ liters of water after it has drained for $m$ minutes. What does the number 5000 represent?
choices: The amount of water that drains out each minute
The number of minutes that it takes to completely empty the pool
The amount of water in the pool before draining starts
The amount of water left after 200 minutes
questions.answer: The amount of water in the pool before draining starts
questions.solution: When $m = 0$, the term $200m$ is 0, so the pool holds 5000 liters. That is the starting amount. The 200 is the rate of draining.

solve.answer: The amount of water in the pool before draining starts
solve.work: At m = 0 the pool holds 5000 L: water before draining starts.

questions.skill: Read an expression as a combination of simpler pieces
questions.stem: Which phrase describes the expression $4(x + 1)^2$?
questions.solution: First $x + 1$ is added, then that sum is squared, and then the result is multiplied by 4.

questions.skill: Identify coefficients, factors and constants
questions.stem: The expression $4x(x - 3)$ is a product of three factors. What are they?
questions.solution: $4x(x - 3)$ means $4 \cdot x \cdot (x - 3)$. The factors are 4, $x$ and the quantity $x - 3$.

questions.skill: Interpret the base, exponent and starting value of an exponential expression
questions.stem: A sample has $64 \cdot (0.5)^y$ grams of a substance after $y$ years. How many grams remain after 2 years?
questions.solution: The amount is multiplied by 0.5 each year. After 2 years: $64 \cdot 0.5 \cdot 0.5 = 16$ grams.

questions.skill: Identify coefficients, factors and constants
questions.stem: In the expression $-x^2 + 6x$, what is the coefficient of $x^2$?
questions.solution: $-x^2$ means $-1 \cdot x^2$, so the coefficient is $-1$.

questions.skill: Compare what two expressions say about change
questions.stem: Rob's savings are $40 + 6w$ dollars after $w$ weeks and Tia's are $6 + 40w$ dollars. Which statement is true?
choices: Rob started with more, and he also saves more each week
Tia started with more, but Rob saves more each week
Rob started with more, but Tia saves more each week
They started with the same amount, but Tia saves more
questions.answer: Rob started with more, but Tia saves more each week
questions.solution: Rob starts with 40 and Tia with 6, so Rob started with more. Rob adds 6 a week and Tia adds 40, so Tia saves more.

solve.answer: Rob started with more, but Tia saves more each week
solve.work: Rob starts 40, saves 6/week; Tia starts 6, saves 40/week.

questions.skill: Identify coefficients, factors and constants
questions.stem: In the expression $9 - 2.5x$, what is the coefficient of $x$?
questions.solution: The coefficient is the number multiplying $x$, with its sign: $-2.5$.

questions.skill: Read an expression as a combination of simpler pieces
questions.stem: The expression $4 + 3(x - 1)$ is the sum of which two pieces?
questions.solution: The plus sign between 4 and $3(x - 1)$ separates the two terms. The second is the product of 3 and $x - 1$.

solve.work: The expression is 4 plus the product 3(x-1).

questions.skill: Interpret the parts of a quadratic expression
questions.stem: A square with side $s$ has a smaller square with side 2 cut out of one corner. The area left is $s^2 - 4$. What does the 4 represent?
choices: The side length of the square that was cut out
The area of the square that was cut out
The area of the original square
The perimeter of the square that was cut out
questions.answer: The area of the square that was cut out
questions.solution: The cut-out square has area $2 \cdot 2 = 4$, which is subtracted from the area $s^2$ of the original square.

solve.answer: The area of the square that was cut out
solve.work: 4 = 2^2, the area of the cut-out square.

She saves 75 dollars each week for 12 weeks
She started with 75 dollars and adds 12 dollars each week
questions.answer: She started with 75 dollars and adds 12 dollars each week

solve.answer: She started with 75 dollars and adds 12 dollars each week
solve.work: 75 is the start, 12 is added each week.

questions.skill: Interpret a part of an expression in context
questions.stem: A meal costs $m$ dollars and a drink costs 5 dollars. With a 20 percent tip, the total is $1.2(m + 5)$ dollars. What does $m + 5$ represent?

The total cost of the meal and drink including the tip
The cost of the meal alone, without the drink
The cost of the meal and the drink before the tip
questions.answer: The cost of the meal and the drink before the tip
questions.solution: The meal and the drink together cost $m + 5$. Multiplying by 1.2 adds the 20 percent tip to that.

solve.answer: The cost of the meal and the drink before the tip
solve.work: m+5 is the meal plus drink before the 1.2 tip factor.

questions.skill: Interpret rates and starting values in a linear expression
questions.stem: The height of an elevator above the ground, in meters, after $s$ seconds is $30 - 2s$. What does the $-2$ tell you?
choices: The elevator moves down 2 meters every second
The elevator starts 2 meters below the ground
The elevator moves up 2 meters every second
questions.answer: The elevator moves down 2 meters every second
questions.solution: Each second the height changes by $-2$ meters, so the elevator goes down 2 meters every second. The 30 is where it starts.

solve.answer: The elevator moves down 2 meters every second
solve.work: 30 - 2s: height drops by 2 m for each second, so moving down 2 m per second.

questions.skill: Interpret a part of an expression in context
questions.stem: A tutor's pay for a week is $18h + 25$ dollars, where $h$ is the number of hours worked. For $h = 10$, what is the value of the part $18h$?
questions.solution: $18h = 18 \cdot 10 = 180$ dollars.

Two times the sum of a number and 3
The square of the sum of a number and 3
The sum of a number and 9

questions.answer: X has the smaller joining fee, but Y adds less each month
questions.solution: X starts at 30 and Y at 50, so X has the smaller joining fee. X adds 20 a month and Y adds 15, so Y adds less.

solve.answer: X has the smaller joining fee, but Y adds less each month
solve.work: X: fee 30, +20/month. Y: fee 50, +15/month. X smaller fee, Y adds less.

solve.work: Factor 0.8 keeps 80%, so drops 20% a year.

questions.solution: The pay goes up by 0.5 dollars for each mile, the coefficient of $m$.

solve.work: Coefficient of m is 0.5: each extra mile adds 0.5 dollars.

solve.work: 4x^2 + 3x - 8 has three terms. Others are written as products (one term each).

questions.skill: Interpret the base, exponent and starting value of an exponential expression
questions.stem: The number of views of a video after $d$ days is $200 \cdot 1.5^d$. What does the 1.5 tell you?
choices: Each day there are 1.5 more views than there were the day before
Each day the number of views is 1.5 times the day before
The number of views grows by 150 percent each day
The video had 1.5 views on the first day it was posted
questions.answer: Each day the number of views is 1.5 times the day before
questions.solution: The base 1.5 is the number multiplied in for each day, so each day has 1.5 times as many views as the day before.

solve.answer: Each day the number of views is 1.5 times the day before
solve.work: 1.5 is the growth factor: each day views are 1.5 times the day before (a 50% increase, not 150%).

questions.skill: Count the terms of an expression
questions.stem: As it is written, how many terms does the expression $\frac{x^2}{2} - 3x + 4 - x$ have?
questions.solution: The terms are $\frac{x^2}{2}$, $3x$, $4$ and $x$, so there are 4 (even though $3x$ and $x$ could later be combined).

questions.skill: Interpret the parts of a quadratic expression
questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 40 meters. Its width is $x$ meters and its area is $x(20 - x)$ square meters. What does $20 - x$ represent?
choices: The perimeter of the rectangle, in meters
The area of the rectangle, in square meters
The width of the rectangle, in meters
The length of the rectangle, in meters
questions.answer: The length of the rectangle, in meters
questions.solution: Half the perimeter is 20, and the width and length add to 20. So the length is $20 - x$, and area is width times length.

solve.answer: The length of the rectangle, in meters
solve.work: Perimeter 40 means length + width = 20, so length = 20 - x.

questions.skill: Interpret a coefficient in context
questions.stem: A gym charges a one-time sign-up fee and a fixed fee each month. The total cost after $m$ months is $25m + 40$ dollars. Which statement describes the 25?
choices: The total cost after one month
The number of months in the plan
The fee charged for each month
questions.answer: The fee charged for each month
questions.solution: The 25 is multiplied by $m$, so it is the amount added for each month. The one-time sign-up fee is the 40.

solve.answer: The fee charged for each month
solve.work: 25 is the coefficient of m, the monthly fee; 40 is the sign-up fee.

questions.skill: Interpret the base, exponent and starting value of an exponential expression
questions.stem: The amount of a medicine in a person's body, in milligrams, $h$ hours after a dose is $80(0.5)^h$. Which statement is true?
choices: Each hour, half a milligram of the medicine is lost
Each hour, half of the amount from the hour before remains
After 1 hour, a full 80 milligrams still remain
After 2 hours, only 0.25 milligram of the medicine still remains
questions.answer: Each hour, half of the amount from the hour before remains
questions.solution: The base 0.5 is the factor each hour: the amount is multiplied by 0.5, so half remains. After 1 hour there are $80 \times 0.5 = 40$ milligrams, and after 2 hours $80 \times 0.25 = 20$ milligrams.

solve.answer: Each hour, half of the amount from the hour before remains
solve.work: Factor 0.5 per hour: each hour half of the previous amount remains. After 1 h 40 mg; after 2 h 20 mg; not 0.5 mg lost per hour.

questions.skill: Interpret a part of an expression in context
questions.stem: A square garden has side length $s$ meters. A path 2 meters wide goes all the way around it. The area of the garden and path together is $(s + 4)^2$ square meters. What does $s + 4$ represent?
choices: The area of the path around the garden
The side length of the garden by itself
The side length of the garden and path together
The width of the path around the garden
questions.answer: The side length of the garden and path together
questions.solution: The path adds 2 meters on each of the two sides, so the larger square has side $s + 2 + 2 = s + 4$. The area of that larger square is $(s + 4)^2$.

solve.answer: The side length of the garden and path together
solve.work: Path 2 m each side adds 4 to the side: s + 4 is side of garden plus path.

questions.skill: Interpret a part of an expression in context
questions.stem: A phone plan includes 50 texts. For $s$ texts, where $s$ is more than 50, the monthly cost in dollars is $15 + 0.2(s - 50)$. What does $s - 50$ represent?
choices: The number of texts above the 50 that are included
The cost of the first 50 texts that are included in the plan
The cost of each text above the 50 included
The total number of texts that were sent
questions.answer: The number of texts above the 50 that are included
questions.solution: Of the $s$ texts sent, 50 are included in the plan. What is left, $s - 50$, is the number of extra texts. Each one costs 0.2 dollars.

solve.answer: The number of texts above the 50 that are included
solve.issues: Option wording "above the 50 that are included" is slightly awkward but readable as texts beyond the included 50.
solve.work: s - 50 counts texts beyond the 50 included.

questions.skill: Identify coefficients, factors and constants
questions.stem: The expression $2(3x - 1) + 4x$ is simplified to have one $x$ term and one constant term. What is the coefficient of $x$?
questions.solution: Distribute: $2(3x - 1) = 6x - 2$. Then $6x - 2 + 4x = 10x - 2$. The coefficient of $x$ is 10.

questions.skill: Count the terms of an expression
questions.stem: As it is written, how many terms does the expression $(x + 2)(x - 3) + 5x - 4$ have?
questions.solution: The parts that are added are $(x + 2)(x - 3)$, $5x$ and $-4$. There are 3 terms. (Multiplying out gives $x^2 + 4x - 10$, which also has 3 terms.)

questions.skill: Interpret the base, exponent and starting value of an exponential expression
questions.stem: The balance of an account, in dollars, after $t$ years is $1000(1.02)^{4t}$, because interest is added every quarter (4 times a year). How many times has interest been added after 3 years?
questions.solution: The exponent $4t$ counts the number of times the balance is multiplied by 1.02. With $t = 3$ it is $4 \times 3 = 12$.

questions.skill: Compare what two expressions say about change
questions.stem: Company A charges $4 + 2m$ dollars for a taxi ride of $m$ miles. Company B charges $1 + 2.5m$ dollars. Which statement is true?
choices: Company B charges more per mile but has the smaller starting fee
Company A charges more per mile but has the smaller starting fee
Company B charges more per mile and has the larger starting fee
Company A and Company B charge the same amount per mile
questions.answer: Company B charges more per mile but has the smaller starting fee
questions.solution: The coefficient of $m$ is the charge per mile: 2 for Company A and 2.5 for B, so B charges more per mile. The constant is the starting fee: 4 for A and 1 for B, so B starts lower.

solve.answer: Company B charges more per mile but has the smaller starting fee
solve.work: Per mile: A 2, B 2.5, so B more per mile. Starting: A 4, B 1, so B smaller start fee.

questions.skill: Interpret the parts of a quadratic expression
questions.stem: A rectangle has width $w$ and length $w + 5$, so its area is $w^2 + 5w$. In this sum, what does the term $5w$ represent?
choices: The area of a square with side length $w$
The area of the part of the rectangle beyond a $w$ by $w$ square
questions.answer: The area of the part of the rectangle beyond a $w$ by $w$ square
questions.solution: The rectangle is a $w$ by $w$ square (area $w^2$) with an extra strip 5 long and $w$ wide attached. The strip has area $5w$.

solve.answer: The area of the part of the rectangle beyond a $w$ by $w$ square
solve.work: Area w(w+5) = w^2 + 5w; w^2 is the w-by-w square, 5w the 5-by-w strip beyond it.

questions.skill: Interpret a part of an expression in context
questions.stem: Drinks at a cafe cost 4 dollars each, and a meal costs 25 dollars. With 7% sales tax added, the total for $n$ drinks is $1.07(25 + 4n)$ dollars. What is the bill, in dollars, before tax, for 5 drinks? (This is the value of $25 + 4n$ when $n = 5$.)
questions.solution: The part $25 + 4n$ is the meal plus the drinks, before tax is added. For $n = 5$ it is $25 + 4 \times 5 = 45$ dollars.

questions.skill: Compare what two expressions say about change
questions.stem: Account A holds $1000(1.05)^t$ dollars after $t$ years, and account B holds $1000 + 60t$ dollars. Which statement describes how they grow?
choices: A grows by the same amount each year, and B grows by the same percent each year
A grows by the same percent each year, and B grows by the same amount each year
Both accounts grow by the same amount each year
Both accounts grow by the same percent each year
questions.answer: A grows by the same percent each year, and B grows by the same amount each year
questions.solution: In A the balance is multiplied by 1.05 each year, which is the same percent increase (5%). In B, 60 dollars is added each year, which is the same amount.

solve.answer: A grows by the same percent each year, and B grows by the same amount each year
solve.work: A: factor 1.05, same percent (5%) per year. B: +60 per year, same amount.

questions.skill: Identify coefficients, factors and constants
questions.stem: In the expression $2x^2 + 3kx - 7$, where $k$ is a fixed number, which is the coefficient of $x$?
questions.solution: The coefficient of $x$ is everything that multiplies $x$ in that term. In $3kx$, that is $3k$.

questions.skill: Identify coefficients, factors and constants
questions.stem: The expression $5 - 2(3 - 4x)$ is simplified to have one $x$ term and one constant term. What is the coefficient of $x$?
questions.solution: $5 - 2(3 - 4x) = 5 - 6 + 8x = 8x - 1$. The coefficient of $x$ is 8.

questions.skill: Interpret the base, exponent and starting value of an exponential expression
questions.stem: The value of a car, in dollars, after $t$ years is $24000(0.85)^t$. Which statement is true?
choices: Each year the car loses 85 percent of its value
Each year the car loses 15 percent of its value
Each year the car loses 0.85 dollars of its value
The car is worth 85 dollars after one year
questions.answer: Each year the car loses 15 percent of its value
questions.solution: Each year the value is 0.85, or 85 percent, of the year before, so 15 percent is lost each year.

solve.answer: Each year the car loses 15 percent of its value
solve.work: Factor 0.85 means 85% kept each year, so 15% lost each year.

questions.skill: Interpret the base, exponent and starting value of an exponential expression
questions.stem: The amount of a substance after $t$ hours is $240 \cdot (0.5)^{t/4}$ grams. How many hours does it take for the amount to be cut in half?
questions.solution: The exponent $t/4$ goes up by 1 every 4 hours, and each increase of 1 multiplies the amount by 0.5. So the amount is halved every 4 hours.

solve.work: Amount halves when t/4 = 1 (factor 0.5^1), so t = 4 hours.

questions.skill: Read an expression as a combination of simpler pieces
questions.stem: Treating $x + 3$ as a single piece, which expression equals $5(x + 3) - 2(x + 3)$?
questions.solution: Five of the piece minus two of the piece is three of the piece: $3(x + 3)$.

questions.skill: Interpret a part of an expression in context
questions.stem: A circular ring has an outer radius $R$ and an inner radius $r$. Its area is $\pi R^2 - \pi r^2$. What does the term $\pi r^2$ represent?
choices: The area of the whole outer circle of the ring
The area of the ring, without the hole in it
The distance around the edge of the inner circle
The area of the inner circle that is taken away
questions.answer: The area of the inner circle that is taken away
questions.solution: $\pi r^2$ is the area of a circle with radius $r$, the hole in the middle, and it is subtracted from the whole outer circle.

solve.answer: The area of the inner circle that is taken away
solve.work: pi R^2 is the outer circle; subtracting pi r^2 removes the inner circle (the hole).

questions.skill: Interpret a part of an expression in context
questions.stem: A rectangle has width $w$ meters and length $w + 4$ meters, so its perimeter is $2w + 2(w + 4)$. How many meters greater is the value of the part $2(w + 4)$ than the value of the part $2w$?
questions.solution: $2(w + 4) - 2w = 2w + 8 - 2w = 8$ meters, whatever $w$ is.

questions.skill: Compare what two expressions say about change
questions.stem: Town X has $8000(1.02)^t$ people after $t$ years and town Y has $8000 + 160t$ people. Which statement is true?
choices: X gains the same number of people each year, but Y gains more each year
Both towns gain the same number of people each year
X gains more people each year than the year before, but Y gains the same number
X gains fewer people each year than the year before, and Y gains the same number
questions.answer: X gains more people each year than the year before, but Y gains the same number
questions.solution: Y adds 160 people every year. X grows by 2 percent of its current size, and its size keeps growing, so each year it gains a little more than the year before.

solve.answer: X gains more people each year than the year before, but Y gains the same number
solve.work: X is exponential (x1.02 each year) so its yearly gain grows; Y is linear, +160 each year.

questions.skill: Interpret a part of an expression in context
questions.stem: Anya buys $a$ adult tickets at 12 dollars each and $c$ child tickets at 7 dollars each. Her total is $12a + 7c$ dollars. She buys 3 adult tickets and pays 64 dollars in all. How many child tickets does she buy?
questions.solution: The adult tickets cost $12 \cdot 3 = 36$ dollars. The child tickets cost $64 - 36 = 28$ dollars, which is $28 \div 7 = 4$ tickets.

The tank holds 140 liters after 10 minutes
The tank is empty after 6 minutes
questions.answer: The tank is empty after 6 minutes
questions.solution: After 6 minutes the tank holds $200 - 36 = 164$ liters, so it is not empty. The other statements are true: the start is 200, the rate is 6 a minute, and after 10 minutes it holds $200 - 60 = 140$.

questions.solution: The coefficient of $x$ is $m + 2$. Setting $m + 2 = 9$ gives $m = 7$.

questions.skill: Count the terms of an expression
questions.stem: As it is written, how many terms does the expression $(2x + 1)(x - 4) - 3(x + 2)^2 + 6$ have?
questions.solution: The terms are the product $(2x + 1)(x - 4)$, the product $3(x + 2)^2$ and the number 6. Each product is one term, so there are 3.

solve.work: Top-level terms separated by + / -: (2x+1)(x-4), -3(x+2)^2, 6. That is 3 terms.

questions.skill: Read an expression as a combination of simpler pieces
questions.stem: Which expression shows $2x^2 - 8x + 6$ as 2 times a simpler expression?
questions.solution: Dividing each term by 2 gives $x^2$, $-4x$ and $3$, so the expression is $2(x^2 - 4x + 3)$.

questions.skill: Interpret rates and starting values in a linear expression
questions.stem: The amount left to pay on a loan after $w$ weeks is $450 - 30w$ dollars. By how many dollars does the amount left decrease over 4 weeks?
questions.solution: The amount drops by 30 dollars each week, so over 4 weeks it drops by $30 \cdot 4 = 120$ dollars.

questions.skill: Interpret the parts of a quadratic expression
questions.stem: A theater finds that when it sells $x$ tickets, each ticket costs $50 - x$ dollars, so the revenue is $x(50 - x)$ dollars. What does the factor $50 - x$ represent?
choices: The number of tickets that are sold
The revenue from the tickets, in dollars
The number of tickets that go unsold
The price of one ticket, in dollars
questions.answer: The price of one ticket, in dollars
questions.solution: Revenue is the number of tickets times the price of one ticket. The number sold is $x$, so $50 - x$ is the price of one ticket.

solve.answer: The price of one ticket, in dollars
solve.work: Revenue = tickets * price; 50-x is the price per ticket.

questions.skill: Read an expression as a combination of simpler pieces
questions.stem: What is the smallest value that the expression $3(x - 2)^2 + 5$ can have?
questions.solution: The square $(x - 2)^2$ is never negative, so $3(x - 2)^2$ is at least 0. The smallest value of the whole expression is $0 + 5 = 5$.

solve.work: (x-2)^2 >= 0, minimum 0 at x=2, so smallest value 3*0+5 = 5.

questions.skill: Interpret rates and starting values in a linear expression
questions.stem: The cost of a taxi ride of $m$ miles is $15 + 2.5m$ dollars. How many more dollars does a 10-mile ride cost than a 6-mile ride?
questions.solution: The two rides differ by 4 miles, and each mile costs 2.5 dollars, so the difference is $4 \cdot 2.5 = 10$ dollars. (The 15 dollar fee is the same for both.)

questions.skill: Interpret a part of an expression in context
questions.stem: A phone costs $p$ dollars. A store takes 10 dollars off with a coupon and then adds 6 percent tax, so the total is $1.06(p - 10)$ dollars. What does $p - 10$ represent?
choices: The amount of tax that is added to the price
The price after the coupon and before the tax
The final total that is paid, including the tax
questions.answer: The price after the coupon and before the tax
questions.solution: The coupon takes 10 dollars off $p$, giving $p - 10$. Multiplying by 1.06 then adds the tax.

solve.answer: The price after the coupon and before the tax
solve.work: p - 10 is the price after the 10-dollar coupon; multiplying by 1.06 adds tax afterwards.

Plan D has the larger starting fee, and plan D charges more per minute
Plan C has the larger starting fee, but plan D charges more per minute
Plan C has the larger starting fee, and plan C charges more per minute
questions.answer: Plan D has the larger starting fee, but plan C charges more per minute
questions.solution: D starts at 35 and C at 20, so D has the larger starting fee. C adds 0.1 a minute and D adds 0.05, so C charges more per minute.

solve.work: Starting fees: C 20, D 35, so D larger. Per minute: C 0.10, D 0.05, so C charges more per minute.

questions.skill: Count the terms of an expression
questions.stem: Which of these expressions has exactly two terms after it is simplified?
questions.solution: $x^2 + 3x - x^2 + 4 = 3x + 4$, which has two terms. The others simplify to 6, $6x$ and 7, which have one term each.

questions.skill: Interpret the parts of a quadratic expression
questions.stem: A square of side $x + 4$ is cut into four pieces: an $x$ by $x$ square, two $x$ by 4 rectangles and a 4 by 4 square. Its area is $x^2 + 8x + 16$. Which term is the combined area of the two rectangles?
questions.solution: Each rectangle has area $4x$, so two of them have area $8x$.

questions.skill: Interpret the base, exponent and starting value of an exponential expression
questions.stem: A colony has $50 \cdot 2^{3t}$ members after $t$ days. By what number is the colony multiplied each day?
questions.solution: Each day $t$ goes up by 1, so the exponent $3t$ goes up by 3, which multiplies the amount by $2^3 = 8$.

solve.work: 2^(3t) = 8^t, so the factor each day is 8.

questions.skill: factor a monic quadratic
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $x^2 + 5x + 6$?
questions.solution: Find two numbers with product 6 and sum 5: they are 2 and 3. So $x^2 + 5x + 6 = (x+2)(x+3)$. Check: $(x+2)(x+3) = x^2 + 3x + 2x + 6$.

questions.skill: zeros from the factored form
questions.stem: The equation $(x-4)(x+7)=0$ has two solutions. What is the smaller one?
questions.solution: A product is 0 when a factor is 0. $x - 4 = 0$ gives $x = 4$, and $x + 7 = 0$ gives $x = -7$. The smaller solution is $-7$.

questions.skill: factor a difference of squares
questions.stem: Which product equals $x^2 - 49$?
questions.solution: A difference of squares factors as $a^2 - b^2 = (a-b)(a+b)$. Here $x^2 - 49 = x^2 - 7^2 = (x-7)(x+7)$. The middle terms cancel: $7x - 7x = 0$.

questions.skill: solve a quadratic equation by factoring
questions.stem: Solve $x^2 + 7x + 12 = 0$. What is the larger solution?
questions.solution: Factor: two numbers with product 12 and sum 7 are 3 and 4, so $(x+3)(x+4) = 0$. The solutions are $x = -3$ and $x = -4$. The larger is $-3$.

questions.skill: factor a monic quadratic
questions.stem: Factor $x^2 - 8x + 15$.
questions.solution: We need two numbers with product $+15$ and sum $-8$. Both must be negative: $-3$ and $-5$. So $x^2 - 8x + 15 = (x-3)(x-5)$.

questions.skill: solve a quadratic equation by factoring
questions.stem: The equation $x^2 + x - 6 = 0$ has one positive solution. What is it?
questions.solution: Two numbers with product $-6$ and sum $1$ are $3$ and $-2$. So $(x+3)(x-2) = 0$, giving $x = -3$ or $x = 2$. The positive solution is 2.

questions.skill: zeros of a quadratic function
questions.stem: What are the zeros of $f(x) = (x-1)(x+6)$?
questions.solution: Set each factor to 0: $x - 1 = 0$ gives $x = 1$, and $x + 6 = 0$ gives $x = -6$. The zeros are $1$ and $-6$.
