questions.stem: A club needs to raise at least 500 dollars. It already has 140 dollars and sells boxes of cookies for 6 dollars each. Which inequality shows the number of boxes, $b$, it must sell?
questions.solution: The money raised is $140 + 6b$ dollars, and it must be at least 500: $140 + 6b \ge 500$. "At least" means greater than or equal to.

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality from a situation
questions.stem: A runner wants to run at least 50 kilometers this month. She has run 18 kilometers and will run 4 kilometers each day from now on. What is the least number of days she needs to run?
questions.solution: The distance after $d$ more days is $18 + 4d$, and it must be at least 50: $18 + 4d \ge 50$. Subtract 18: $4d \ge 32$, so $d \ge 8$. The least number of days is 8.

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: A car is worth $20{,}000$ dollars and loses 10 percent of its value each year. Which equation can be used to find the number of years, $t$, until the car is worth $12{,}000$ dollars?
questions.solution: Losing 10 percent each year leaves 90 percent, so the value is multiplied by 0.9 each year: $20{,}000(0.9)^{t}$. Setting it equal to $12{,}000$ gives the equation. Using 0.1 keeps only 10 percent, 1.1 is growth, and subtracting is linear decay.

questions.skill: Solve an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: A 640 gram sample of a substance loses half of its mass every hour. After how many hours will 20 grams remain?
questions.solution: The mass after $h$ hours is $640\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{h}$. Solve $640\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{h} = 20$. Divide by 640: $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{h} = \dfrac{1}{32}$, so $h = 5$. (Check: 640, 320, 160, 80, 40, 20.)

questions.skill: Write a quadratic equation from a situation
questions.stem: A rectangle is 4 meters longer than it is wide, and its area is 60 square meters. Which equation can be used to find the width, $w$, in meters?
questions.solution: The length is $w + 4$, and area is width times length: $w(w + 4) = 60$. Adding the sides, or using the perimeter, does not give the area.

solve.work: Width w, length w+4, area w(w+4) = 60.

questions.skill: Solve a quadratic equation from a situation
questions.stem: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 72. What is the smaller integer?
questions.solution: Let the smaller integer be $n$: $n(n + 1) = 72$, so $n^2 + n - 72 = 0$. Factor: $(n + 9)(n - 8) = 0$. The positive solution is $n = 8$ (and $8 \cdot 9 = 72$).

questions.skill: Write a quadratic equation from a situation
questions.stem: The height of a ball, in feet, $t$ seconds after it is thrown is $h = -16t^{2} + 48t$. Which equation can be used to find when the ball is 32 feet high?
questions.solution: The height is $-16t^2 + 48t$, so the ball is 32 feet high when $-16t^{2} + 48t = 32$. Setting the height equal to 0 would find when it lands.

questions.skill: Solve a linear equation from a situation
questions.stem: A tank holds 80 liters. A hose adds 15 liters each minute while a drain removes 5 liters each minute, both running at once. After how many minutes will the tank hold 480 liters?
questions.solution: The tank gains $15 - 5 = 10$ liters each minute, so after $m$ minutes it holds $80 + 10m$ liters. Solve $80 + 10m = 480$: $10m = 400$, so $m = 40$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear equation from a situation
questions.stem: The length of a rectangle is 3 centimeters more than twice its width. The perimeter is 54 centimeters. What is the width, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Let $w$ be the width, so the length is $2w + 3$. The perimeter is $2w + 2(2w + 3) = 54$, which is $6w + 6 = 54$. Then $6w = 48$ and $w = 8$. (The length is 19, and $2(8 + 19) = 54$.)

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality from a situation
questions.stem: A phone plan costs 20 dollars a month plus 0.10 dollars for each text. Kim wants to spend at most 35 dollars in a month. She writes and solves an inequality for the number of texts, $t$, she can send. Which is the solution?
questions.solution: The cost is $20 + 0.10t \le 35$. Subtract 20: $0.10t \le 15$. Divide by 0.10: $t \le 150$. Reversing the sign gives $t \ge 150$; dividing by 10 instead of multiplying by 10 gives 1.5.

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality from a situation
questions.stem: Maria wants an average of at least 90 on her 4 tests. Her first three scores are 88, 92 and 85. What is the lowest score she can get on the fourth test and still reach her goal?
questions.solution: Let $x$ be the fourth score: $\dfrac{88 + 92 + 85 + x}{4} \ge 90$. Multiply by 4: $265 + x \ge 360$. Subtract 265: $x \ge 95$. The lowest score is 95.

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: An investment of $1{,}200$ dollars grows by 5 percent each year. Which inequality can be used to find the number of years, $t$, until the investment is worth more than $1{,}800$ dollars?
questions.solution: Growing 5 percent a year multiplies the value by 1.05 each year: $1{,}200(1.05)^{t}$. "More than" gives $>$. Using 0.05 shrinks the value, 1.5 is 50 percent growth, and adding is linear growth.

questions.skill: Solve an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: A rare coin is worth 150 dollars and doubles in value every 5 years. After how many years will the coin be worth 2400 dollars?
questions.solution: The value after $n$ years is $150 \cdot 2^{n/5}$. Solve $150 \cdot 2^{n/5} = 2400$: $2^{n/5} = 16 = 2^4$, so $\dfrac{n}{5} = 4$ and $n = 20$. (150, 300, 600, 1200, 2400 are the values after 0, 5, 10, 15, 20 years.)

questions.skill: Solve a quadratic equation from a situation
questions.stem: A picture is 12 inches wide and 8 inches tall. A frame of the same width, $x$ inches, goes all the way around the picture. The picture and frame together cover 140 square inches. What is $x$, in inches?
questions.solution: The picture and frame measure $12 + 2x$ by $8 + 2x$. So $(12 + 2x)(8 + 2x) = 140$, which is $4x^2 + 40x + 96 = 140$, or $x^2 + 10x - 11 = 0$. Factor: $(x + 11)(x - 1) = 0$. A width cannot be negative, so $x = 1$. (Check: $14 \cdot 10 = 140$.)

questions.skill: Write a quadratic equation from a situation
questions.stem: A rectangular pen is 2 feet longer than 3 times its width, $w$. Its area is 56 square feet. Which equation can be used to find $w$?
questions.solution: The length is "3 times the width, plus 2", so $3w + 2$. Area is width times length: $w(3w + 2) = 56$. (For $w = 4$, the length is 14 and $4 \cdot 14 = 56$.) Swapping the 2 and the 3 gives a different length.

questions.skill: Solve a quadratic equation from a situation
questions.stem: A ball's height, in feet, after $t$ seconds is $h = -16t^{2} + 80t$. What is the first time, in seconds, that the ball is 96 feet high?
questions.solution: Set $-16t^2 + 80t = 96$. Move everything to one side and divide by $-16$: $t^2 - 5t + 6 = 0$. Factor: $(t - 2)(t - 3) = 0$, so $t = 2$ or $t = 3$. The ball is 96 feet high going up at 2 seconds and coming down at 3 seconds, so the first time is 2.

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: Which situation can be modeled by the equation $50(0.8)^{t} = 20$, where $t$ is the number of years and the money is in thousands of dollars?
choices: A machine worth 50 gains 20 percent of its value each year and is worth 20 after $t$ years
A machine worth 50 loses 0.8 of its value each year and is worth 20 after $t$ years
A machine worth 20 loses 20 percent of its value each year and is worth 50 after $t$ years
A machine worth 50 loses 20 percent of its value each year and is worth 20 after $t$ years
questions.answer: A machine worth 50 loses 20 percent of its value each year and is worth 20 after $t$ years
questions.solution: The number 50 is the starting amount, and 0.8 means 80 percent is kept each year, which is a loss of 20 percent. The result after $t$ years is 20. So the machine starts at 50, loses 20 percent a year, and ends at 20. A gain would use 1.2, and losing 0.8 each year would be the linear $50 - 0.8t$.

solve.answer: A machine worth 50 loses 20 percent of its value each year and is worth 20 after $t$ years
solve.work: Factor 0.8 means keeps 80%, loses 20%; starts at 50, worth 20 after t years. D.

questions.skill: Write a linear equation from a situation
questions.stem: A gym charges a joining fee of 20 dollars plus 15 dollars for each month. Let $m$ be the number of months and $C$ the total cost in dollars. Which equation models the total cost?
questions.solution: The fee is paid once (20) and the monthly charge is paid $m$ times ($15m$). So $C = 15m + 20$. The rate per month is the number that multiplies $m$.

solve.work: Fixed fee 20 plus 15 per month: C = 15m + 20.

questions.skill: Write a linear equation from a situation
questions.stem: A taxi charges 3 dollars to start plus 2 dollars for each mile. The cost $C$ in dollars for $m$ miles is $C = 2m + b$. What is $b$?
questions.solution: The 3 dollars is charged even when $m = 0$, so it is the constant term: $b = 3$.

solve.work: Start charge 3 is the constant: b = 3.

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: A colony starts with 100 bacteria, and the number doubles every hour. Let $P$ be the number of bacteria after $t$ hours. Which equation models this?
questions.solution: The starting amount is 100 and it is multiplied by 2 once for each hour, so after $t$ hours it is $100 \cdot 2^t$. Repeated multiplication is an exponent on the growth factor.

questions.skill: Write a quadratic equation from a situation
questions.stem: A square garden has side length $s$ meters and area $A$ square meters. Which equation relates $A$ to $s$?
questions.solution: The area of a square is its side length times itself, so $A = s \cdot s = s^2$. The equation $A = 4s$ would be the perimeter.

solve.work: Area of a square = side squared: A = s^2.

questions.skill: Match an equation to a table of values
questions.stem: A table gives $y$ for each $x$. When $x$ is 0, 1, 2 and 3, $y$ is 5, 8, 11 and 14. Which equation matches the table?
questions.solution: The $y$-value goes up by 3 each time $x$ goes up by 1, so the slope is 3. At $x = 0$, $y = 5$, so the equation is $y = 3x + 5$. Check at $x = 3$: $3(3) + 5 = 14$.

solve.work: y goes up by 3 each step, starts at 5: y = 3x + 5.

questions.skill: Read features of a graph from its equation
questions.stem: The graph of $y = 2x + 7$ crosses the $y$-axis at the point $(0, k)$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: On the $y$-axis, $x = 0$. Then $y = 2(0) + 7 = 7$, so $k = 7$.

questions.skill: Read features of a graph from its equation
questions.stem: Which statement about the graph of $y = -3x + 4$ is true?
choices: It slants upward and crosses the $y$-axis at 4.
It slants downward and crosses the $y$-axis at 4.
It slants downward and crosses the $y$-axis at $-3$.
It slants upward and crosses the $y$-axis at $-3$.
questions.answer: It slants downward and crosses the $y$-axis at 4.
questions.solution: The slope is $-3$, which is negative, so the graph slants downward. The constant term is 4, so it crosses the $y$-axis at 4.

solve.answer: It slants downward and crosses the $y$-axis at 4.
solve.work: Slope -3 is negative so it slants downward; y-intercept 4.

questions.skill: Tell which kind of relationship a situation or table shows
questions.stem: Which situation is best modeled by an exponential equation?
choices: A runner jogs at a steady 8 kilometers per hour.
A plumber charges a 40 dollar visit fee plus 30 dollars per hour.
A square tile gets bigger and its area depends on its side length.
The number of bacteria in a dish doubles every hour.
questions.answer: The number of bacteria in a dish doubles every hour.
questions.solution: Doubling every hour means repeated multiplication by the same factor, which is exponential. The runner and the plumber change by the same amount each hour, so they are linear, and the area of a square depends on the side squared, which is quadratic.

solve.answer: The number of bacteria in a dish doubles every hour.
solve.work: Doubling every hour is repeated multiplication: exponential.

questions.skill: Use an equation to find points on its graph
questions.stem: The total cost at a gym is $C = 15m + 20$ dollars after $m$ months. What is the total cost after 4 months, in dollars?
questions.solution: Put $m = 4$ into the equation: $C = 15(4) + 20 = 60 + 20 = 80$ dollars.

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: A savings account starts at 500 dollars and grows by 4 percent each year. Let $B$ be the balance in dollars after $t$ years. Which equation models the balance?
questions.solution: Growing by 4 percent each year means multiplying by $1 + 0.04 = 1.04$ each year. Starting from 500, after $t$ years the balance is $B = 500 \cdot 1.04^{t}$.

solve.work: Grows by 4% per year: multiply by 1.04 each year, B = 500(1.04)^t. 0.04^t shrinks, 1.4^t is 40%, 500+0.04t is linear and tiny.

questions.skill: Write a linear equation from a situation
questions.stem: Adult tickets cost 6 dollars each and student tickets cost 4 dollars each. A club sells $a$ adult tickets and $s$ student tickets and collects exactly 240 dollars. Which equation fits this situation?
questions.solution: Adult sales bring in $6a$ dollars and student sales bring in $4s$ dollars. Together they are 240 dollars: $6a + 4s = 240$. Each price multiplies its own ticket count.

solve.work: 6 per adult times a plus 4 per student times s equals 240: 6a + 4s = 240.

questions.skill: Write a linear equation from a situation
questions.stem: A hiker walks along a straight trail at a steady pace. She is 14 miles from the trailhead after 2 hours and 26 miles from it after 4 hours. Her distance $y$ in miles after $x$ hours is $y = mx + b$. What is $m + b$?
questions.solution: The rate is $m = \frac{26 - 14}{4 - 2} = 6$ miles per hour. Then $14 = 6(2) + b$, so $b = 2$. The answer is $m + b = 6 + 2 = 8$.

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: A car is worth 20,000 dollars when it is new and loses 15 percent of its value each year. Let $V$ be its value in dollars after $t$ years. Which equation models this?
questions.solution: Losing 15 percent each year means keeping 85 percent, so the value is multiplied by $0.85$ each year: $V = 20{,}000(0.85)^t$. A factor of $0.15$ would keep only 15 percent, and $1.15$ would be growth.

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: A town of 8,000 people grows by 5 percent each year. Its population after $t$ years is $P = 8000 \cdot b^t$. What is $b$?
questions.solution: Growing by 5 percent means each year's population is $100\% + 5\% = 105\%$ of the year before, so the growth factor is $b = 1.05$.

solve.work: Growth of 5% multiplies by 1.05 each year: b = 1.05.

questions.skill: Write a quadratic equation from a situation
questions.stem: A rectangle has width $w$ and length $w + 5$. Which equation gives its area $A$?
questions.solution: Area is length times width: $A = w(w + 5) = w^2 + 5w$. The 5 must be multiplied by $w$ as well.

questions.skill: Match an equation to a table of values
questions.stem: A table gives $y$ for each $x$. When $x$ is 0, 1, 2 and 3, $y$ is 2, 6, 18 and 54. Which equation matches the table?
questions.solution: Each $y$-value is 3 times the one before, so the relationship is exponential with growth factor 3. At $x = 0$, $y = 2$, so $y = 2 \cdot 3^x$. Check at $x = 3$: $2 \cdot 27 = 54$.

questions.skill: Match an equation to a table of values
questions.stem: A table gives $y$ for each $x$. When $x$ is 0, 1, 2 and 3, $y$ is $-3$, $-1$, 5 and 15. The equation has the form $y = ax^2 + c$. What is $a + c$?

questions.skill: Read features of a graph from its equation
questions.stem: A tank holds 50 gallons of water, and a pump removes 4 gallons each minute. The number of gallons left after $t$ minutes is $g = 50 - 4t$. The graph crosses the $t$-axis at what value of $t$, in minutes?
questions.solution: On the $t$-axis, $g = 0$. Solve $50 - 4t = 0$: $t = \frac{50}{4} = 12.5$. The tank is empty after 12.5 minutes.

questions.skill: Read features of a graph from its equation
questions.stem: Which statement about the graph of $y = 5 \cdot 2^x$ is true?
choices: It crosses the $y$-axis at 2 and rises faster and faster to the right.
It crosses the $y$-axis at 5 and rises by the same amount each time $x$ goes up by 1.
It crosses the $y$-axis at 5 and rises faster and faster to the right.
It crosses the $y$-axis at 10 and rises faster and faster to the right.
questions.answer: It crosses the $y$-axis at 5 and rises faster and faster to the right.
questions.solution: At $x = 0$, $y = 5 \cdot 2^0 = 5$, so it crosses the $y$-axis at 5. The values are multiplied by 2 each step, so the rises get bigger and bigger. It is not a straight line.

solve.answer: It crosses the $y$-axis at 5 and rises faster and faster to the right.
solve.work: At x=0, y = 5; exponential growth with base 2 rises faster and faster.

questions.skill: Tell which kind of relationship a situation or table shows
questions.stem: A table gives $y$ for each $x$. When $x$ is 1, 2, 3 and 4, $y$ is 1, 4, 9 and 16. What kind of relationship does the table show?
choices: Linear, because the $y$-values keep getting larger as $x$ gets larger.
Quadratic, because the differences between the $y$-values go up by the same amount each time.
Exponential, because the $y$-values get larger by more each time $x$ goes up by 1.
Exponential, because each $y$-value is a whole number times the one before it.
questions.answer: Quadratic, because the differences between the $y$-values go up by the same amount each time.
questions.solution: The differences between the $y$-values are 3, 5 and 7, and those differences go up by 2 each time, which is the signature of a quadratic ($y = x^2$). A linear table has equal differences, and an exponential table has equal ratios (here the ratios are 4, 2.25 and 1.78).

solve.answer: Quadratic, because the differences between the $y$-values go up by the same amount each time.
solve.work: Differences 3, 5, 7 go up by 2 each time (constant second difference): quadratic (y = x^2). Other options give wrong type or false reasoning (9/4 is not whole).

questions.skill: Write a linear equation from a situation
questions.stem: A line passes through the points $(2, 7)$ and $(5, 16)$. Which equation is an equation of this line?
questions.solution: The slope is $\frac{16 - 7}{5 - 2} = 3$. Using $(2, 7)$: $7 = 3(2) + b$, so $b = 1$. The equation is $y = 3x + 1$. Check with $(5, 16)$: $3(5) + 1 = 16$.

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: A patient takes 80 milligrams of a medicine. The amount in the body is cut in half every 6 hours. Let $A$ be the amount in milligrams after $t$ hours. Which equation models this?
questions.solution: The amount is halved once for every 6 hours, so the number of halvings is $\frac{t}{6}$. That gives $A = 80\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{t}{6}}$. Check: at $t = 6$ it is $80 \cdot \frac{1}{2} = 40$.

solve.work: Halves every 6 hours: number of halvings is t/6, so A = 80(1/2)^(t/6).

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: A culture starts with 6 bacteria and triples every 2 hours. After $t$ hours the number of bacteria is $N = 6 \cdot 3^{kt}$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: Tripling happens once every 2 hours, so the exponent must be $\frac{t}{2}$. Then $kt = \frac{t}{2}$ and $k = \frac{1}{2}$. Check: at $t = 2$, $N = 6 \cdot 3^1 = 18$.

solve.work: Triples every 2 hours: exponent t/2, so k = 1/2.

questions.skill: Write a quadratic equation from a situation
questions.stem: A baseball is hit upward from a height of 5 feet at a speed of 30 feet per second. After $t$ seconds its height in feet is $h = -16t^2 + vt + s$, where $v$ is the starting speed in feet per second and $s$ is the starting height in feet. Which equation models the ball's height?
questions.solution: Put $v = 30$ and $s = 5$ into the formula: $h = -16t^2 + 30t + 5$. At $t = 0$ the height is 5 feet, the starting height, as it should be.

questions.skill: Write a quadratic equation from a situation
questions.stem: A shop finds that if it sells $x$ scarves in a day, the price of each scarf is $50 - 2x$ dollars. The daily revenue (the number sold times the price of each) can be written $R = ax^2 + bx$. What is $a + b$?

questions.skill: Match an equation to a table of values
questions.stem: A table gives $y$ for each $x$. When $x$ is 0, 1, 2 and 3, $y$ is 3, 12, 48 and 192. The equation has the form $y = a \cdot b^x$. What is $a + b$?
questions.solution: At $x = 0$, $y = a = 3$. Each $y$-value is $12 \div 3 = 4$ times the one before, so $b = 4$. Check: $3 \cdot 4^3 = 192$. So $a + b = 7$.

questions.skill: Read features of a graph from its equation
questions.stem: A stone is thrown from the ground and its height in feet after $t$ seconds is $h = -16t^2 + 64t$. The graph is at height 0 when $t = 0$ and again at a later time. What is the later time, in seconds?
questions.solution: Set $h = 0$ and factor: $-16t(t - 4) = 0$. So $t = 0$ or $t = 4$. The stone lands at $t = 4$ seconds.

questions.skill: Read features of a graph from its equation
questions.stem: Which equation has a graph that crosses the $y$-axis at $(0, 6)$ and crosses the $x$-axis at $(3, 0)$?
questions.solution: The $y$-intercept 6 means the equation ends in $+ 6$. Then $0 = 3m + 6$ gives $m = -2$. So $y = -2x + 6$. The graph of $y = 2x + 6$ crosses the $x$-axis at $-3$, and $y = -3x + 6$ crosses it at 2.

questions.skill: Use an equation to find points on its graph
questions.stem: The graph of $3m + 5l = 90$ crosses the $l$-axis at $(0, k)$ and the $m$-axis at $(j, 0)$. What is $j + k$?

questions.skill: Use an equation to find points on its graph
questions.stem: A model rocket's height in feet after $t$ seconds is $h = -16t^2 + 48t + 6$. What is its height after 2 seconds, in feet?

questions.skill: Write a system of equations from a story
questions.stem: A school sold 40 tickets in all. Adult tickets cost 8 dollars each and student tickets cost 5 dollars each. The school collected 245 dollars. Let $a$ be the number of adult tickets and $s$ the number of student tickets. Which system models the story?
questions.solution: The number of tickets is $a + s = 40$. The money is 8 dollars for each adult ticket and 5 dollars for each student ticket: $8a + 5s = 245$.

solve.work: Count: a + s = 40; money: 8a + 5s = 245 (gives a = 15, s = 25).

questions.skill: Solve a system about two related quantities
questions.stem: Mia and Jo picked 12 apples in all. Mia picked 4 more apples than Jo. With $m$ for Mia's apples and $j$ for Jo's, the system is $m + j = 12$ and $m = j + 4$. How many apples did Mia pick?
questions.solution: Replace $m$ in the first equation: $(j + 4) + j = 12$, so $2j = 8$ and $j = 4$. Then $m = 4 + 4 = 8$.

questions.skill: Translate a phrase into an inequality
questions.stem: Balls cost 6 dollars each. A coach can spend at most 100 dollars on balls. Which inequality shows the number of balls $n$ she can buy?
questions.solution: "At most 100 dollars" means the cost can be 100 or less. The cost of $n$ balls is $6n$, so $6n \le 100$.

solve.issues: Minor: option 6n < 100 has the same whole-number solutions (100 is not a multiple of 6), though "at most" clearly means <=.

questions.skill: Write a system of inequalities from a story
questions.stem: A bus holds at most 50 people. A trip needs at least 2 adults. Let $a$ be the number of adults and $c$ the number of children. Which system models the story?
questions.solution: "At most 50 people" is $a + c \le 50$. "At least 2 adults" is $a \ge 2$. The other systems use the wrong direction or leave out "equal to".

solve.work: At most 50 people: a + c <= 50; at least 2 adults: a >= 2.

questions.skill: Solve a counts-and-prices system
questions.stem: Two pens and 1 notebook cost 7 dollars. One pen and 1 notebook cost 5 dollars. With $p$ for the cost of a pen and $n$ for the cost of a notebook, the system is $2p + n = 7$ and $p + n = 5$. How many dollars does one pen cost?
questions.solution: Subtract the second equation from the first: $(2p + n) - (p + n) = 7 - 5$, so $p = 2$ dollars. Then $n = 3$.

questions.skill: Check a pair of values against the constraints
questions.stem: Maya spends at most 10 dollars on $x$ pencils that cost 2 dollars each and $y$ erasers that cost 1 dollar each, so $2x + y \le 10$. Which purchase is possible?
questions.solution: For $x = 3$ and $y = 4$: $2(3) + 4 = 10$, which is at most 10. The other purchases cost 11 dollars each.

questions.skill: Interpret a part of a model or its solution
questions.stem: A farm has $x$ chickens and $y$ cows. A model is $x + y = 30$ and $2x + 4y = 80$. What does the term $4y$ represent?
choices: The number of legs on all the chickens
The total number of animals on the farm
The number of cows on the farm
The number of legs on all the cows
questions.answer: The number of legs on all the cows
questions.solution: Each cow has 4 legs and there are $y$ cows, so the cows have $4y$ legs in all.

solve.answer: The number of legs on all the cows
solve.work: Cows have 4 legs, so 4y is the legs on all the cows.

questions.skill: Solve a system about two related quantities
questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 24 centimeters. Its length is 2 centimeters more than its width. With $l$ for the length and $w$ for the width, the system is $2l + 2w = 24$ and $l = w + 2$. What is the width, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Replace $l$: $2(w + 2) + 2w = 24$, so $4w + 4 = 24$ and $w = 5$ centimeters. The length is 7.

questions.skill: Write a system with an equation and an inequality
questions.stem: A concert has 120 tickets and all of them are sold. At least 30 of the tickets sold are child tickets. Let $a$ be the number of adult tickets and $c$ the number of child tickets. Which system models the story?
questions.solution: "All 120 sold" is an equation: $a + c = 120$. "At least 30 are child tickets" is an inequality: $c \ge 30$.

solve.work: All 120 sold: a + c = 120; at least 30 child: c >= 30.

questions.skill: Find a limit from the constraints
questions.stem: A bakery can make at most 20 loaves a day. With $p$ plain loaves and $w$ wheat loaves, the limit is $p + w \le 20$. If the bakery makes 12 plain loaves, what is the greatest number of wheat loaves it can make?
questions.solution: Put $p = 12$: $12 + w \le 20$, so $w \le 8$. The greatest number is 8.

questions.skill: Write a system of equations from a story
questions.stem: Jo has 18 coins, all dimes and quarters, worth 3.30 dollars in all. Let $d$ be the number of dimes and $q$ the number of quarters. Which system models the story?
questions.solution: The number of coins is $d + q = 18$. A dime is worth 0.10 dollars and a quarter 0.25 dollars, so the value is $0.10d + 0.25q = 3.30$.

questions.skill: Solve a counts-and-prices system
questions.stem: Adult tickets cost 9 dollars each and child tickets cost 5 dollars each. A family buys 6 tickets and pays 38 dollars. How many adult tickets did they buy?
questions.solution: With $a + c = 6$ and $9a + 5c = 38$, replace $c$ with $6 - a$: $9a + 30 - 5a = 38$. Then $4a = 8$ and $a = 2$.

questions.skill: Write a system of inequalities from a story
questions.stem: A gardener buys tomato plants that cost 3 dollars each and pepper plants that cost 2 dollars each. She wants at least 10 plants in all and can spend at most 36 dollars. Let $t$ be the number of tomato plants and $p$ the number of pepper plants. Which system models the story?
questions.solution: "At least 10 plants" is $t + p \ge 10$. The cost is 3 dollars for each tomato plant and 2 dollars for each pepper plant, and "at most 36 dollars" gives $3t + 2p \le 36$.

solve.work: At least 10 plants: t + p >= 10; at most 36 dollars: 3t + 2p <= 36.

questions.skill: Check a pair of values against the constraints
questions.stem: A fundraiser sells $x$ cookies at 2 dollars each and $y$ brownies at 3 dollars each. The group needs $2x + 3y \ge 100$ and can bake only $x + y \le 45$ items. Which sale meets both conditions?
questions.solution: For 20 and 20: $40 + 60 = 100$, which is at least 100, and $20 + 20 = 40$, which is at most 45. The others miss one condition: 80 dollars, 50 items, and 95 dollars.

questions.skill: Solve a counts-and-prices system
questions.stem: Nuts cost 6 dollars a pound and raisins cost 4 dollars a pound. A 10 pound mix of nuts and raisins costs 52 dollars. How many pounds of nuts are in the mix?
questions.solution: With $n + r = 10$ and $6n + 4r = 52$, replace $r$ with $10 - n$: $6n + 40 - 4n = 52$. Then $2n = 12$ and $n = 6$ pounds.

questions.skill: Interpret a part of a model or its solution
questions.stem: A truck carries $x$ small boxes of 2 pounds each and $y$ large boxes of 5 pounds each. Its weight limit is modeled by $2x + 5y \le 60$. The point $(10, 8)$ satisfies $2x + 5y = 60$. What does that mean?
choices: The truck is loaded to exactly its limit with 10 small boxes and 8 large boxes
The truck is over its limit with 10 small boxes and 8 large boxes
The truck carries 60 boxes in all, 10 small and 8 large
The truck can still take more weight after 10 small boxes and 8 large boxes
questions.answer: The truck is loaded to exactly its limit with 10 small boxes and 8 large boxes
questions.solution: Check: $2(10) + 5(8) = 20 + 40 = 60$ pounds, which equals the limit. So the truck is full but not over the limit.

solve.answer: The truck is loaded to exactly its limit with 10 small boxes and 8 large boxes
solve.work: 2(10) + 5(8) = 60 exactly: loaded to exactly its limit.

questions.skill: Write a system with an equation and an inequality
questions.stem: A student walks for $h$ hours at 3 miles per hour and bikes for $b$ hours at 9 miles per hour. She goes exactly 36 miles and spends at most 6 hours in all. Which system models the story?
questions.solution: Distance is rate times time: $3h + 9b$ must equal 36. "At most 6 hours in all" gives $h + b \le 6$.

questions.skill: Find a limit from the constraints
questions.stem: A coach picks $x$ forwards and $y$ defenders. The team has at most 12 players, so $x + y \le 12$. There must be at least twice as many defenders as forwards, so $y \ge 2x$. What is the greatest number of forwards possible?
questions.solution: Since $y \ge 2x$, we have $x + y \ge 3x$. Together with $x + y \le 12$, this gives $3x \le 12$, so $x \le 4$. With $x = 4$ and $y = 8$ both conditions hold.

solve.work: y >= 2x and x + y <= 12 give 3x <= x + y <= 12, x <= 4; x = 4, y = 8 works.

questions.skill: Translate a phrase into an inequality
questions.stem: Tickets cost 5 dollars each plus a one-time fee of 4 dollars. Liam can spend no more than 50 dollars. Which inequality shows the number of tickets $t$ he can buy?
questions.solution: The cost is 5 dollars for each of the $t$ tickets plus the fee once: $5t + 4$. "No more than 50" means $\le 50$.

solve.work: 5t for tickets plus 4 once, no more than 50: 5t + 4 <= 50.

questions.skill: Solve a system about two related quantities
questions.stem: Mia is 3 times as old as her cousin. In 4 years, the sum of their ages will be 40. With $m$ for Mia's age and $c$ for her cousin's age now, the system is $m = 3c$ and $(m + 4) + (c + 4) = 40$. How old is Mia now?
questions.solution: The second equation gives $m + c = 32$. Replace $m$ with $3c$: $4c = 32$, so $c = 8$ and $m = 24$.

questions.skill: Write a system of equations from a story
questions.stem: A chemist mixes $x$ liters of a 10% acid solution with $y$ liters of a 30% acid solution to make 20 liters of a 25% acid solution. Which system models the story?
questions.solution: The volumes add to 20 liters: $x + y = 20$. The pure acid is $0.10x + 0.30y$, which must equal 25% of 20 liters, or $0.25(20)$.

questions.skill: Solve a rates or break-even system
questions.stem: A boat travels 30 miles downstream in 3 hours and 30 miles back upstream in 5 hours. With $b$ for the boat's speed in still water and $c$ for the current, both in miles per hour, the system is $3(b + c) = 30$ and $5(b - c) = 30$. What is $b$?
questions.solution: The downstream speed is $b + c = 10$ and the upstream speed is $b - c = 6$. Adding the equations gives $2b = 16$, so $b = 8$ miles per hour.

questions.skill: Write a system of inequalities from a story
questions.stem: A shop makes $s$ shirts, which take 2 hours each, and $h$ hats, which take 1 hour each. It has at most 40 hours a week, must make at least 5 shirts, and cannot make a negative number of hats. Which system models the story?
questions.solution: Shirts use $2s$ hours and hats use $h$ hours, so $2s + h \le 40$. "At least 5 shirts" is $s \ge 5$ and no negative hats is $h \ge 0$.

questions.skill: Find a limit from the constraints
questions.stem: Chairs rent for 2 dollars each and tables rent for 3 dollars each. An event can spend at most 30 dollars and needs at least 4 tables. With $c$ chairs and $t$ tables, the conditions are $2c + 3t \le 30$ and $t \ge 4$. What is the greatest number of chairs it can rent?
questions.solution: The most chairs are possible with the fewest tables, $t = 4$. Then $2c + 12 \le 30$, so $2c \le 18$ and $c \le 9$.

solve.work: Fewest tables gives most chairs: t = 4, 2c <= 30 - 12 = 18, c <= 9; c = 9 uses exactly 30.

questions.skill: Check a pair of values against the constraints
questions.stem: Dana has at most 60 minutes to exercise: $x$ minutes of running and $y$ minutes of cycling. Running burns 10 calories a minute and cycling burns 6 calories a minute. She wants to burn at least 400 calories. Which plan meets both goals?
questions.solution: The conditions are $x + y \le 60$ and $10x + 6y \ge 400$. For 30 and 30: 60 minutes and $300 + 180 = 480$ calories. The others burn 320 calories, use 70 minutes, and burn 340 calories.

questions.skill: Interpret a part of a model or its solution
questions.stem: A company's cost for $n$ items is $C = 500 + 4n$ dollars and its revenue is $R = 9n$ dollars. The solution of the system, where $C = R$, is $n = 100$ and $C = R = 900$. What does the solution mean?
choices: When 100 items are made and sold, cost and revenue are both 900 dollars
The company makes 900 dollars of profit on 100 items
After 900 items are sold, the company earns 100 dollars
The company makes 100 dollars on each item sold
questions.answer: When 100 items are made and sold, cost and revenue are both 900 dollars
questions.solution: At $n = 100$: $500 + 4(100) = 900$ and $9(100) = 900$. Cost equals revenue there, so the company just breaks even.

solve.answer: When 100 items are made and sold, cost and revenue are both 900 dollars
solve.work: At n = 100, C = 500 + 400 = 900 and R = 900: break-even.

questions.skill: Solve a rates or break-even system
questions.stem: Kayak shop A charges a 14 dollar fee plus 7.50 dollars an hour. Shop B charges a 6 dollar fee plus 9.50 dollars an hour. For how many hours is the total cost the same at both shops?
questions.solution: The costs are $14 + 7.5x$ and $6 + 9.5x$. Setting them equal gives $8 = 2x$, so $x = 4$ hours. Both cost 44 dollars.

questions.skill: Translate a phrase into an inequality
questions.stem: A box holds $x$ books and $y$ magazines. The number of magazines is at most 3 more than twice the number of books. Which inequality models the story?
questions.solution: Twice the number of books is $2x$, and 3 more than that is $2x + 3$. "At most" means $y \le 2x + 3$.

solve.work: Twice the books plus 3 is 2x + 3; magazines at most that: y <= 2x + 3.

questions.skill: Solve a counts-and-prices system
questions.stem: A theater sold 250 tickets in all. Adult tickets cost 11 dollars each and child tickets cost 7 dollars each. The theater collected 2,430 dollars. How many child tickets were sold?

questions.skill: Write a system of inequalities from a story
questions.stem: Maya has 100 dollars to spend on $b$ books that cost 12 dollars each. She wants at least 20 dollars left over and wants to buy at least 2 books. Which system models the story?
questions.solution: The books cost $12b$ and at least 20 dollars must remain, so $12b + 20 \le 100$. Buying at least 2 books gives $b \ge 2$.

solve.work: Spending 12b, at least 20 left: 12b + 20 <= 100; at least 2 books: b >= 2.

questions.skill: Solve a product formula for a variable
questions.stem: The distance formula is $d = rt$, with distance d, rate r and time t. Solve for $t$.
questions.solution: Divide both sides of $d = rt$ by r to get $t = \frac{d}{r}$.

solve.work: Divide both sides of d = rt by r: t = d/r.

questions.skill: Solve a product formula for a variable
questions.stem: The volume of a box is $V = lwh$. Solve this formula for $h$.
questions.solution: h is multiplied by $lw$, so divide both sides by $lw$: $h = \frac{V}{lw}$.

solve.work: Divide both sides by lw: h = V/(lw).

questions.skill: Solve a sum or difference formula for a variable
questions.stem: The perimeter of a triangle with sides a, b and c is $P = a + b + c$. Solve for $c$.
questions.solution: Subtract a and b from both sides of $P = a + b + c$: $c = P - a - b$.

solve.work: Subtract a and b from both sides: c = P - a - b.

questions.skill: Solve a product formula for a variable
questions.stem: A car travels 150 miles in 3 hours. Using $d = rt$, solve for $r$ and find the rate in miles per hour.
questions.solution: Divide both sides of $d = rt$ by t to get $r = \frac{d}{t}$. Then $r = \frac{150}{3} = 50$.

questions.skill: Solve a sum or difference formula for a variable
questions.stem: Solve the formula $y = mx + b$ for $b$.
questions.solution: Subtract mx from both sides: $b = y - mx$.

solve.work: Subtract mx from both sides: b = y - mx.

questions.skill: Solve a product formula for a variable
questions.stem: The force formula is $F = ma$. A force of 60 newtons acts on a 12 kilogram object. Solve for $a$ and find the acceleration.
questions.solution: Divide both sides of $F = ma$ by m to get $a = \frac{F}{m}$. Then $a = \frac{60}{12} = 5$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula with a fraction coefficient
questions.stem: The area of a triangle is $A = \frac{1}{2}bh$. A triangle has area 24 and base 8. Find its height h.
questions.solution: Multiply both sides by 2: $2A = bh$. Divide by b: $h = \frac{2A}{b} = \frac{2 \times 24}{8} = 6$.

questions.skill: Solve a product formula for a variable
questions.stem: The circumference of a circle is $C = 2\pi r$. Solve this formula for $r$.
questions.solution: r is multiplied by $2\pi$, so divide both sides by $2\pi$: $r = \frac{C}{2\pi}$.

solve.work: Divide by 2 pi: r = C/(2 pi).

questions.skill: Solve a formula needing two steps
questions.stem: The perimeter of a rectangle is $P = 2l + 2w$. A rectangle has perimeter 36 and length 11. Find its width w.
questions.solution: Subtract $2l = 22$ from 36 to get $2w = 14$. Divide by 2: $w = 7$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula for one quantity
questions.stem: A taxi fare is $F = 2m + 3$ dollars for a ride of $m$ miles. Which equation gives $m$ in terms of $F$?
questions.solution: Undo the added 3 first: $F - 3 = 2m$. Then divide both sides by 2: $m = \frac{F - 3}{2}$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula with a fraction coefficient
questions.stem: The area of a triangle is $A = \frac{1}{2}bh$. Solve for $b$.
questions.solution: Multiply both sides by 2: $2A = bh$. Divide both sides by h: $b = \frac{2A}{h}$.

solve.work: Multiply by 2: 2A = bh, divide by h: b = 2A/h.

questions.skill: Solve a formula needing two steps
questions.stem: The perimeter of a rectangle is $P = 2l + 2w$. Solve for $w$.
questions.solution: Subtract $2l$ from both sides: $P - 2l = 2w$. Divide both sides by 2: $w = \frac{P - 2l}{2}$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula with a fraction coefficient
questions.stem: The formula $C = \frac{5}{9}(F - 32)$ changes Fahrenheit F to Celsius C. Solve for $F$.
questions.solution: Multiply both sides by $\frac{9}{5}$: $\frac{9}{5}C = F - 32$. Add 32 to both sides: $F = \frac{9}{5}C + 32$.

questions.skill: Rearrange a formula, then use it
questions.stem: Use $F = \frac{9}{5}C + 32$ to find the Fahrenheit temperature when the Celsius temperature is 35.
questions.solution: Substitute $C = 35$: $\frac{9}{5} \times 35 = 63$, and $63 + 32 = 95$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula needing two steps
questions.stem: The line $ax + by = c$ is written in standard form. Solve the equation for $y$.
questions.solution: Subtract ax from both sides: $by = c - ax$. Divide both sides by b: $y = \frac{c - ax}{b}$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula needing two steps
questions.stem: Solve $2x + 3y = 18$ for $y$, then find y when $x = 3$.
questions.solution: Subtract $2x$: $3y = 18 - 2x$. Divide by 3: $y = \frac{18 - 2x}{3}$. For $x = 3$, $y = \frac{18 - 6}{3} = 4$.

questions.skill: Solve a product formula for a variable
questions.stem: The volume of a cylinder is $V = \pi r^2 h$. Solve this formula for $h$.
questions.solution: h is multiplied by $\pi r^2$, so divide both sides by $\pi r^2$: $h = \frac{V}{\pi r^2}$.

solve.work: Divide by pi r^2: h = V/(pi r^2).

questions.skill: Rearrange a formula from a context
questions.stem: Simple interest is $I = prt$, with rate r written as a decimal. Solve for $t$ and find the time in years when the interest is 90 dollars, the principal p is 500 dollars and the rate is 0.06.
questions.solution: Divide both sides of $I = prt$ by $pr$: $t = \frac{I}{pr}$. Then $t = \frac{90}{500 \times 0.06} = \frac{90}{30} = 3$ years.

questions.skill: Solve a formula where the variable appears in a sum or group
questions.stem: The mean m of three scores a, b and c is $m = \frac{a + b + c}{3}$. Solve for $c$.
questions.solution: Multiply both sides by 3: $3m = a + b + c$. Subtract a and b: $c = 3m - a - b$.

solve.work: 3m = a + b + c, so c = 3m - a - b.

questions.skill: Solve a formula needing two steps
questions.stem: Solve $y = mx + b$ for $x$.
questions.solution: Subtract b from both sides: $y - b = mx$. Divide both sides by m: $x = \frac{y - b}{m}$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula where the variable appears in a sum or group
questions.stem: The area of a trapezoid is $A = \frac{1}{2}(b_1 + b_2)h$. Solve for $b_1$.
questions.solution: Multiply both sides by 2: $2A = (b_1 + b_2)h$. Divide by h: $\frac{2A}{h} = b_1 + b_2$. Subtract $b_2$: $b_1 = \frac{2A}{h} - b_2$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula where the variable appears in a sum or group
questions.stem: A trapezoid has area 60, height 5 and one base $b_2 = 10$. Using $A = \frac{1}{2}(b_1 + b_2)h$, find the other base $b_1$.
questions.solution: Multiply by 2: $120 = (b_1 + 10) \times 5$. Divide by 5: $24 = b_1 + 10$. So $b_1 = 14$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula where the variable appears in a sum or group
questions.stem: The surface area of a cylinder is $S = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h$. Solve for $h$.
questions.solution: Subtract $2\pi r^2$ from both sides: $S - 2\pi r^2 = 2\pi r h$. Divide both sides by $2\pi r$: $h = \frac{S - 2\pi r^2}{2\pi r}$.

solve.work: S - 2 pi r^2 = 2 pi r h, h = (S - 2 pi r^2)/(2 pi r).

questions.skill: Solve a formula with a fraction coefficient
questions.stem: A line has x-intercept a and y-intercept b, so its equation is $\frac{x}{a} + \frac{y}{b} = 1$. Solve for $y$.
questions.solution: Subtract $\frac{x}{a}$: $\frac{y}{b} = 1 - \frac{x}{a}$. Multiply both sides by b: $y = b - \frac{bx}{a}$.

solve.work: y/b = 1 - x/a, y = b(1 - x/a) = b - bx/a.

questions.skill: Solve a formula with a fraction coefficient
questions.stem: Kinetic energy is $E = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$. Solve for $m$, then find the mass in kilograms of an object with energy 100 joules and speed 5 meters per second.
questions.solution: Multiply by 2: $2E = mv^2$. Divide by $v^2$: $m = \frac{2E}{v^2}$. Then $m = \frac{2 \times 100}{25} = 8$.

questions.skill: Rearrange a formula from a context
questions.stem: Simple interest gives $A = P(1 + rt)$. Solve for $r$, then find r (as a decimal) when $A = 1260$, $P = 1000$ and $t = 4$.
questions.solution: Divide by P: $\frac{A}{P} = 1 + rt$. Subtract 1: $\frac{A}{P} - 1 = rt$. Divide by t: $r = \frac{A - P}{Pt}$. Then $r = \frac{260}{4000} = 0.065$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula where the variable appears in a sum or group
questions.stem: The point-slope form is $y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)$. Solve it for $x$, then find x when $y = 11$, $y_1 = 3$, $m = 2$ and $x_1 = 4$.
questions.solution: Divide by m: $\frac{y - y_1}{m} = x - x_1$. Add $x_1$: $x = x_1 + \frac{y - y_1}{m}$. Then $x = 4 + \frac{8}{2} = 8$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula where the variable appears in a sum or group
questions.stem: Solve $ax + b = cx + d$ for $x$. Assume $a \ne c$.
questions.solution: Subtract cx and b from both sides: $ax - cx = d - b$. Factor: $(a - c)x = d - b$. Divide by $a - c$: $x = \frac{d - b}{a - c}$.

solve.work: ax - cx = d - b, x(a - c) = d - b, x = (d - b)/(a - c).

questions.skill: Solve a formula with a fraction coefficient
questions.stem: An object falls a distance $d = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$. Solve for $g$, then find g in meters per second squared when $d = 80$ meters and $t = 4$ seconds.
questions.solution: Multiply by 2: $2d = gt^2$. Divide by $t^2$: $g = \frac{2d}{t^2}$. Then $g = \frac{160}{16} = 10$.

questions.skill: Rearrange a formula from a context
questions.stem: A plumber charges a flat fee f plus h dollars per hour, so for t hours the cost is $C = f + ht$. Solve for $t$.
questions.solution: Subtract f from both sides: $C - f = ht$. Divide both sides by h: $t = \frac{C - f}{h}$.

questions.skill: Name the step that was done
questions.stem: Solving $3x + 5 = 20$, a student writes $3x = 15$. What was done to both sides?
questions.solution: The 5 on the left was removed by subtracting 5. To keep the sides equal, 5 is also subtracted from 20, giving 15. So 5 was subtracted from both sides.

questions.skill: Name the step that was done
questions.stem: To solve $x - 6 = 9$, a student adds the same number to both sides. What number is added?
questions.solution: Adding 6 undoes the subtraction of 6 and leaves $x = 15$. So the number added is 6.

questions.skill: Justify a step with a property
questions.stem: A student changes $x + 9 = 15$ into $x = 6$. Which property of equality justifies this step?
questions.solution: Subtracting 9 from both sides gives $x = 6$, and the property that allows subtracting the same number from both sides is the Subtraction Property of Equality.

questions.skill: Explain why a method works
questions.stem: Why is it allowed to subtract the same number from both sides of an equation?
choices: Both sides get smaller, so the answer is always smaller too.
The number is moved across the equal sign, so its sign must change.
Subtracting turns the equation into one that is always true.
Both sides stay equal, so the new equation has the same solution.
questions.answer: Both sides stay equal, so the new equation has the same solution.
questions.solution: Two equal quantities stay equal when the same amount is taken from each. So the new equation is true for exactly the same values of $x$ as the old one.

solve.answer: Both sides stay equal, so the new equation has the same solution.
solve.work: Equal quantities minus the same number stay equal, so the solution set is unchanged.

questions.skill: Check a solution by substitution
questions.stem: A student solves $2x - 3 = 7$ and gets $x = 5$. To check, replace $x$ with 5. What is the value of $2x - 3$ then?
questions.solution: With $x = 5$: $2(5) - 3 = 10 - 3 = 7$. This matches the right side, so $x = 5$ is a solution.

questions.skill: Justify a step with a property
questions.stem: A student changes $2(x + 3) = 14$ into $2x + 6 = 14$. Which property justifies this step?
questions.solution: The 2 is multiplied by each term in the parentheses: $2 \cdot x + 2 \cdot 3 = 2x + 6$. That is the Distributive Property.

solve.work: 2(x+3)=2x+6 is distribution of 2 over the sum.

questions.skill: Explain why a method works
questions.stem: A student solves $x^2 = 49$ and writes $x = 7$ or $x = -7$. Which statement explains why both values are written?
choices: Only 7 works, and $-7$ is written to show the opposite value.
Both 7 and $-7$ square to 49, so each one makes the equation true.
Dividing both sides by 2 undoes the square, so $x = 24.5$.
A square root of 49 is 7, and the second value is written for checking.
questions.answer: Both 7 and $-7$ square to 49, so each one makes the equation true.
questions.solution: Since $7^2 = 49$ and $(-7)^2 = 49$, both numbers satisfy the equation. Taking the square root of both sides therefore gives two solutions.

solve.answer: Both 7 and $-7$ square to 49, so each one makes the equation true.
solve.work: 7^2=49 and (-7)^2=49, so both satisfy the equation.

questions.skill: Square roots and the Zero Product Property
questions.stem: Use the Zero Product Property on $(x - 2)(x + 5) = 0$. What is the smaller solution?
questions.solution: A product is 0 only if a factor is 0, so $x - 2 = 0$ or $x + 5 = 0$. The solutions are $x = 2$ and $x = -5$, and the smaller is $-5$.

solve.work: x-2=0 gives 2; x+5=0 gives -5. Smaller is -5.

questions.skill: Name the step that was done
questions.stem: A student solves $-x = 6$ by multiplying both sides by $-1$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: Multiplying both sides by $-1$ gives $x = -6$. Check: $-(-6) = 6$.

questions.skill: Carry out the justified steps
questions.stem: To solve $2(x + 3) = 14$, a student first divides both sides by 2. What number is on the right side after that step?
questions.solution: Dividing both sides by 2 gives $x + 3 = 7$. The number on the right side is 7.

questions.skill: Find the error in a solution
questions.stem: A student solves $2x + 6 = 14$ and writes $2x = 20$ as the first step. What mistake was made?
choices: The student subtracted 6 from the left side only.
The student divided the left side by 2 but not the right.
The student multiplied the right side by 6.
The student added 6 instead of subtracting 6.
questions.answer: The student added 6 instead of subtracting 6.
questions.solution: To remove $+6$ from the left, 6 must be subtracted from both sides, giving $2x = 8$. The student added 6 to 14 instead, getting 20.

solve.answer: The student added 6 instead of subtracting 6.
solve.work: 2x+6=14 should become 2x=8; 2x=20 means 6 was added to 14 instead of subtracted.

questions.skill: Justify a step with a property
questions.stem: Solving $3(x - 2) = 12$, a student writes $x - 2 = 4$. Which step is justified?
choices: Divide both sides by 3, by the Division Property of Equality.
Distribute the 3, by the Distributive Property.
Subtract 3 from both sides, by the Subtraction Property of Equality.
Add 2 to both sides, by the Addition Property of Equality.
questions.answer: Divide both sides by 3, by the Division Property of Equality.
questions.solution: Dividing both sides by 3 turns $3(x - 2)$ into $x - 2$ and 12 into 4. The reason is the Division Property of Equality.

solve.answer: Divide both sides by 3, by the Division Property of Equality.

questions.skill: Carry out the justified steps
questions.stem: A student solves $5x - 10 = 30$ by adding 10 to both sides and then dividing both sides by 5. What is $x$?
questions.solution: Add 10 to both sides: $5x = 40$. Divide both sides by 5: $x = 8$.

questions.skill: Justify a step with a property
questions.stem: A student combines like terms to change $4x + 2x = 18$ into $6x = 18$, then divides both sides by 6. What is $x$?
questions.solution: $4x + 2x = 6x$ by combining like terms. Dividing both sides of $6x = 18$ by 6 gives $x = 3$.

questions.skill: Completing the square
questions.stem: Solving $x^2 + 6x = 7$, a student writes $x^2 + 6x + 9 = 16$. What was done?
choices: Added 9 to the left side only, to make a perfect square.
Added 6 to both sides, to match the middle term.
Added 36 to both sides, which is $6^2$.
questions.solution: Half of 6 is 3, and $3^2 = 9$. Adding 9 to both sides keeps the sides equal: $7 + 9 = 16$. The left side then becomes $(x + 3)^2$.

questions.skill: Completing the square
questions.stem: To solve $x^2 + 8x = 9$ by completing the square, what number must be added to both sides?
questions.solution: Half of 8 is 4, and $4^2 = 16$. Adding 16 to both sides makes the left side $(x + 4)^2$.

questions.skill: Square roots and the Zero Product Property
questions.stem: A student factors $x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0$ as $(x - 2)(x - 3) = 0$ and concludes $x = 2$ or $x = 3$. Which fact justifies the conclusion?
choices: If a product is 0, both of its factors are 0.
If a sum is 0, at least one of its terms is 0.
If a product is 6, at least one of its factors is 6.
If a product is 0, at least one of its factors is 0.
questions.answer: If a product is 0, at least one of its factors is 0.
questions.solution: This is the Zero Product Property. Because the product equals 0, either $x - 2 = 0$ or $x - 3 = 0$.

solve.answer: If a product is 0, at least one of its factors is 0.
solve.work: Zero Product Property: if ab=0 then a=0 or b=0.

questions.skill: Name the step that was done
questions.stem: A student changes $5x - 4 = 2x + 8$ into $3x - 4 = 8$ by subtracting $2x$ from both sides. What is the coefficient of $x$ in $3x - 4 = 8$?
questions.solution: Subtracting $2x$ from both sides leaves $5x - 2x = 3x$ on the left, and the right side becomes 8. The coefficient is 3.

questions.skill: Square roots and the Zero Product Property
questions.stem: A student solves $x^2 = 36$ by taking the square root of both sides. How many different values of $x$ make the equation true?
questions.solution: Both 6 and $-6$ square to 36, so there are 2 solutions.

questions.skill: Name the step that was done
questions.stem: Which equation results from adding 6 to both sides of $3x - 6 = 12$?
questions.solution: Adding 6 to both sides means writing $+ 6$ on each side: $3x - 6 + 6 = 12 + 6$. This simplifies to $3x = 18$.

questions.skill: Find the error in a solution
questions.stem: A student solves $x^2 = 5x$ by dividing both sides by $x$ and gets $x = 5$. What is wrong with this method?
choices: Dividing both sides by $x$ is never allowed in any equation.
The answer should be $x = -5$ because $x$ is squared.
Both sides should have been multiplied by $x$ instead.
questions.solution: The equation is also true for $x = 0$, but dividing by $x$ assumes $x \ne 0$ and drops that solution. Better: $x^2 - 5x = 0$, so $x(x - 5) = 0$ and $x = 0$ or $x = 5$.

solve.work: x^2-5x=0, x(x-5)=0, x=0 or 5. Dividing by x drops x=0.

questions.skill: Find the error in a solution
questions.stem: A student solves $2(x - 3) + 4 = 14$. Step 1: $2x - 6 + 4 = 14$. Step 2: $2x - 2 = 14$. Step 3: $2x = 12$. Step 4: $x = 6$. In which numbered step does the first error occur?
questions.solution: Steps 1 and 2 are correct. In Step 3 the student should add 2 to 14, giving $2x = 16$, but wrote 12. The first error is in Step 3.

solve.work: Step1 correct (2x-6+4=14). Step2 correct (2x-2=14). Step3 should be 2x=16, not 12: first error step 3.

questions.skill: Justify a step with a property
questions.stem: To solve $\frac{x}{2} + 3 = 7$, a student writes $\frac{x}{2} = 4$ and then $x = 8$. Which reasons justify the two steps, in order?
choices: Subtract 3 from both sides, then multiply both sides by 2.
Subtract 3 from both sides, then divide both sides by 2.
Add 3 to both sides, then multiply both sides by 2.
Subtract 7 from both sides, then multiply both sides by 2.
questions.answer: Subtract 3 from both sides, then multiply both sides by 2.
questions.solution: Subtracting 3 from both sides gives $\frac{x}{2} = 4$. Multiplying both sides by 2 undoes the division and gives $x = 8$.

solve.answer: Subtract 3 from both sides, then multiply both sides by 2.

questions.skill: Completing the square
questions.stem: A student solves $x^2 - 10x + 3 = 0$ and writes: Step 1, $x^2 - 10x = -3$. Step 2, $x^2 - 10x + 25 = 22$. Step 3, $(x - 5)^2 = 22$. Which reason justifies Step 3?
choices: The left side is a perfect square trinomial: $(x - 5)^2$.
The Zero Product Property splits the left side into two factors.
Taking the square root of both sides removes the exponent 2.
Subtracting 5 from both sides turns $x^2 - 10x$ into $(x - 5)^2$.
questions.answer: The left side is a perfect square trinomial: $(x - 5)^2$.
questions.solution: $x^2 - 10x + 25$ is a perfect square trinomial because $(x - 5)^2 = x^2 - 10x + 25$. Nothing is done to the right side in this step.

solve.answer: The left side is a perfect square trinomial: $(x - 5)^2$.
solve.work: x^2-10x+25 factors as (x-5)^2; right side 22 unchanged.

questions.skill: Completing the square
questions.stem: Completing the square on $x^2 - 12x = 5$ gives $(x - 6)^2 = k$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: Add $\left(\frac{12}{2}\right)^2 = 36$ to both sides. The left side becomes $(x - 6)^2$ and the right side becomes $5 + 36 = 41$.

questions.skill: Explain why a method works
questions.stem: In deriving the quadratic formula, the first step divides both sides of $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ by $a$. Why is this allowed?
choices: In a quadratic, $a$ is always 1, so dividing by it changes nothing.
Dividing by $a$ removes the $x^2$ term and makes the equation linear.
Since $a \ne 0$ in a quadratic, dividing both sides by $a$ keeps them equal.
Any number may be used to divide, even 0, if both sides are divided.
questions.answer: Since $a \ne 0$ in a quadratic, dividing both sides by $a$ keeps them equal.
questions.solution: If $a$ were 0 there would be no $x^2$ term, and division by 0 is undefined. Since $a \ne 0$, dividing both sides by $a$ gives an equivalent equation.

solve.answer: Since $a \ne 0$ in a quadratic, dividing both sides by $a$ keeps them equal.
solve.work: a is nonzero for a quadratic, so dividing both sides by a is valid.

questions.skill: Explain why a method works
questions.stem: Two students solve $2(x - 3) = 10$. Ana divides both sides by 2 first. Ben distributes first. Which statement is true?
choices: Only Ana is correct, since distributing may never be done first.
Both are correct, since each step keeps the equation equivalent.
Only Ben is correct, since division has to come last.
Neither is correct, since the answer depends on the order of steps.
questions.answer: Both are correct, since each step keeps the equation equivalent.
questions.solution: Ana: $x - 3 = 5$, so $x = 8$. Ben: $2x - 6 = 10$, so $2x = 16$ and $x = 8$. Every step keeps the solution the same, so either order works.

solve.answer: Both are correct, since each step keeps the equation equivalent.
solve.work: Ana: x-3=5, x=8. Ben: 2x-6=10, 2x=16, x=8. Both valid.

questions.skill: Carry out the justified steps
questions.stem: A student solves $3(2x - 4) = 2(x + 6)$. Distributing gives $6x - 12 = 2x + 12$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: Subtract $2x$ from both sides: $4x - 12 = 12$. Add 12 to both sides: $4x = 24$. Divide by 4: $x = 6$.

questions.skill: Find the error in a solution
questions.stem: A student solves $x^2 + 4 = 0$ and writes $x^2 = -4$, then $x = \pm 2$. What is wrong?
choices: The student should have added 4 to both sides, not subtracted.
The student should have written $x = \pm 4$ instead.
The student should have divided both sides by 4 first.
No real number squared is $-4$, so there is no solution.
questions.answer: No real number squared is $-4$, so there is no solution.
questions.solution: The first step is right: $x^2 = -4$. But a real number squared is never negative, and $(\pm 2)^2 = 4$, not $-4$. So there is no real solution.

solve.answer: No real number squared is $-4$, so there is no solution.
solve.work: x^2=-4 has no real solution; (+-2)^2=4 not -4.

questions.skill: Square roots and the Zero Product Property
questions.stem: A student solves $(x - 1)(x - 2) = 6$ by writing $x - 1 = 6$ or $x - 2 = 6$. Why is this not justified?
choices: The Zero Product Property only applies when the factors are equal.
Equations with factors can only be solved after dividing by $x - 2$.
The Zero Product Property only applies when the product equals 0.
A factor that is subtracted cannot be set equal to a number.
questions.answer: The Zero Product Property only applies when the product equals 0.
questions.solution: A product of 6 does not force a factor to be 6, since $2 \cdot 3$ and $1 \cdot 6$ both make 6. First rewrite as $x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0$, so $(x - 4)(x + 1) = 0$.

solve.answer: The Zero Product Property only applies when the product equals 0.
solve.work: Zero Product Property needs product 0; product 6 can arise from many factor pairs.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step equation
questions.stem: Solve $3x + 5 = 20$.
questions.solution: Subtract 5 from both sides: $3x = 15$. Divide both sides by 3: $x = 5$.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step equation
questions.stem: Solve $2x - 7 = 9$.
questions.solution: Add 7 to both sides: $2x = 16$. Divide both sides by 2: $x = 8$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: Solve $5x = 2x + 12$.
questions.solution: Subtract $2x$ from both sides: $3x = 12$. Divide both sides by 3: $x = 4$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality
questions.stem: Solve $x + 6 > 10$.
questions.solution: Subtract 6 from both sides: $x > 4$. The inequality sign stays the same.

questions.skill: Solve an equation that needs the distributive property or like terms
questions.solution: Divide both sides by 2: $x + 3 = 7$. Subtract 3: $x = 4$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with fractions or decimals
questions.stem: Solve $\frac{x}{4} + 2 = 5$.
questions.solution: Subtract 2 from both sides: $\frac{x}{4} = 3$. Multiply both sides by 4: $x = 12$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: Solve $4x = x + 15$.
questions.solution: Subtract $x$ from both sides: $3x = 15$. Divide by 3: $x = 5$.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step equation
questions.stem: Solve $-3x = 18$.
questions.solution: Divide both sides by $-3$: $x = 18 \div (-3) = -6$.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step equation
questions.stem: A number is multiplied by 4, then 9 is subtracted. The result is 27. What is the number?
questions.solution: Write $4n - 9 = 27$. Add 9: $4n = 36$. Divide by 4: $n = 9$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation that needs the distributive property or like terms
questions.stem: Solve $x + 2x = 21$.
questions.solution: Combine like terms: $3x = 21$. Divide by 3: $x = 7$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: Solve $7x - 4 = 5x + 6$.
questions.solution: Subtract $5x$ from both sides: $2x - 4 = 6$. Add 4: $2x = 10$. Divide by 2: $x = 5$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation that needs the distributive property or like terms
questions.solution: Divide both sides by 3: $2x - 1 = 7$. Add 1: $2x = 8$. Divide by 2: $x = 4$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation that needs the distributive property or like terms
questions.solution: Distribute: $4x + 2x - 10 = 20$. Combine: $6x - 10 = 20$. Add 10: $6x = 30$. Divide by 6: $x = 5$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with fractions or decimals
questions.solution: Subtract 1.2 from both sides: $0.5x = 2.5$. Divide by 0.5: $x = 5$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with fractions or decimals
questions.stem: Solve $\frac{2}{3}x = 8$.
questions.solution: Multiply both sides by $\frac{3}{2}$: $x = 8 \times \frac{3}{2} = 12$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality
questions.stem: Solve $-2x + 5 \ge 11$.
questions.solution: Subtract 5: $-2x \ge 6$. Divide by $-2$ and reverse the sign: $x \le -3$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality
questions.stem: Solve $4x - 3 < 2x + 9$.
questions.solution: Subtract $2x$: $2x - 3 < 9$. Add 3: $2x < 12$. Divide by 2: $x < 6$.

questions.skill: Decide how many solutions an equation has
questions.stem: How many solutions does $3x + 4 = 3x + 9$ have?
questions.solution: Subtract $3x$ from both sides: $4 = 9$. That is never true, so there is no solution.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step equation
questions.stem: Ava has 15 dollars and saves 4 dollars each week. After how many weeks will she have 51 dollars?
questions.solution: After w weeks she has $15 + 4w$ dollars. Solve $15 + 4w = 51$: $4w = 36$, so $w = 9$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with the variable on both sides
questions.solution: Subtract $3x$: $6x - 4 = 20$. Add 4: $6x = 24$. Divide by 6: $x = 4$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation that needs the distributive property or like terms
questions.solution: Distribute: $5x - 10 - 3x - 12 = 6$. Combine: $2x - 22 = 6$. Add 22: $2x = 28$. Divide by 2: $x = 14$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with fractions or decimals
questions.stem: Solve $\frac{x + 3}{2} = \frac{x - 1}{3}$.
questions.solution: Multiply both sides by 6: $3(x + 3) = 2(x - 1)$. Distribute: $3x + 9 = 2x - 2$. Subtract $2x$: $x + 9 = -2$. Subtract 9: $x = -11$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with fractions or decimals
questions.stem: Solve $\frac{x}{3} + \frac{x}{4} = 14$.
questions.solution: Multiply both sides by 12: $4x + 3x = 168$. So $7x = 168$ and $x = 24$.

questions.skill: Decide how many solutions an equation has
questions.stem: For which value of $k$ does $3(x - 2) = 3x + k$ have infinitely many solutions?
questions.solution: Distribute: $3x - 6 = 3x + k$. The two sides are the same expression for every $x$ exactly when $k = -6$.

solve.work: 3x - 6 = 3x + k for all x iff k = -6.

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality
questions.solution: Distribute: $-3x + 6 > 12$. Subtract 6: $-3x > 6$. Divide by $-3$ and reverse the sign: $x < -2$.

questions.skill: Solve a compound inequality
questions.stem: Solve $-4 < 2x - 2 \le 8$.
questions.solution: Add 2 to all three parts: $-2 < 2x \le 10$. Divide all parts by 2: $-1 < x \le 5$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with letters as coefficients
questions.stem: Solve $ax + b = c$ for $x$, where $a \ne 0$.
questions.solution: Subtract $b$ from both sides: $ax = c - b$. Divide both sides by $a$: $x = \frac{c - b}{a}$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality
questions.stem: Taylor has 60 dollars. A game costs 12 dollars, and each extra level pack costs 7.50 dollars. What is the greatest number of level packs Taylor can buy along with the game?
questions.solution: With n packs the cost is $12 + 7.5n \le 60$. Subtract 12: $7.5n \le 48$. Divide by 7.5: $n \le 6.4$. Taylor can buy only whole packs, so the greatest is 6.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with the variable on both sides
questions.solution: Distribute: $6x - 12 = 4x + 4 + 2$. Subtract $4x$: $2x - 12 = 6$. Add 12: $2x = 18$. Divide by 2: $x = 9$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality
questions.stem: What is the greatest integer $x$ that makes $4 - 3x > -10$ true?
questions.solution: Subtract 4: $-3x > -14$. Divide by $-3$ and reverse the sign: $x < \frac{14}{3}$, about 4.67. The greatest integer less than that is 4.

questions.skill: Solve by taking square roots
questions.stem: Solve $x^2 = 49$. What is the positive solution?
questions.solution: Both $7$ and $-7$ square to 49, so the solutions are $x = 7$ and $x = -7$. The positive one is 7.

questions.skill: Solve by taking square roots
questions.stem: Which gives all the real solutions of $x^2 = 81$?
questions.solution: Taking the square root of both sides gives $x = \pm\sqrt{81} = \pm 9$. Both $9$ and $-9$ square to 81, so there are two solutions.

questions.skill: Solve by factoring: leading coefficient 1
questions.stem: Which gives all the solutions of $x^2 + 7x + 12 = 0$?
questions.solution: Find two numbers with product 12 and sum 7: they are 3 and 4. So $(x + 3)(x + 4) = 0$, which gives $x = -3$ or $x = -4$.

questions.skill: Solve by factoring: leading coefficient 1
questions.stem: Solve $x^2 - 8x + 15 = 0$. What is the smaller solution?
questions.solution: Two numbers with product 15 and sum $-8$ are $-3$ and $-5$. So $(x - 3)(x - 5) = 0$ and $x = 3$ or $x = 5$. The smaller is 3.

questions.skill: Solve by factoring: common factor, difference of squares, leading coefficient above 1
questions.stem: Solve $x^2 - 6x = 0$. What is the greater solution?
questions.solution: Factor out $x$: $x(x - 6) = 0$. So $x = 0$ or $x = 6$. The greater solution is 6.

questions.skill: Rewrite in standard form, then factor
questions.stem: Which equation is $x^2 = 2x + 8$ written with 0 on one side, ready to factor?
questions.solution: Subtract $2x$ and subtract 8 from both sides: $x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0$. Each term moved to the other side changes sign.

questions.skill: Number of real solutions
questions.stem: Which statement about the equation $x^2 = -16$ is true?
questions.solution: A real number squared is never negative, so no real number satisfies $x^2 = -16$. Note that $(-4)^2 = 16$, not $-16$.

solve.work: A real square is never negative, so no real solutions.

questions.skill: Zero product property and checking solutions
questions.stem: Solve $(x - 4)(x + 7) = 0$. What is the positive solution?
questions.solution: A product is 0 only when one factor is 0. So $x - 4 = 0$ or $x + 7 = 0$, giving $x = 4$ or $x = -7$. The positive solution is 4.

questions.skill: Zero product property and checking solutions
questions.stem: Which value is a solution of $x^2 - x - 20 = 0$?
questions.solution: Substitute each value. For $x = 5$: $25 - 5 - 20 = 0$, so it works. For $x = 4$ the result is $-8$, for $x = -5$ it is $10$, and for $x = 20$ it is $360$.

questions.skill: Quadratic equations in context
questions.stem: A square garden has an area of 64 square meters. How long is each side, in meters?
questions.solution: The side $s$ satisfies $s^2 = 64$. Then $s = 8$ or $s = -8$, but a length cannot be negative. Each side is 8 meters.

questions.skill: Solve by taking square roots
questions.solution: Take the square root of both sides: $x - 3 = 4$ or $x - 3 = -4$. Adding 3 gives $x = 7$ or $x = -1$. Check: $(7-3)^2 = 16$ and $(-1-3)^2 = 16$.

questions.skill: Solve by factoring: leading coefficient 1
questions.stem: Solve $x^2 + 2x - 24 = 0$. What is the positive solution?
questions.solution: Two numbers with product $-24$ and sum 2 are 6 and $-4$. So $(x + 6)(x - 4) = 0$, giving $x = -6$ or $x = 4$. The positive solution is 4.

questions.skill: Solve by factoring: leading coefficient 1
questions.stem: Which gives all the solutions of $x^2 - 5x - 14 = 0$?
questions.solution: Two numbers with product $-14$ and sum $-5$ are $-7$ and $2$. So $(x - 7)(x + 2) = 0$, giving $x = 7$ or $x = -2$.

questions.skill: Solve by factoring: common factor, difference of squares, leading coefficient above 1
questions.stem: Which gives all the solutions of $2x^2 + 7x + 3 = 0$?
questions.solution: Factor: $2x^2 + 7x + 3 = (2x + 1)(x + 3)$. Setting each factor to 0: $2x + 1 = 0$ gives $x = -\frac{1}{2}$, and $x + 3 = 0$ gives $x = -3$.

questions.skill: Solve by factoring: common factor, difference of squares, leading coefficient above 1
questions.stem: Use the difference of squares to solve $4x^2 - 49 = 0$. What is the positive solution?
questions.solution: Since $4x^2 - 49 = (2x - 7)(2x + 7)$, the solutions come from $2x - 7 = 0$ and $2x + 7 = 0$. They are $x = \frac{7}{2}$ and $x = -\frac{7}{2}$. The positive one is $\frac{7}{2}$, or 3.5.

questions.skill: Rewrite in standard form, then factor
questions.stem: Solve $x^2 = 3x + 10$. What is the positive solution?
questions.solution: Write it with 0 on one side: $x^2 - 3x - 10 = 0$. Factor: $(x - 5)(x + 2) = 0$. So $x = 5$ or $x = -2$. The positive solution is 5.

questions.skill: Number of real solutions
questions.stem: How many different real solutions does $x^2 - 10x + 25 = 0$ have?
questions.solution: Factor: $(x - 5)(x - 5) = 0$. Both factors give the same solution, $x = 5$, so there is exactly one different real solution.

questions.skill: Zero product property and checking solutions
questions.stem: A student solves $(x - 2)(x + 5) = 8$ by writing $x - 2 = 8$ or $x + 5 = 8$. Why is this wrong?
choices: A product can equal 8 without either factor equaling 8
Both factors should be set equal to 4, since $2 \times 4 = 8$
Only the first factor should be set equal to 8
The numbers 2 and 5 should have been added first
questions.answer: A product can equal 8 without either factor equaling 8
questions.solution: The zero product property works only because a product of 0 forces a factor to be 0. A product of 8 can come from many pairs of factors, such as $2 \times 4$ or $1 \times 8$. The right method is to multiply out, move 8 to the left side, and then factor.

solve.answer: A product can equal 8 without either factor equaling 8
solve.work: Zero product property needs product 0; a product of 8 does not force a factor to be 8 (actual: x^2+3x-18=0, x=3 or -6).

questions.skill: Zero product property and checking solutions
questions.stem: A student solves $x^2 = 5x$ by dividing both sides by $x$ and gets $x = 5$. Which solution did the student lose?
questions.solution: Dividing by $x$ is not allowed when $x = 0$. Instead write $x^2 - 5x = 0$, so $x(x - 5) = 0$ and $x = 0$ or $x = 5$. The lost solution is $x = 0$.

solve.work: x^2-5x=0, x(x-5)=0, x=0 or 5; dividing by x lost x=0.

questions.skill: Quadratic equations in context
questions.stem: A rectangle is 3 centimeters longer than it is wide. Its area is 54 square centimeters. What is its width, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Let the width be $w$. Then $w(w + 3) = 54$, so $w^2 + 3w - 54 = 0$, which factors as $(w + 9)(w - 6) = 0$. A width cannot be negative, so $w = 6$. Check: $6 \times 9 = 54$.

questions.skill: Solve by taking square roots
questions.stem: Solve $4(x + 1)^2 = 36$. What is the larger of the two solutions?
questions.solution: Divide both sides by 4: $(x + 1)^2 = 9$. Then $x + 1 = 3$ or $x + 1 = -3$, so $x = 2$ or $x = -4$. The larger is 2.

questions.skill: Solve by taking square roots
questions.solution: Divide both sides by 3: $(x - 2)^2 = 5$. Take square roots: $x - 2 = \pm\sqrt{5}$. Add 2: $x = 2 \pm \sqrt{5}$.

questions.skill: Solve by factoring: leading coefficient 1
questions.stem: The equation $x^2 - 13x + 36 = 0$ has two solutions. What is the sum of the squares of the two solutions?
questions.solution: Factor: $(x - 4)(x - 9) = 0$, so the solutions are 4 and 9. The sum of their squares is $16 + 81 = 97$.

questions.skill: Solve by factoring: leading coefficient 1
questions.stem: The solutions of $x^2 + kx + 18 = 0$ are both negative whole numbers, and one of them is $-2$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: The product of the solutions is 18, so the other solution is $18 \div (-2) = -9$. Then the equation is $(x + 2)(x + 9) = x^2 + 11x + 18$, so $k = 11$.

solve.work: Product of roots 18, one is -2, other -9; sum -11 = -k, k=11.

questions.skill: Solve by factoring: common factor, difference of squares, leading coefficient above 1
questions.stem: Solve $6x^2 - x - 2 = 0$. What is the positive solution?
questions.solution: Factor: $6x^2 - x - 2 = (3x - 2)(2x + 1)$. Check: $6x^2 + 3x - 4x - 2$. The solutions are $x = \frac{2}{3}$ and $x = -\frac{1}{2}$. The positive one is $\frac{2}{3}$.

questions.skill: Solve by factoring: common factor, difference of squares, leading coefficient above 1
questions.stem: Which gives all the solutions of $3x^2 - 10x + 8 = 0$?

questions.skill: Rewrite in standard form, then factor
questions.solution: The product equals 12, not 0, so first multiply out: $x^2 + 5x + 6 = 12$. Then $x^2 + 5x - 6 = 0$, which factors as $(x + 6)(x - 1) = 0$. So $x = -6$ or $x = 1$.

questions.skill: Number of real solutions
questions.stem: For which value of $k$ does $x^2 + 3 = k$ have exactly one real solution?
questions.solution: Write it as $x^2 = k - 3$. There is exactly one solution when $k - 3 = 0$, since then $x = 0$. So $k = 3$. For $k = 6$ there are two solutions, and for $k = 0$ or $k = -3$ there are none.

solve.work: x^2=k-3; exactly one solution when k-3=0, k=3.

questions.skill: Zero product property and checking solutions
questions.stem: The solutions of $x^2 + bx + c = 0$ are 3 and $-8$. What is $b + c$?
questions.solution: The equation is $(x - 3)(x + 8) = 0$, which multiplies out to $x^2 + 5x - 24 = 0$. So $b = 5$ and $c = -24$, and $b + c = -19$.

questions.skill: Quadratic equations in context
questions.stem: A ball is thrown from a platform. Its height in feet after $t$ seconds is $h = -16t^2 + 48t + 64$. It lands when $h = 0$. After how many seconds does it land?
questions.solution: Set $-16t^2 + 48t + 64 = 0$ and divide by $-16$: $t^2 - 3t - 4 = 0$. Factor: $(t - 4)(t + 1) = 0$. So $t = 4$ or $t = -1$. Time cannot be negative, so it lands after 4 seconds.

questions.skill: Add two equations
questions.stem: Add the equations $x + y = 9$ and $x - y = 3$ (left sides together, right sides together). The sum is $2x = ?$. Find the ?
questions.solution: The $y$ terms cancel: $y + (-y) = 0$. The left sides give $x + x = 2x$ and the right sides give $9 + 3 = 12$. The sum is $2x = 12$.

questions.skill: A solution still fits the new equation
questions.stem: A pair of numbers makes both equations of a system true. What is true of that same pair in the sum of the two equations?
choices: It makes the sum equation false
It makes the sum true only when x = y
It cannot be tested in the sum equation
It also makes the sum equation true
questions.answer: It also makes the sum equation true
questions.solution: If the pair makes each equation true, then each side of one equals the matching side of the other. Adding equal amounts to equal amounts keeps the sides equal, so the sum is true too.

solve.answer: It also makes the sum equation true
solve.work: If both equations are true for the pair, adding equal quantities to equal quantities keeps the sum true.

questions.skill: A solution still fits the new equation
questions.stem: The solution of a system is $x = 4$, $y = 1$. Adding its two equations gives $4x + y = 17$. What does $4x + y$ equal when $x = 4$ and $y = 1$?
questions.solution: Put in the solution: $4 \times 4 + 1 = 17$. It matches the right side of the sum equation.

questions.skill: Add two equations
questions.stem: Which equation is the sum of $2x + y = 5$ and $x - y = 1$?
questions.solution: Add the left sides: $2x + x = 3x$ and $y + (-y) = 0$. Add the right sides: $5 + 1 = 6$. The sum is $3x = 6$.

questions.skill: Multiply an equation by a number
questions.stem: Multiply both sides of $x + 2y = 5$ by 3. The new equation is $3x + ?y = 15$. Find the ?
questions.solution: Every term is multiplied by 3, so $2y$ becomes $6y$. The new equation is $3x + 6y = 15$.

questions.skill: A solution still fits the new equation
questions.stem: The solution of a system is $x = 2$, $y = 3$. The equations are $x + y = 5$ and $x - y = -1$. Which equation does $x = 2$, $y = 3$ also satisfy?
questions.solution: Adding the equations gives $2x = 4$, and $2 \times 2 = 4$ is true. In the other equations, $2x$ is 4 (not 6), $2y$ is 6 (not 4), and $x + 2y$ is 8 (not 7).

solve.work: Sum of the equations: 2x=4; check 2(2)=4 true. 2x=6, 2y=4 false; x+2y=8 not 7.

questions.skill: Adding equals to equals
questions.stem: Zoe adds the true equations $5 = 5$ and $3 = 3$ (left sides together, right sides together). Is the result true?
questions.solution: The left sides add to $5 + 3 = 8$ and the right sides add to $5 + 3 = 8$. Adding equal amounts to equal amounts gives $8 = 8$, which is true.

questions.skill: Multiply an equation by a number
questions.stem: Which change to an equation does NOT change its solutions?
choices: Multiplying only the left side by 4
Adding 4 to only the right side
questions.solution: Doing the same thing to both sides keeps the sides equal, and multiplying by 4 can be undone by dividing by 4. Changing only one side, or multiplying by 0, changes the solutions.

solve.work: Multiplying both sides by a nonzero number is reversible, so the solutions stay. By 0 or one side only changes them.
