Positive: as age goes up, price tends to go down
questions.answer: Negative: as age goes up, price tends to go down
questions.solution: Points that go down from left to right show a negative association: a larger age goes with a lower price.

solve.answer: Negative: as age goes up, price tends to go down
solve.work: Down from left to right: negative association, price falls as age rises.

questions.skill: Compute and interpret residuals
questions.stem: For one data point, the actual value of $y$ is 40 and the value predicted by a fitted line is 35. Which expression gives the residual?
questions.solution: A residual is the actual value minus the predicted value, so it is $40 - 35 = 5$.

questions.skill: Compute and interpret residuals
questions.stem: A data point lies above the fitted line on a scatter plot. What is true about its residual?
choices: It is negative, because the point is farther up than the line
It is zero, because the point is close to the fitted line
It is negative, because the actual value is less than predicted
It is positive, because the actual value exceeds the prediction
questions.answer: It is positive, because the actual value exceeds the prediction
questions.solution: Residual = actual - predicted. A point above the line has an actual $y$ greater than the line's prediction, so the residual is positive.

solve.answer: It is positive, because the actual value exceeds the prediction
solve.work: Above the line: actual > predicted, so residual positive.

questions.skill: Interpret slope and intercept in context
questions.stem: A fitted line $\hat{y} = 2.5x + 40$ predicts the cost $\hat{y}$ in dollars of renting a bike for $x$ hours. What does the 2.5 mean?
choices: The rental costs 2.5 dollars when $x$ is 40 hours
Every rental lasts about 2.5 hours, on average
Each extra hour adds about 2.5 dollars to the cost
The predicted cost is always 2.5 times as much as 40
questions.answer: Each extra hour adds about 2.5 dollars to the cost
questions.solution: The slope is the change in predicted $y$ for each one-unit increase in $x$: 2.5 dollars more for each additional hour.

solve.answer: Each extra hour adds about 2.5 dollars to the cost
solve.work: Slope 2.5: each additional hour adds about $2.50 to the predicted cost.

questions.skill: Judge a linear fit with residuals
questions.stem: The least squares line for a set of points is the line that
choices: passes through every one of the points in the data
has the smallest possible sum of squared residuals
has the same number of points on each side of it
is drawn through the first and the last points
questions.answer: has the smallest possible sum of squared residuals
questions.solution: The least squares line is the line with the smallest possible sum of squared residuals. It usually does not pass through every point.

solve.answer: has the smallest possible sum of squared residuals
solve.work: Least squares minimizes the sum of squared residuals.

questions.skill: Predict with a fitted line
questions.stem: A fitted line $\hat{y} = 3x + 12$ predicts the points $\hat{y}$ a student earns on a quiz after $x$ hours of practice. How many points does the line predict for 6 hours of practice?

questions.skill: Compute and interpret residuals
questions.stem: A student actually scored 52 points on a quiz. The fitted line predicted 47 points. What is the residual?
questions.solution: Residual = actual - predicted $= 52 - 47 = 5$.

questions.skill: Exponential model: predict and interpret
questions.stem: The number of bacteria in a dish is modeled by $y = 100 \cdot 2^t$, where $t$ is the number of hours. How many bacteria does the model predict after 3 hours?

questions.skill: Interpret slope and intercept in context
questions.stem: The line $\hat{y} = 4.5x + 20$ models the distance $\hat{y}$ in miles a hiker has walked after $x$ hours. By how many miles does the line say the distance changes when $x$ increases by 3 hours?
questions.solution: The slope 4.5 is the change in predicted distance for 1 hour, so for 3 hours it is $4.5 \times 3 = 13.5$ miles.

questions.skill: Choose a model type from data
questions.stem: A table gives $x$: 0, 1, 2, 3 and $y$: 2, 6, 18, 54. Which type of model fits these data, and why?
choices: Exponential, because each $y$ is 3 times the one before it
Linear, because each $y$ is larger than the one before it
Linear, because each $y$ is 4 more than the one before it
Exponential, because each $y$ is 2 more than the one before it
questions.answer: Exponential, because each $y$ is 3 times the one before it
questions.solution: The $y$-values are multiplied by 3 each time $x$ goes up by 1, which is exponential growth. They do not increase by a constant amount.

solve.answer: Exponential, because each $y$ is 3 times the one before it

questions.skill: Judge a linear fit with residuals
questions.stem: A student fits a line to some data and plots the residuals against $x$. The residuals are scattered above and below zero with no pattern. What does this suggest?
choices: A linear model is a poor fit and a curve is needed
The data points must all lie on one line
The fitted line has a slope of zero
A linear model is a reasonable fit for the data
questions.answer: A linear model is a reasonable fit for the data
questions.solution: Residuals with no pattern mean the line captures the trend. A curved pattern would suggest the line is not appropriate.

solve.answer: A linear model is a reasonable fit for the data
solve.work: Random scatter of residuals around 0 indicates a linear model is appropriate.

questions.skill: Interpret slope and intercept in context
questions.stem: A fitted line $\hat{y} = 8 + 1.5x$ predicts the total cost $\hat{y}$ in dollars of an online music account that has $x$ songs downloaded. What does the 8 mean?
choices: Each song that is downloaded costs a flat 8 dollars
The account can hold at most 8 songs at any time
The predicted cost with no songs downloaded is 8 dollars
The predicted cost with 8 songs downloaded is 1.5 dollars
questions.answer: The predicted cost with no songs downloaded is 8 dollars
questions.solution: The intercept is the predicted value of $y$ when $x = 0$: with no songs, the predicted cost is 8 dollars.

solve.answer: The predicted cost with no songs downloaded is 8 dollars
solve.work: Intercept 8: predicted cost when x = 0 songs.

questions.skill: Exponential model: predict and interpret
questions.stem: The value of a savings account is modeled by $y = 300(1.06)^t$, where $t$ is the number of years. What does the 1.06 tell us?
choices: The predicted value grows by 1.06 dollars each year
The predicted value grows by 6% each year
The predicted value grows by 106% each year
questions.answer: The predicted value grows by 6% each year
questions.solution: Multiplying by 1.06 each year increases the value by 6% each year. The starting value is 300.

solve.answer: The predicted value grows by 6% each year

questions.skill: Predict with a fitted line
questions.stem: A line was fitted to data on children aged 5 to 12 to predict height from age. A student uses it to predict the height of a 40-year-old. Which statement is best?
choices: It is unreliable, because 40 is far outside the data
It is reliable, because a line keeps going forever
It is reliable, because a residual is always zero
It is exact, because a computer was used to fit the line
questions.answer: It is unreliable, because 40 is far outside the data
questions.solution: Predicting far outside the range of the data is extrapolation. The pattern may not continue, so the prediction cannot be trusted.

solve.answer: It is unreliable, because 40 is far outside the data
solve.work: Extrapolating far beyond ages 5-12 is unreliable.

questions.skill: Compute and interpret residuals
questions.stem: A fitted line $\hat{y} = 1.8x + 32$ predicts the height in centimeters of a young sunflower $x$ days after it was measured first. On day 25, the actual height was 70 centimeters. What is the residual?
questions.solution: Predicted: $1.8(25) + 32 = 45 + 32 = 77$. Residual = actual - predicted $= 70 - 77 = -7$.

questions.skill: Predict with a fitted line
questions.stem: The line $\hat{y} = 2.5x + 10$ predicts the price in dollars of a custom T-shirt order that has $x$ colors of ink. For what number of colors does the line predict a price of 60 dollars?
questions.solution: Solve $2.5x + 10 = 60$. Subtract 10: $2.5x = 50$. Divide by 2.5: $x = 20$.

questions.skill: Compute and interpret residuals
questions.stem: For one point, the fitted line predicts $\hat{y} = 48$, and the residual is $-3$. What is the actual value of $y$?
questions.solution: Residual = actual - predicted, so actual = predicted + residual $= 48 + (-3) = 45$.

questions.skill: Predict with a fitted line
questions.stem: The points (2, 5), (4, 9) and (6, 13) lie exactly on a line. Use that line to predict $y$ when $x = 10$.
questions.solution: The slope is $\frac{9-5}{4-2} = 2$. From (2, 5), moving 8 units right adds $2 \times 8 = 16$, so $y = 5 + 16 = 21$.

questions.skill: Judge a linear fit with residuals
questions.stem: A residual plot for a linear model shows residuals that are positive for small $x$, negative for middle $x$, and positive again for large $x$, forming a U shape. What does this suggest?
choices: The line is an excellent fit, because the residuals are small
The line has the correct slope, but its intercept is wrong
The data contain exactly one point that is wrong
A line is not the best model, and a curve would fit better
questions.answer: A line is not the best model, and a curve would fit better
questions.solution: A curved pattern in the residuals means the data bend away from a straight line, so a linear model is not appropriate.

solve.answer: A line is not the best model, and a curve would fit better
solve.work: A curved (U-shaped) residual pattern means a line is not appropriate; a curve fits better.

questions.skill: Judge a linear fit with residuals
questions.stem: Two linear models are fitted to the same data. The residuals for Model A are 1, $-2$, 1 and 0. The residuals for Model B are 4, $-5$, 3 and $-2$. Both residual plots show no pattern. Which statement is best?
choices: Model B fits better, because it has larger residuals
Model B fits better, because it has more negative residuals
Model A fits better, because its residuals are smaller
The models fit equally well, because both have no pattern
questions.answer: Model A fits better, because its residuals are smaller
questions.solution: Smaller residuals mean the model's predictions are closer to the actual values, so Model A fits better.

solve.answer: Model A fits better, because its residuals are smaller
solve.work: Model A residuals are much smaller (sum of squares 6 vs 54), so A fits better.

questions.skill: Choose a model type from data
questions.stem: A table gives $x$: 0, 1, 2, 3 and $y$: 100, 80, 64, 51.2. Which model type fits these data, and why?
choices: Linear with a negative slope, because $y$ decreases each time
Exponential decay, because each $y$ is 0.8 times the last
Exponential growth, because $y$ changes by a constant factor
Linear with a negative slope, because $y$ drops by 20 each time
questions.answer: Exponential decay, because each $y$ is 0.8 times the last
questions.solution: Each $y$ is 0.8 times the previous one ($100 \times 0.8 = 80$, $80 \times 0.8 = 64$, $64 \times 0.8 = 51.2$). A factor less than 1 is exponential decay. The drops (20, 16, 12.8) are not constant.

solve.answer: Exponential decay, because each $y$ is 0.8 times the last

questions.skill: Compute and interpret residuals
questions.stem: A student says that for the line $\hat{y} = 1.5x + 20$ the point (10, 32) has a residual of 3. Which response is correct?
choices: The residual is $-3$, because 32 is less than 35
The residual is $-3$, because the point is to the right of the line
The residual is 3, because the predicted value is 35
questions.answer: The residual is $-3$, because 32 is less than 35
questions.solution: Predicted: $1.5(10) + 20 = 35$. Residual = actual - predicted $= 32 - 35 = -3$. The student subtracted in the wrong order.

solve.answer: The residual is $-3$, because 32 is less than 35

questions.skill: Judge a linear fit with residuals
questions.stem: The fitted line $\hat{y} = 2x + 1$ is compared with the data points (1, 3), (2, 7), (3, 8) and (5, 13). Find the sum of the squares of the four residuals.

questions.skill: Exponential model: predict and interpret
questions.stem: The value of a car is modeled by $V = 24000(0.85)^t$ dollars, where $t$ is the number of years since it was bought. According to the model, what is the car's value after 2 years, in dollars?

questions.skill: Exponential model: predict and interpret
questions.stem: An exponential model $y = a \cdot b^x$ fits the data exactly: when $x = 0$, $y = 5$; when $x = 1$, $y = 15$; and when $x = 2$, $y = 45$. What does the model predict for $y$ when $x = 5$?
questions.solution: The starting value is $a = 5$ and each step multiplies by $b = 3$. So $y = 5 \cdot 3^5 = 5 \times 243 = 1215$.

questions.skill: Interpret slope and intercept in context
questions.stem: The line $\hat{y} = 150 - 12t$ models the liters of water left in a tank $t$ minutes after it starts to drain. According to the line, after how many minutes is the tank empty?
questions.solution: The tank is empty when $\hat{y} = 0$: $150 - 12t = 0$, so $t = \frac{150}{12} = 12.5$ minutes.

questions.skill: Compute and interpret residuals
questions.stem: The fitted line $\hat{y} = 3.2x + 14$ is compared with two data points: (5, 27) and (10, 50). What is the sum of the two residuals?
questions.solution: At $x = 5$ the prediction is 30, so the residual is $27 - 30 = -3$. At $x = 10$ the prediction is 46, so the residual is $50 - 46 = 4$. The sum is $-3 + 4 = 1$.

questions.skill: Interpret the slope of a linear model
questions.stem: The equation $y = 3x + 5$ predicts the height $y$, in centimeters, of a plant $x$ weeks after it was planted. What does the 3 tell us?
choices: The plant is predicted to be 3 cm tall when planted
The plant is predicted to grow 5 cm each week
The plant is predicted to grow 3 cm each week
The plant is predicted to stop growing after 3 weeks
questions.answer: The plant is predicted to grow 3 cm each week
questions.solution: The slope is the change in $y$ for each increase of 1 in $x$. Here the height goes up by 3 centimeters for each extra week. The 5 is the height at $x = 0$.

solve.answer: The plant is predicted to grow 3 cm each week

questions.skill: Interpret the slope of a linear model
questions.stem: The model $C = 4t + 20$ predicts the cost $C$, in dollars, of renting a bike for $t$ hours. By how many dollars does the predicted cost go up for each extra hour?
questions.solution: The slope, 4, is the change in cost for each extra hour. The predicted cost goes up 4 dollars per hour.

questions.skill: Interpret the intercept of a linear model
questions.stem: A gym charges a starting fee plus a monthly price. The model $C = 15m + 40$ predicts the total cost $C$, in dollars, for $m$ months of membership. What does the 40 tell us?
choices: The monthly price, 40 dollars, which is paid each month
The starting fee, 40 dollars, paid before any months
The number of months, 40, that were paid for in total
The total cost, 40 dollars, after 15 months
questions.answer: The starting fee, 40 dollars, paid before any months
questions.solution: The intercept is the value of $C$ when $m = 0$. At 0 months the cost is $15(0) + 40 = 40$ dollars, which is the starting fee.

solve.answer: The starting fee, 40 dollars, paid before any months

questions.skill: Interpret the intercept of a linear model
questions.stem: The model $S = 5t + 18$ predicts the balance $S$, in dollars, of a savings account $t$ weeks after it is opened. What balance does the model predict at the moment the account is opened?
questions.solution: The moment of opening is $t = 0$. Then $S = 5(0) + 18 = 18$ dollars. This is the intercept.

questions.skill: Interpolate with a linear model
questions.stem: The model $N = 3d + 10$ predicts the number $N$ of members a club has on day $d$. It was built from data for days 5 through 20. How many members does it predict on day 8?
questions.solution: Day 8 is inside the range 5 to 20, so this is an interpolation. $N = 3(8) + 10 = 34$.

questions.skill: Interpolate with a linear model
questions.stem: A model was built from data on children aged 10 to 18. Which prediction is an interpolation?
questions.solution: Interpolation means predicting for an input inside the range of the data. Only age 14 is between 10 and 18.

questions.skill: Extrapolate with a linear model
questions.stem: A model was built from data with $x$ from 1 to 10. Using it to predict $y$ at $x = 30$ is an example of what?
questions.solution: Predicting for an input outside the range of the data is extrapolation. Predicting inside the range is interpolation.

questions.skill: Extrapolate with a linear model
questions.stem: The model $y = 3x + 2$ predicts the height $y$, in centimeters, of a seedling in week $x$. It was built from data for weeks 1 to 5. What height does it predict for week 8?
questions.solution: Week 8 is outside the data (weeks 1 to 5), so this is an extrapolation. $y = 3(8) + 2 = 26$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Judge whether a prediction is valid
questions.stem: Which question helps you decide whether a prediction from a linear model is valid?
choices: Is the slope of the model a whole number of units?
Is the $x$-value near the $x$-values in the data?
Is the $y$-intercept of the model a positive number?
Is the $x$-value we want a whole number?
questions.answer: Is the $x$-value near the $x$-values in the data?
questions.solution: A prediction is most trustworthy when the input is within, or close to, the range of the data that built the model. Whether the slope or the numbers are whole does not matter.

solve.answer: Is the $x$-value near the $x$-values in the data?
solve.work: Validity depends on x being near the data range.

questions.skill: Judge whether a prediction is valid
questions.stem: A model for the value of a car predicts that, in year 25, the car will be worth negative 2000 dollars. What is wrong with this prediction?
choices: A car must be worth the same amount in every year
A car cannot be worth a negative amount of money
A model should never be used to predict a car's value
The year 25 is too small a number to use
questions.answer: A car cannot be worth a negative amount of money
questions.solution: A value of money cannot be negative, so the model should not be used for that year. It fits the data only over the years where the line gives sensible values.

solve.answer: A car cannot be worth a negative amount of money
solve.work: Negative value impossible for a car.

questions.skill: Interpret the slope of a linear model
questions.stem: A tank is being drained. The model $V = -12t + 600$ predicts the volume $V$, in liters, left in the tank $t$ minutes after draining starts. What does the $-12$ tell us?
choices: The volume is predicted to drop by 12 liters each minute
The tank is predicted to hold 12 liters at the start
The volume is predicted to rise by 12 liters each minute
The tank is predicted to be empty after 12 minutes
questions.answer: The volume is predicted to drop by 12 liters each minute
questions.solution: The slope $-12$ is the change in volume for each extra minute. It is negative, so the volume goes down, by 12 liters each minute.

solve.answer: The volume is predicted to drop by 12 liters each minute
solve.work: Slope -12: volume drops 12 L per minute.

questions.skill: Interpret the slope of a linear model
questions.stem: A line of best fit predicts a student's exam score $y$ from the hours studied $x$: $y = 6.5x + 48$. By how many points does the model predict the score to go up if a student studies 3 more hours?
questions.solution: Each extra hour raises the predicted score by the slope, 6.5 points. For 3 more hours the increase is $6.5 \times 3 = 19.5$ points.

questions.skill: Interpret the intercept of a linear model
questions.stem: A model predicts a person's weight $w$, in kilograms, from height $h$, in centimeters: $w = 0.9h - 85$. Which statement about the intercept, $-85$, is correct?
choices: It means every person weighs 85 kilograms less than their height
It has no practical meaning, because a height of 0 cm is not possible
It means weight rises by 85 kilograms for each extra centimeter of height
It means a person 85 cm tall is predicted to weigh 0 kilograms
questions.answer: It has no practical meaning, because a height of 0 cm is not possible
questions.solution: The intercept is the prediction at $h = 0$. Nobody has a height of 0 cm, and a weight of $-85$ kilograms is impossible, so here the intercept has no real meaning. It only helps position the line.

solve.answer: It has no practical meaning, because a height of 0 cm is not possible
solve.work: Height 0 cm impossible, so intercept has no practical meaning. (B false: 0.9*85-85 = -8.5.)

questions.skill: Interpret the intercept of a linear model
questions.stem: A line of best fit predicts that a kitten weighs 17 ounces at 4 weeks old and that its weight goes up by 3 ounces each week. What weight, in ounces, does the model predict at birth (0 weeks)?
questions.solution: Going back from week 4 to week 0 is 4 weeks, so subtract $3 \times 4 = 12$ ounces: $17 - 12 = 5$ ounces. This is the intercept.

questions.skill: Interpolate with a linear model
questions.stem: The model $S = 1.5a + 4$ predicts sales $S$, in thousands of dollars, from advertising spending $a$, in thousands of dollars. It was built from data with $a$ from 2 to 10. How many thousands of dollars in sales does it predict for $a = 6.4$?
questions.solution: $a = 6.4$ is between 2 and 10, so this is an interpolation. $S = 1.5(6.4) + 4 = 9.6 + 4 = 13.6$.

questions.skill: Interpolate with a linear model
questions.stem: The model $y = 5x - 2$ was built from data with $x$ from 4 to 20. Which prediction uses interpolation and is calculated correctly?
questions.solution: Only $x = 10$ is inside the range 4 to 20. Then $y = 5(10) - 2 = 48$. The value 52 comes from adding 2 instead of subtracting it, and $x = 2$ and $x = 25$ are outside the range, so they are extrapolations.

solve.work: x=10 inside [4,20]; 5*10-2 = 48. D miscalculated; B and C are extrapolations.

questions.skill: Extrapolate with a linear model
questions.stem: A model based on data from 2010 to 2020 is $P = 3.2t + 150$, where $P$ is a town's population in hundreds and $t$ is the number of years since 2010. What population, in hundreds, does the model predict for the year 2030?
questions.solution: 2030 is $t = 20$ years after 2010, outside the data, so this is an extrapolation. $P = 3.2(20) + 150 = 64 + 150 = 214$.

questions.skill: Extrapolate with a linear model
questions.stem: The model $h = 6.2a + 80$ predicts a child's height $h$, in centimeters, at age $a$, and was built from data on children aged 2 to 10. A student predicts that a 30-year-old is $6.2(30) + 80 = 266$ centimeters tall. Why is this prediction unreasonable?
choices: Age 30 is far outside the data, where growth is no longer steady
The slope is positive, so the model cannot be used to predict heights
The intercept is greater than zero, so the model must be wrong
The model can only be used with whole-number ages
questions.answer: Age 30 is far outside the data, where growth is no longer steady
questions.solution: Age 30 is far beyond the ages 2 to 10 in the data. Children grow at a roughly steady rate, but adults stop growing, so the line does not continue to fit.

solve.answer: Age 30 is far outside the data, where growth is no longer steady
solve.work: Age 30 far outside 2-10 where growth stops: extrapolation unreasonable.

questions.skill: Judge whether a prediction is valid
questions.stem: The model $F = -12w + 300$ predicts the number $F$ of fish in a pond $w$ weeks after a disease starts. For $w = 30$ it gives $F = -60$. What does this show?
choices: The pond is predicted to have 60 fish left at week 30
The model is valid, because the slope of the line is negative
The disease is predicted to stop spreading after week 30
The model fails at week 30, since fish cannot be negative
questions.answer: The model fails at week 30, since fish cannot be negative
questions.solution: A number of fish cannot be negative, so the prediction $-60$ is impossible. The line only describes the pond for weeks up to the point where $F$ reaches 0.

solve.answer: The model fails at week 30, since fish cannot be negative
solve.work: Fish count cannot be negative; model fails at week 30.

questions.skill: Judge whether a prediction is valid
questions.stem: The model $P = 100 - 12.5t$ predicts the percent charge $P$ left in a phone battery after $t$ hours. A percent charge cannot be negative. What is the greatest whole number of hours $t$ for which the model gives a charge that is not negative?
questions.solution: We need $100 - 12.5t \ge 0$, so $t \le 100 \div 12.5 = 8$. At $t = 8$ the charge is 0 percent, and after that the model would give negative values. The greatest whole number is 8.

solve.work: 100 - 12.5t >= 0 -> t <= 8; t = 8 gives 0 (not negative). Greatest whole number 8.

questions.skill: Interpret the slope of a linear model
questions.stem: The model $P = -1.8a + 22$ predicts the price $P$, in thousands of dollars, of a used car that is $a$ years old. Which statement correctly interprets the slope?
choices: Each extra year of age lowers the predicted price by 1.8 dollars
Each extra year of age raises the predicted price by 1.8 thousand dollars
A car that is new is predicted to cost 1.8 thousand dollars
Each extra year of age lowers the predicted price by 1.8 thousand dollars
questions.answer: Each extra year of age lowers the predicted price by 1.8 thousand dollars
questions.solution: The slope is $-1.8$, and $P$ is in thousands of dollars, so each extra year changes the predicted price by $-1.8$ thousand dollars. The price falls by 1.8 thousand dollars (1,800 dollars) per year.

solve.answer: Each extra year of age lowers the predicted price by 1.8 thousand dollars
solve.work: Slope -1.8 thousand dollars per year: lowers by 1.8 thousand each year.

questions.skill: Interpret the slope of a linear model
questions.stem: A line of best fit passes through the points $(2, 31)$ and $(6, 59)$, where $x$ is the hours of tutoring and $y$ is the total cost in dollars. What is the slope of the model, in dollars per hour?
questions.solution: Slope $= \frac{59 - 31}{6 - 2} = \frac{28}{4} = 7$. The model predicts a cost of 7 dollars for each extra hour.

questions.skill: Interpret the intercept of a linear model
questions.stem: Two printing services have models for the cost $C$, in dollars, of printing $p$ pages. Service A: $C = 0.10p + 30$. Service B: $C = 0.25p + 5$. Which statement is correct?
choices: A has the lower starting cost and the lower cost per page
B has the higher starting cost but the lower cost per page
B has the higher starting cost and the higher cost per page
A has the higher starting cost but the lower cost per page
questions.answer: A has the higher starting cost but the lower cost per page
questions.solution: The intercepts are the starting costs: A is 30 dollars and B is 5 dollars, so A starts higher. The slopes are the costs per page: A is 0.10 and B is 0.25, so A is lower per page.

solve.answer: A has the higher starting cost but the lower cost per page
solve.work: A: start 30 > 5, per page 0.10 < 0.25. So A higher start, lower per page.

questions.skill: Interpret the intercept of a linear model
questions.stem: A line of best fit passes through the points $(10, 47)$ and $(20, 87)$. What value of $y$ does the model predict at $x = 0$?
questions.solution: The slope is $\frac{87 - 47}{20 - 10} = 4$. Going from $x = 10$ back to $x = 0$ lowers $y$ by $4 \times 10 = 40$, so $y = 47 - 40 = 7$. This is the $y$-intercept.

questions.skill: Interpolate with a linear model
questions.stem: Ana drives at a steady 50 miles per hour. The model $g = -0.04m + 14$ predicts the gallons $g$ of gas left in her tank after $m$ miles, and it was built from trips of 50 to 300 miles. How many gallons does it predict are left after 3.5 hours of driving?
questions.solution: In 3.5 hours she drives $50 \times 3.5 = 175$ miles, which is inside 50 to 300. Then $g = -0.04(175) + 14 = -7 + 14 = 7$ gallons.

questions.skill: Interpolate with a linear model
questions.stem: A linear model for the temperature, in degrees Fahrenheit, $h$ hours after 6 a.m. was built from readings between hour 4 and hour 10. It predicts 50 degrees at hour 4 and 80 degrees at hour 10. What temperature does it predict at hour 7?
questions.solution: The line rises $80 - 50 = 30$ degrees in 6 hours, which is 5 degrees per hour. From hour 4 to hour 7 is 3 hours, so $50 + 15 = 65$ degrees. Hour 7 is the middle of the range.

questions.skill: Extrapolate with a linear model
questions.stem: The model $V = -15t + 900$ predicts the liters $V$ left in a tank $t$ minutes after draining starts. It was built from data with $t$ from 10 to 40. According to the model, after how many minutes will the tank be empty?
questions.solution: The tank is empty when $V = 0$: $-15t + 900 = 0$, so $t = 900 \div 15 = 60$ minutes. This is outside the data (10 to 40), so it is an extrapolation.

questions.skill: Extrapolate with a linear model
questions.stem: A model is built from data with $x$ from 20 to 60. Which pair of predictions are both extrapolations?
questions.solution: An extrapolation is a prediction outside 20 to 60. Both 15 and 65 are outside. In the other pairs, at least one value (25, 55, 30 or 50) is inside the range.

solve.work: 15 < 20 and 65 > 60: both extrapolations. A and B have one each; C none.

questions.skill: Judge whether a prediction is valid
questions.stem: A plant's height rose steadily for the first 8 weeks and then leveled off at 40 centimeters. A linear model fitted to the data for weeks 1 to 8 predicts a height of 90 centimeters at week 20. Why should this prediction not be trusted?
choices: The growth leveled off, so the line does not describe week 20
The line was fitted to just 8 weeks of data, which is too few
Heights of plants can never be predicted by using any line
Week 20 is a whole number of weeks, so no line can fit it
questions.answer: The growth leveled off, so the line does not describe week 20
questions.solution: The line only describes the steady growth of weeks 1 to 8. The plant leveled off at 40 centimeters, so a prediction of 90 centimeters at week 20 is not valid.

solve.answer: The growth leveled off, so the line does not describe week 20
solve.work: Growth leveled off at 40 cm, so linear trend doesn't hold at week 20.

questions.skill: Judge whether a prediction is valid
questions.stem: The model $S = 3e + 35$ predicts the yearly salary $S$, in thousands of dollars, of a worker with $e$ years of experience, using data on workers with 0 to 15 years of experience. Sam uses it to predict that a worker with 40 years of experience earns 155 thousand dollars. What is the best evaluation of Sam's prediction?
choices: Valid, because the model gives a positive salary for 40 years
Valid, because the slope of the model is positive
Doubtful, since 40 years is far outside the data range
Doubtful, because the intercept 35 is too small for a salary
questions.answer: Doubtful, since 40 years is far outside the data range
questions.solution: The calculation is right: $3(40) + 35 = 155$. But 40 years of experience is far outside the data (0 to 15 years), and pay need not keep rising at the same rate, so the prediction is doubtful.

solve.answer: Doubtful, since 40 years is far outside the data range
solve.work: 3*40+35 = 155, but 40 years is far outside 0-15: doubtful.

questions.skill: Compute and interpret a residual
questions.stem: A line of best fit predicts $y = 2x + 5$. At $x = 4$, the observed value is $y = 16$. A residual is the observed value minus the predicted value. What is the residual?
questions.solution: Predicted: $2(4) + 5 = 13$. Residual: $16 - 13 = 3$.

questions.skill: Compute and interpret a residual
questions.stem: The residual for one point is positive, where residual means observed value minus predicted value. Where is that point?
choices: Below the line of best fit
On the line of best fit
Above the line of best fit
questions.answer: Above the line of best fit
questions.solution: A positive residual means the observed value is greater than the predicted value, so the point is above the line.

solve.answer: Above the line of best fit
solve.work: Residual = observed - predicted > 0, so observed y exceeds the line's value: the point is above the line.

questions.skill: Interpret the correlation coefficient
questions.stem: A line of best fit for a data set slopes downward (it has a negative slope). Which statement about $r$ must be true?
questions.solution: The sign of $r$ always matches the direction of the line of best fit. A downward slope means $r$ is negative. It is not the slope itself.

solve.work: r has the same sign as the slope of the least-squares line, so r is negative.

questions.skill: Correlation versus causation and properties of r
questions.stem: A town finds that on days when more ice cream is sold, more people get sunburned, with $r = 0.85$. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: Eating ice cream causes people to get more sunburns
They tend to rise together, but one need not cause the other
Sunburns cause people to buy more ice cream
The two are unrelated, since $r$ is below $1$
questions.answer: They tend to rise together, but one need not cause the other
questions.solution: A strong correlation shows the two move together. It does not show cause. Something else, such as hot sunny weather, can drive both.

solve.answer: They tend to rise together, but one need not cause the other
solve.work: Strong positive correlation, but correlation is not causation (both driven by sunny weather).

questions.skill: Compute the correlation coefficient
questions.stem: For a data set, $S_{xy} = -12$, $S_{xx} = 16$ and $S_{yy} = 25$. Use $r = \frac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} \cdot S_{yy}}}$ to find $r$.

questions.skill: Describe a relationship from a scatter plot
questions.stem: Maya plots the outdoor temperature against the number of cups of hot chocolate a stand sells each day. The points fall close to a line that slopes downward from left to right. Which description fits best?
questions.solution: Points close to a line mean a strong relationship. The line slopes down, so as temperature rises, sales fall: the relationship is negative.

solve.work: Downward slope = negative; points close to a line = strong.

questions.skill: Interpret the correlation coefficient
questions.stem: Which value of $r$ shows the strongest linear relationship?
questions.solution: Strength depends on how close $r$ is to $1$ or $-1$, not on the sign. The value $-0.92$ is closest to $-1$, so it is the strongest.

questions.skill: Judge a linear fit from a residual plot
questions.stem: A residual plot for a linear model shows points scattered at random above and below the horizontal axis, with no pattern. What does this suggest?
choices: A linear model is a poor fit for the data
The data set contains no outliers
A linear model is a good fit for the data
questions.answer: A linear model is a good fit for the data
questions.solution: Residuals scattered at random with no pattern mean a line captures the trend in the data, so a linear model is a good fit.

solve.answer: A linear model is a good fit for the data
solve.work: Random residual scatter with no pattern indicates a linear model fits well.

questions.skill: Describe a relationship from a scatter plot
questions.stem: Four data sets have correlation coefficients $0.64$, $-0.38$, $0.05$ and $-0.91$. How many of the data sets show a negative linear relationship?
questions.solution: A negative $r$ means a negative relationship. Two of the values, $-0.38$ and $-0.91$, are negative. The answer is 2.

questions.skill: Compute the correlation coefficient
questions.stem: The points $(1, 3)$, $(2, 5)$, $(3, 7)$ and $(4, 9)$ all lie exactly on one line that slopes upward. What is the value of $r$?
questions.solution: Points that lie exactly on a line with a positive slope have a perfect positive correlation, so $r = 1$.

solve.work: Points exactly on an increasing line (y=2x+1): r = 1.

questions.skill: Judge a linear fit from a residual plot
questions.stem: A residual plot for a linear model shows the points forming a clear U-shaped curve. What is the best conclusion?
choices: A curved model would fit these data better than a line
The line fits well, since some residuals are above the axis and some below
The correlation coefficient must be exactly $0$
The data set must contain exactly one outlier
questions.answer: A curved model would fit these data better than a line
questions.solution: A pattern in the residual plot, such as a U shape, means the data bend in a way the line misses. A curve would fit better.

solve.answer: A curved model would fit these data better than a line
solve.work: A clear pattern (U-shape) in residuals means a linear model is not appropriate; a curved model fits better.

questions.skill: Compute and interpret a residual
questions.stem: A model predicts that a used car will sell for 9000 dollars. It actually sells for 8200 dollars. What is the residual (observed minus predicted), in dollars?
questions.solution: Residual = observed $-$ predicted $= 8200 - 9000 = -800$.

questions.skill: Compute and interpret a residual
questions.stem: The line $y = 3x - 2$ is used to model three points: $(2, 5)$, $(4, 9)$ and $(6, 18)$. What is the largest absolute value of a residual (distance of a point above or below the line) among the three points?
questions.solution: Predicted values: $4$, $10$, $16$. Residuals: $5 - 4 = 1$, $9 - 10 = -1$, $18 - 16 = 2$. The largest absolute value is $2$.

solve.work: Predicted: x=2 ->4, residual 1; x=4 ->10, residual -1; x=6 ->16, residual 2. Largest |residual| = 2.

questions.skill: Interpret the correlation coefficient
questions.stem: The correlation between hours of TV watched per week and test scores is $r = -0.7$. Which is the best interpretation?
choices: Watching TV causes test scores to fall by 70 percent
Seventy percent of students who watch TV get low scores
More TV time tends to go with lower scores, fairly strongly
Each extra hour of TV lowers a score by exactly $0.7$ points
questions.answer: More TV time tends to go with lower scores, fairly strongly
questions.solution: A negative $r$ means the variables move in opposite directions. The size $0.7$ is fairly strong. $r$ does not show cause, a percent of students, or a slope.

solve.answer: More TV time tends to go with lower scores, fairly strongly
solve.work: r = -0.7: negative, fairly strong linear association; it is not a slope, percent or cause.

questions.skill: Interpret the correlation coefficient
questions.stem: Four data sets have these correlation coefficients: Set P, $r = 0.62$; Set Q, $r = -0.81$; Set R, $r = 0.79$; Set S, $r = -0.15$. Which set has points closest to lying on a straight line?
questions.solution: The set with $r$ farthest from $0$ (closest to $1$ or $-1$) is closest to a line. $|-0.81|$ is the largest, so it is Set Q.

questions.skill: Describe a relationship from a scatter plot
questions.stem: For five points, the $x$-values are $1, 2, 3, 4, 5$ and the $y$-values are $9, 7, 8, 4, 2$. Which statement describes $r$?
questions.solution: As $x$ goes up, $y$ mostly goes down, and the points follow a line closely. Computing gives $r \approx -0.92$, which is close to $-1$.

solve.work: Means 3 and 6; Sxy=-17, Sxx=10, Syy=34; r=-17/sqrt(340)~-0.92.

questions.skill: Compute the correlation coefficient
questions.stem: A teacher records $(x, y)$ for five students: $(1, 1)$, $(2, 3)$, $(3, 2)$, $(4, 5)$ and $(5, 4)$. The mean of the $x$-values is 3, the mean of the $y$-values is 3, and the sums of squared deviations are $S_{xx} = 10$ and $S_{yy} = 10$. Use $r = \frac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} \cdot S_{yy}}}$ to find $r$.
questions.solution: Deviations of $x$: $-2, -1, 0, 1, 2$. Deviations of $y$: $-2, 0, -1, 2, 1$. Products: $4, 0, 0, 2, 2$, so $S_{xy} = 8$. Then $r = 8 / \sqrt{100} = 0.8$.

questions.skill: Compute and interpret a residual
questions.stem: A model predicts a plant's height with $y = 1.5x + 12$, where $x$ is the number of weeks and $y$ is the height in centimeters. After 10 weeks the plant is 25 centimeters tall. What is the residual (observed minus predicted), in centimeters?
questions.solution: Predicted: $1.5(10) + 12 = 27$. Residual: $25 - 27 = -2$. The plant is 2 centimeters shorter than predicted.

questions.skill: Correlation versus causation and properties of r
questions.stem: A study finds $r = 0.7$ between the number of libraries and the number of restaurants in a city. Which statement is false?
choices: Building more libraries will cause more restaurants to open
Cities with more libraries tend to have more restaurants
The relationship is positive and fairly strong
City size may explain both counts
questions.answer: Building more libraries will cause more restaurants to open
questions.solution: Correlation does not show cause. The false claim says libraries cause restaurants to open; a third factor such as city size may explain both.

solve.answer: Building more libraries will cause more restaurants to open
solve.work: Correlation does not show causation, so "Building more libraries will cause more restaurants to open" is false. The others are true/plausible statements.

questions.skill: Correlation versus causation and properties of r
questions.stem: The correlation between students' heights in inches and their weights in pounds is $r = 0.8$. Every height is then converted from inches to centimeters. What is the new correlation coefficient?
questions.solution: Changing the units of a variable, by multiplying by a positive number, does not change $r$. It stays $0.8$.

solve.work: Converting units is a positive linear change (x2.54), which does not change r: 0.8.

questions.skill: Compute the correlation coefficient
questions.stem: The data are $(1, 7)$, $(2, 9)$, $(3, 5)$, $(4, 3)$ and $(5, 1)$. Use $r = \frac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} \cdot S_{yy}}}$ to find $r$.

questions.skill: Correlation versus causation and properties of r
questions.stem: A scatter plot has points close to a line, with $r = 0.95$. One new point is added at a middle $x$-value, far above the line that the other points follow. What happens to $r$?
questions.solution: A point far from the line weakens the linear trend, so $r$ gets smaller in size and moves toward $0$. It does not become exactly $0$.

solve.work: A point at middle x far off the line weakens the linear pattern, so r drops toward 0 (it stays positive, not exactly 0).

questions.skill: Judge a linear fit from a residual plot
questions.stem: The residuals of a linear model, listed in order of increasing $x$, are $4, 1, -2, -4, -2, 1, 4$. What does this pattern suggest?
choices: The residuals are random, so a line is a good model
The residuals are equal, so the data are linear
The correlation coefficient must be negative
The data curve, so a line is not a good model
questions.answer: The data curve, so a line is not a good model
questions.solution: The residuals fall and then rise in a smooth U shape. A pattern like this means the data are curved, so a line is not a good model.

solve.answer: The data curve, so a line is not a good model
solve.work: Residuals go positive, negative, positive in a U shape: a systematic pattern, so the data curve and a line is not a good fit.

questions.skill: Compute the correlation coefficient
questions.stem: A data set has $r = 0.5$, $S_{xx} = 16$ and $S_{yy} = 36$. Find $S_{xy}$ if $r = \frac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} \cdot S_{yy}}}$.

questions.skill: Compute and interpret a residual
questions.stem: A line of best fit is $y = 0.8x + 4$. At $x = 15$, the residual (observed minus predicted) is $-2.5$. What is the observed value of $y$ at that point?
questions.solution: Predicted: $0.8(15) + 4 = 16$. Observed = predicted + residual $= 16 + (-2.5) = 13.5$.

questions.skill: Correlation versus causation and properties of r
questions.stem: Which statement about the correlation coefficient is true?
choices: A value of $r$ near $0$ means the two variables are unrelated in every way
The value of $r$ is the slope of the line of best fit
A value of $r$ near $0$ can occur when the points follow a clear curve
A value of $r$ can be greater than $1$ for very steep data
questions.answer: A value of $r$ near $0$ can occur when the points follow a clear curve
questions.solution: $r$ measures only straight-line relationships. Points can follow a clear curve and still have $r$ near $0$. $r$ is not the slope and is always between $-1$ and $1$.

solve.answer: A value of $r$ near $0$ can occur when the points follow a clear curve
solve.work: r is not the slope, is between -1 and 1, and measures only linear association; points on a clear curve (e.g. a U shape) can give r near 0.

questions.skill: Judge a linear fit from a residual plot
questions.stem: A data set has $r = 0.97$, but its residual plot shows a clear curved pattern. Which conclusion is best?
choices: A line is the best model, because $r$ is close to $1$
A line is not the best model, even though $r$ is high
The residual plot must have been drawn wrongly
The correlation coefficient must be computed again
questions.answer: A line is not the best model, even though $r$ is high
questions.solution: A high $r$ only says the trend is strongly linear on average. A curved residual pattern shows a line misses a systematic bend, so a curve fits better.

solve.answer: A line is not the best model, even though $r$ is high
solve.work: A curved residual pattern means a linear model is not appropriate despite high r.

questions.skill: Interpret the correlation coefficient
questions.stem: Four data sets have these correlation coefficients: A, $0.7$; B, $-0.9$; C, $0.85$; D, $-0.3$. Which list orders them from the strongest to the weakest linear relationship?
questions.solution: Strength is the size of $r$ (ignore the sign): B $0.9$, C $0.85$, A $0.7$, D $0.3$. So the order is B, C, A, D.

solve.work: Strength by |r|: B 0.9, C 0.85, A 0.7, D 0.3. Order B, C, A, D.

questions.skill: Compute and interpret a residual
questions.stem: The residual is observed minus predicted. For one point the residual is $-4$. Mia says the line's prediction for that point was 4 too low. Which statement is correct?
choices: Mia is correct, since the residual is negative
Mia is wrong, since the prediction was 4 too high
Mia is wrong, since a residual cannot be negative
Mia is wrong, since the point lies on the line
questions.answer: Mia is wrong, since the prediction was 4 too high
questions.solution: Observed $-$ predicted $= -4$ means observed is 4 less than predicted. So the prediction was 4 too high, not too low.

solve.answer: Mia is wrong, since the prediction was 4 too high
solve.work: Residual = observed - predicted = -4, so predicted = observed + 4: the prediction was 4 too high. Mia is wrong.

questions.skill: Correlation versus causation and properties of r
questions.stem: For a data set, $r = -0.6$. Every $y$-value is replaced by its opposite (the new $y$ is $-y$). What is the new value of $r$?
questions.solution: Multiplying every $y$-value by $-1$ flips the direction of the relationship, so the sign of $r$ changes. The size stays the same: $r = 0.6$.

solve.work: Negating y negates every product deviation, so r becomes 0.6.

questions.skill: Tell a causal claim from a statement of association
questions.stem: Which statement only describes an association, without saying that one thing causes the other?
choices: Students who sleep more hours each night tend to have higher test scores.
Getting more hours of sleep makes students earn higher test scores.
Sleeping for longer every night causes a student's test score to go up.
Test scores rise because students are sleeping a greater number of hours.
questions.answer: Students who sleep more hours each night tend to have higher test scores.
questions.solution: Only the first statement says what tends to go along with what. The other three say that sleep makes, causes or is the reason for the higher scores.

solve.answer: Students who sleep more hours each night tend to have higher test scores.
solve.work: "Tend to have" states association only; others say because/makes/causes.

questions.skill: Explain two things rising together by a common cause
questions.stem: Ice cream sales and sunburn cases both go up in the summer months. Which is the best explanation?
choices: Eating ice cream makes people more likely to get a sunburn in summer
Hot, sunny weather leads to both more ice cream sales and more sunburns
Getting a sunburn makes people want to buy more ice cream than before
The number of sunburn cases decides how much ice cream gets sold
questions.answer: Hot, sunny weather leads to both more ice cream sales and more sunburns
questions.solution: Sunny weather is a third variable that drives both. Neither one causes the other.

solve.answer: Hot, sunny weather leads to both more ice cream sales and more sunburns
solve.work: Hot sunny weather is a lurking variable driving both.

questions.skill: Tell a causal claim from a statement of association
questions.stem: Here are four statements. (1) Taller children tend to read better. (2) Eating breakfast makes children read better. (3) Children who own bicycles tend to be older. (4) Drinking more water causes headaches to go away. How many of these statements say that one variable causes a change in the other?
questions.solution: Statements (2) and (4) say that one thing makes or causes the other. Statements (1) and (3) only describe what tends to go together. So the answer is 2.

questions.skill: State what it means for two variables to be associated
questions.stem: Two variables are associated. Which statement must be true?
choices: A change in one variable is always the cause of a change in the other
A third variable has been ruled out as an explanation for the pattern
The values of one variable tend to go along with the values of the other
Every change in one variable is matched exactly by a change in the other
questions.answer: The values of one variable tend to go along with the values of the other
questions.solution: Association only means the two variables tend to go together in some pattern. It does not say that one causes the other, and it does not rule out a third variable.

solve.answer: The values of one variable tend to go along with the values of the other
solve.work: Association means values tend to go together; nothing about cause.

questions.skill: Explain two things rising together by a common cause
questions.stem: Across a city, fires with more fire trucks at the scene tend to have more damage. A reporter says the trucks cause the damage. Which explanation is more sensible?
choices: More trucks cause more damage, because trucks are what arrive at the fire
The damage and the number of trucks are unrelated, since trucks cannot cause damage
Fires with more trucks last longer because of the trucks that are sent to them
Bigger fires cause both more damage and more trucks being sent
questions.answer: Bigger fires cause both more damage and more trucks being sent
questions.solution: The size of the fire is a third variable. A bigger fire does more damage and also needs more trucks. The trucks do not cause the damage.

solve.answer: Bigger fires cause both more damage and more trucks being sent
solve.work: Fire size is the lurking variable causing both damage and trucks.

questions.skill: Know which studies can support a cause-and-effect conclusion
questions.stem: Which study could best show that a new fertilizer causes plants to grow taller?
choices: Randomly choose which plants get the fertilizer, then compare the heights of the two groups
Ask gardeners which of their plants they fed fertilizer, then compare the heights of all the plants
Measure plants that are already tall and check whether any of them got fertilizer
Compare plants from two different gardens, one with fertilizer and one without
questions.answer: Randomly choose which plants get the fertilizer, then compare the heights of the two groups
questions.solution: Random assignment makes the two groups alike in other ways, so a difference in height can be traced to the fertilizer. The other studies leave other differences between the plants.

solve.answer: Randomly choose which plants get the fertilizer, then compare the heights of the two groups

questions.skill: Identify a lurking variable behind an association
questions.stem: Children with bigger shoe sizes tend to have larger vocabularies. Which variable most likely explains both?
choices: The color of the child's hair
The brand of the child's shoes
The favorite food of the child
questions.solution: Older children have bigger feet and know more words. Age is the lurking variable.

solve.work: Age drives both shoe size and vocabulary.

questions.skill: Judge which conclusion a study justifies
questions.stem: A newspaper reports that people who drink coffee live longer, so drinking coffee makes you live longer. What is wrong with this reasoning?
choices: Coffee drinkers cannot be compared with people who do not drink coffee
The report should have said that drinking coffee shortens a person's life
An association alone does not show that coffee is the cause
The report would only be valid if every person on earth were studied
questions.answer: An association alone does not show that coffee is the cause
questions.solution: Living longer goes along with drinking coffee, but that does not show coffee is the reason. Something else may explain both.

solve.answer: An association alone does not show that coffee is the cause
solve.work: Association alone does not establish that coffee is the cause.

questions.skill: Tell a causal claim from a statement of association
questions.stem: Here are five statements. (1) Cities with more libraries tend to have more traffic. (2) The new fertilizer made the corn grow taller. (3) Students who play sports tend to have more friends. (4) The medicine caused the fever to go down. (5) The new tires make the car stop sooner. How many of these statements say that one variable causes a change in the other?
questions.solution: Statements (2), (4) and (5) use "made", "caused" and "make": they claim a cause. Statements (1) and (3) only describe a tendency. So the answer is 3.

solve.work: (2) made, (4) caused, (5) make are causal; (1),(3) association. Count 3.

questions.skill: Explain an association with no causal link
questions.stem: For ten years, the number of movies released each year and the number of swimming pools built in a city rise and fall together. This is best described as
choices: Proof that building more pools causes more movies to be released
Proof that releasing more movies causes more pools to be built
A hidden variable that has been shown to cause both of them
A coincidence: the two rise and fall together with no causal link
questions.answer: A coincidence: the two rise and fall together with no causal link
questions.solution: Two unrelated things can happen to move together over time. That is an association, not a reason to believe either one causes the other.

solve.answer: A coincidence: the two rise and fall together with no causal link
solve.issues: Mild: two series that rise and fall together over ten years in one city could share a common cause (economy, population), so "no causal link" is asserted rather than known; D is still clearly the intended best answer.
solve.work: No plausible mechanism; not proof either way; C claims a hidden cause has been shown, which is not given. Best: coincidence.

questions.skill: Identify a lurking variable behind an association
questions.stem: A study finds that children who take vitamins are healthier than children who do not. Which is a possible lurking variable?
choices: The color and flavor of the vitamin tablets that the children take every single day
Families who give vitamins may also serve healthier meals and visit doctors more
The number of children who took part in the whole study altogether, counted at the start
The month in which the study's survey forms were printed and sent
questions.answer: Families who give vitamins may also serve healthier meals and visit doctors more
questions.solution: A lurking variable is linked to both variables. Healthy family habits are linked to taking vitamins and to being healthy. The other options are unrelated to either.

solve.answer: Families who give vitamins may also serve healthier meals and visit doctors more
solve.work: Families who give vitamins may also eat better and see doctors more: lurking variable.

questions.skill: Judge which conclusion a study justifies
questions.stem: An observational study of 5,000 adults finds that those who eat walnuts weigh less on average. Which conclusion is justified?
choices: Eating walnuts causes people to lose weight, since the sample of adults was so large
Walnuts have no effect on weight at all, because the study was not an experiment
Walnut eaters tend to weigh less, but the study cannot show walnuts are the reason
Weighing less causes people to eat walnuts, which the large sample proves
questions.answer: Walnut eaters tend to weigh less, but the study cannot show walnuts are the reason
questions.solution: An observational study can show an association. A large sample does not turn it into proof of cause, and it does not prove there is no effect either.

solve.answer: Walnut eaters tend to weigh less, but the study cannot show walnuts are the reason
solve.work: Observational: association only, cannot show walnuts cause it.

questions.skill: Judge which conclusion a study justifies
questions.stem: A survey finds that towns with more bakeries tend to have more bicycles. Here are four statements. (1) Towns with more bakeries tend to have more bicycles. (2) Opening a bakery causes a town to get more bicycles. (3) The two variables are associated. (4) The data prove that bicycles cause bakeries to open. How many of these statements does the survey support?
questions.solution: The survey supports the statements about an association: (1) and (3). It does not support either causal claim, (2) or (4). So the answer is 2.

questions.skill: Know which studies can support a cause-and-effect conclusion
questions.stem: Why does random assignment of people to two treatment groups help support a cause-and-effect conclusion?
choices: It guarantees that both of the groups will give exactly the same results
It makes the two groups large enough that their size can be ignored
It removes the need to compare the results of the two groups
It tends to spread other variables evenly over the two groups
questions.answer: It tends to spread other variables evenly over the two groups
questions.solution: With random assignment, other variables are about equally common in both groups. A difference in results is then due to the treatment.

solve.answer: It tends to spread other variables evenly over the two groups
solve.work: Random assignment tends to balance other variables between groups.

questions.skill: Judge which conclusion a study justifies
questions.stem: One hundred students are allowed to choose whether to use a study app. Those who chose it earned higher grades. Which statement is best?
choices: Students who chose the app may differ in other ways, so it is not shown to be the cause
The app caused the higher grades, because the grades of both groups were compared
The app has no effect, because the students chose it themselves instead of being assigned
The app caused the higher grades, since 100 students is large enough to prove it
questions.answer: Students who chose the app may differ in other ways, so it is not shown to be the cause
questions.solution: The students picked the app themselves, so keener students may have chosen it. The study shows an association only.

solve.answer: Students who chose the app may differ in other ways, so it is not shown to be the cause
solve.work: Self-selection: choosers may differ; not shown to be causal.

questions.skill: Explain two things rising together by a common cause
questions.stem: At beaches, those with more lifeguards also have more drownings. Which explanation is most reasonable?
choices: Lifeguards cause drownings by distracting the swimmers who are in the water
Crowded beaches have both more swimmers at risk and more lifeguards hired
Having lifeguards on duty makes swimmers take more risks in the water
Each drowning causes the beach to hire several more lifeguards at once
questions.answer: Crowded beaches have both more swimmers at risk and more lifeguards hired
questions.solution: Beach crowds are the third variable: more swimmers means more chances of a drowning and more lifeguards hired.

solve.answer: Crowded beaches have both more swimmers at risk and more lifeguards hired
solve.work: Crowded beaches: more swimmers at risk and more lifeguards.

questions.skill: Tell a causal claim from a statement of association
questions.stem: Here are six headlines. (1) Teens who sleep less tend to have lower grades. (2) Lack of sleep makes teens fail tests. (3) Children with pets are less anxious on average. (4) Owning a pet reduces a child's anxiety. (5) Reading in dim light damages eyesight. (6) Drinking milk leads to stronger bones in kids. How many headlines claim a cause-and-effect relationship?
questions.solution: Headlines (2), (4), (5) and (6) say one thing makes, reduces, damages or leads to another. Headlines (1) and (3) only describe a tendency. So the answer is 4.

solve.work: Causal: (2) makes, (4) reduces, (5) damages, (6) leads to. Association: (1),(3). Count 4.

questions.skill: Read a correlation without claiming cause
questions.stem: A survey finds a negative association between hours of TV watched and test scores. Which statement is correct?
choices: Students who watch more TV tend to score higher, and the TV is the reason for it
Watching more TV lowers a student's score, because the association is negative, not positive
Students who watch more TV tend to score lower, but this does not show TV is the cause
Students who watch less TV tend to score lower, but TV is not the cause of it
questions.answer: Students who watch more TV tend to score lower, but this does not show TV is the cause
questions.solution: Negative means one goes up as the other goes down, so more TV goes with lower scores. A survey cannot show that the TV is the cause.

solve.answer: Students who watch more TV tend to score lower, but this does not show TV is the cause
solve.work: Negative association: more TV, lower scores; not causation.

questions.skill: Know which studies can support a cause-and-effect conclusion
questions.stem: Which finding would best support the claim that a tutoring program causes grades to improve?
choices: Students who joined the program had higher grades than students who did not join it
Most of the students in the program said that they enjoyed the program a lot and wanted to join it again
Grades went up at the school in the same year that the new program started
Students were randomly assigned to the program or not, and the program group improved more
questions.answer: Students were randomly assigned to the program or not, and the program group improved more
questions.solution: Random assignment makes the groups alike, so a larger improvement in the program group points to the program as the cause.

solve.answer: Students were randomly assigned to the program or not, and the program group improved more
solve.work: Random assignment with greater improvement supports causation.

questions.skill: Recognize confounding in a comparison of treatments
questions.stem: In a hospital, patients given Treatment X had worse outcomes than patients given Treatment Y. Doctors gave X mostly to the sickest patients. What does this show?
choices: The comparison is confounded by how sick the patients were, so X is not shown to be worse
Treatment X is worse, since the patients who got it had worse outcomes than the others
Treatment Y is worse, because sicker patients are always given the weaker of the two treatments
Both treatments work equally well, because the patients differed in their illness
questions.answer: The comparison is confounded by how sick the patients were, so X is not shown to be worse
questions.solution: The sickest patients got X, so the severity of illness is mixed up with the treatment. The data cannot separate the two.

solve.answer: The comparison is confounded by how sick the patients were, so X is not shown to be worse
solve.work: Confounded by severity of illness; X not shown worse.

questions.skill: Explain two things rising together by a common cause
questions.stem: Across a year, sunscreen sales and swimming pool visits are strongly associated, and both are higher on hot days. Which statement best fits the data?
choices: Buying sunscreen causes people to visit swimming pools more often during the day
Temperature is a lurking variable that likely drives both sunscreen sales and pool visits
Visiting swimming pools makes sunscreen sell more, with temperature playing no role at all
Hot days are caused by sunscreen sales and pool visits taken together over a year
questions.answer: Temperature is a lurking variable that likely drives both sunscreen sales and pool visits
questions.solution: Heat sends people to the pool and makes them buy sunscreen. Temperature explains the association, so neither one needs to cause the other.

solve.answer: Temperature is a lurking variable that likely drives both sunscreen sales and pool visits
solve.work: Temperature is a lurking variable driving both.

questions.skill: Identify a lurking variable behind an association
questions.stem: In an observational study, coffee drinkers had more heart disease. Smokers drank more coffee. Which approach best checks whether smoking explains the association?
choices: Compare only the coffee drinkers who smoke with all of the people who do not smoke
Keep adding more coffee drinkers to the study until the association gets stronger and stronger
Compare coffee drinkers with non-drinkers separately among smokers and among non-smokers
Ask the coffee drinkers whether they believe coffee causes heart disease
questions.answer: Compare coffee drinkers with non-drinkers separately among smokers and among non-smokers
questions.solution: Comparing within smokers and within non-smokers holds smoking fixed. If the association disappears there, smoking was the lurking variable.

solve.answer: Compare coffee drinkers with non-drinkers separately among smokers and among non-smokers
solve.work: Stratify: compare coffee vs non-coffee within smokers and within non-smokers.

questions.skill: Judge which conclusion a study justifies
questions.stem: Researchers randomly assigned 60 volunteers to a new diet or to their usual diet. After 3 months, the new-diet group had lost much more weight. Which conclusion is best justified?
choices: The new diet is only associated with weight loss, because no experiment can show a cause
The new diet causes weight loss in every person in the whole country
The new diet cannot be the cause, because the volunteers chose to take part
For these volunteers, the new diet caused the greater weight loss
questions.answer: For these volunteers, the new diet caused the greater weight loss
questions.solution: Random assignment supports a cause-and-effect conclusion for the volunteers studied. It does not extend to everyone.

solve.answer: For these volunteers, the new diet caused the greater weight loss
solve.work: Randomized experiment: for these volunteers the diet caused the greater loss; not generalizable to everyone.

questions.skill: Know which studies can support a cause-and-effect conclusion
questions.stem: Seven studies are described. (1) Plants randomly chosen to get a fertilizer. (2) A survey of 1,000 adults about their diet. (3) A trial in which patients were randomly given a drug or a placebo. (4) A review of the records of past patients. (5) A comparison of children who chose to join a club. (6) Two reading programs randomly assigned to classrooms. (7) Households randomly picked to receive a new light bulb. How many of these studies could support a cause-and-effect conclusion?
questions.solution: Only the studies that use random assignment of a treatment can support a cause-and-effect conclusion: (1), (3), (6) and (7). Surveys, records and self-selected groups show association only. So the answer is 4.

questions.skill: Tell a causal claim from a statement of association
questions.stem: Which headline is most appropriate for an observational study that found people who eat more fruit have lower blood pressure?
choices: Eating more fruit lowers your blood pressure, new study proves it
Fruit eaters tend to have lower blood pressure, a new study finds
New study shows that fruit is the cure for high blood pressure
Fruit causes blood pressure to drop, researchers have concluded
questions.answer: Fruit eaters tend to have lower blood pressure, a new study finds
questions.solution: An observational study can report an association. The other headlines claim that fruit causes the drop.

solve.answer: Fruit eaters tend to have lower blood pressure, a new study finds

questions.skill: Judge which conclusion a study justifies
questions.stem: After accounting for age, income and smoking, an observational study still finds that people who garden live longer. Can the researchers conclude that gardening causes longer life?
choices: Yes, because accounting for three variables rules out every other explanation
Yes, because any association that remains after adjusting must be causal
No, because other lurking variables that were not measured could still explain it
No, because an observational study can never find any association between two variables
questions.answer: No, because other lurking variables that were not measured could still explain it
questions.solution: Adjusting for some variables helps, but unmeasured variables may remain. Only a randomized experiment supports a cause-and-effect conclusion.

solve.answer: No, because other lurking variables that were not measured could still explain it
solve.work: Unmeasured lurking variables may remain; cannot conclude causation.

questions.skill: Read a correlation without claiming cause
questions.stem: A survey finds a strong negative correlation (r = -0.95) between x and y. Student A says changes in x lead to changes in y. Student B says it only shows that x and y are associated. Who is right for data from a survey?
choices: Student A, because a correlation this strong shows that x causes y
Student A, because a negative correlation means y is caused by x
Neither one, because a negative correlation shows no association
Student B, because correlation does not by itself show cause and effect
questions.answer: Student B, because correlation does not by itself show cause and effect
questions.solution: A strong correlation, positive or negative, describes how closely the variables go together. It cannot show cause and effect.

solve.answer: Student B, because correlation does not by itself show cause and effect
solve.work: Survey correlation does not show causation; B is right.
